Looking for changes in each release?

This section summarizes the differences between CueMol2 and CueMol3. To see what changed when the CueMol3 version went up, see the release history.

docs.title: What stays the same
docs.text:
• Scene file (.qsc) compatibility: Scenes created in CueMol2 can be opened in CueMol3.
  • Visualization engine: Renderer types, selection expression syntax and supported file formats are shared.
  • License: Still the MIT License.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.10.504

docs.title: Merged, renamed and removed features
docs.text: A list of where the features of CueMol2 went in CueMol3, or whether they are gone.

docs.title: Renamed or moved features
docs.text:
These features are still available, but their names or locations have changed.

CueMol2 CueMol3 Notes Rendering > POV-Ray rendering... Rendering > Image rendering... The backend is now chosen inside the rendering window, so the menu is named after the type of output. The default is the built-in ray tracer Umbreon; POV-Ray is deprecated → Rendering Rendering > Animation rendering... Rendering > Movie rendering... Now the movie mode of the same rendering window Help > Check for updates Check for Updates... (in the application menu on macOS) A CueMol3-specific mechanism that replaces the Mozilla update system. In-app updating is currently available only on macOS (Apple Silicon) → Updating Tools > Mol bond editor... Add Bond tool in the tool palette Changed from a modal dialog to clicking directly in the molecular view → Toolbar and tool palette Edit > Options (preferences window) Settings tab Opens as a tab in the content area rather than a modal window. Preferences... on macOS Property dialog for each Renderer type Property inspector The dialogs are gone; properties are now edited live in a persistent panel → Property inspector Presets in the color menu Palette panel of the color picker Merged as grayscale plus variations for each hue Paint settings dialog Paint table in the Color panel Cells of the table are now edited directly → Side panels Object deletion dialog Delete in the scene tree The dedicated dialog for specifying what to delete by selection expression has been removed File > New Window File > New Tab See also "Removed features (with alternatives)" below

docs.text: CueMol2 feature Reason for removal Alternative File > New Window Because all windows share a single backend, multiple OS windows cannot be opened Add a tab with File > New Tab Window > Show/Hide Topbar It does not fit the CueMol3 screen layout The toolbar is always shown Window > Clear log contents Same as above The log in the Output panel is cleared when the application is restarted Window > Restore default panel location Same as above Switch the panel layout with the activity bar Window > Panels submenu Same as above. Side panels switch by group, so there is no place for showing or hiding individual panels Same as above Tools > Molecular surface generation with MSMS The route using the external MSMS binary was not in use Use Tools > Mol surface generation... (built-in SES generation) Hierarchical editor in the selection panel (Hierarchical / Terminal / Around-Expand) Writing selection expressions directly covers most uses The selection expression field in the Selection panel, or tree selection in the Molecular structure panel Key binding customization A decision not to port the UXP implementation as it was Cannot be changed at present Help > About plugins... / About config... / Addon manager... / Console Features specific to Mozilla XULRunner Developer tools can be opened from View > Toggle Developer Tools

docs.title: Removed features (without alternatives)
docs.text: CueMol2 feature Reason for removal View > Hardware stereo Decided to be out of scope for the migration File > Open web page... There is no built-in browser. External links are opened in the OS default browser Tools > Execute script... There is no plan to implement it, so it was removed rather than leaving a non-working item Tools > Performance measure Same as above MolClient (generating a molecule from SMILES) It requires an external MolServer (XMLRPC) Export to QSL (lightweight scene) format Removed from CueMol itself Export to LuxRender / LuxCore / Warabi / raw formats Not included in the CueMol3 Export scene (still available in CueMol2) Coloring by script (Script coloring) It could not be selected or created from the UI in CueMol2 either Mouse preset selection Its role overlaps with the pointing device setting → Mouse and trackpad input HiDPI switching / UI language setting CueMol3 has no corresponding processing Writing RMSD information of molecular superposition to a file The RMSD can be checked in the log of the Output panel

docs.title: Features not yet implemented
docs.text:
Separately from the above, some items are planned but do not work yet. → Development status and unimplemented features

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Development status and unimplemented features
docs.text:
This page is a snapshot as of CueMol3 2.3.15.530

CueMol3 is under active development. The limitations and problems listed here may already be resolved in your version.

The CueMol3 release assets can be downloaded from GitHub Releases, but they are work-in-progress versions. If you need stable behavior, use CueMol2 (→ Installation).

docs.title: Partially implemented features
docs.text: Feature Status Detailed settings for each Renderer type The Properties tab of the property inspector has a Common section and a dedicated section for each Renderer type. Nested properties that do not appear there (such as the cross-section shape of cartoon) can be edited in the Generic tab Code signing macOS builds are ad-hoc signed only (no Developer ID signing or notarization), and Windows builds are unsigned. Both require a manual workaround on first launch → Installation

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text: Symptom Details Selection changes in the Sequence panel are slow to take effect After changing the selection in the sequence panel, the highlight in the molecular view may take about 0.5 seconds to update The first expansion of the Molecular structure panel is slow The tree may stutter when first expanded (even when the number of residues is small) The pointing device is sometimes detected incorrectly Detection is estimated from scrolling characteristics, so a mouse and a trackpad may be confused. Specify the device explicitly in Settings Focus on a density map Renderer row jumps to the origin Selecting a density map Renderer (contour / isosurf) row in the scene tree and pressing Focus moves the view to the origin instead of the map. Focus on the map's Object row instead

docs.title: Features confirmed to work
docs.text:
All the features targeted for porting from the CueMol2 (UXP version) GUI were either ported or confirmed as deliberately not ported in 2.3.10.504 (for those not ported, see → Merged, renamed and removed features). For reference, the main implemented features are listed below.

  • Reading and writing files / scenes, network retrieval with Get PDB, recent files, drag & drop from the OS and file associations
  • Scene tree (toggle visibility / rename / reorder / multiple selection / range selection / context menu)
  • Copy & paste via the OS clipboard (exchange with CueMol2 is also possible)
  • Creating Renderers (including presets) and editing their settings in the inspector
  • Coloring (Solid / Paint / CPK / Rainbow / B-factor / electrostatic potential / Multi-gradient)
  • Selection (selection expressions, molecular structure tree, sequence panel, rectangle / lasso tools)
  • Measurement (distance / angle / dihedral) and adding or removing bonds
  • Creating, cutting and regenerating molecular surfaces (two algorithms, MeshMS / BALL), interaction analysis, secondary structure reassignment, molecular superposition
  • Changing symmetry and displaying symmetry mates and unit cells (including Create SYMM mol), adjusting density map display
  • Electrostatic potential calculation with APBS (requires configuring an external tool)
  • Timeline editing and playback of animations, creating morphing animations
  • Still image and movie output in the rendering window (the default is the built-in ray tracer Umbreon. Ink-style NPR output can also be selected)
  • Export scene (PNG / Umbreon / POV-Ray SDL / STL / MQO)

docs.title: Reporting problems
docs.text:
If you find a problem, report it as an Issue in the GitHub repository.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.15.530

docs.title: Changes in the interaction model
docs.text: The biggest change in CueMol3 is where settings are specified.

docs.title: The CueMol2 approach and its problems
docs.text:
Nearly every function in the CueMol2 GUI had the same form.

Press a menu item or button → a modal dialog opens → fill in every field → run with OK

Carrying this form over unchanged would leave the following inconveniences.

  • Settings cannot be adjusted while watching the result. The dialog covers the molecular view and blocks interaction.
  • The same settings appear in two places. The fields in the dialog used to create an Object duplicate the property fields available after it is created.
  • Fixing something later means reopening the same dialog.

docs.title: The CueMol3 policy
docs.text:
CueMol3 drops "everything is a modal dialog" and chooses the location according to the nature of the operation.

Nature of the operation Form in CueMol3 Examples Editing the settings of a persistent target Permanent property inspector Renderer / Object / scene settings A light choice with 1 to 3 options Popover (a small panel that opens in place) Choosing the label set for measurement tools, listing and deleting bonds Involves operations on the molecular view Tool mode + auxiliary panel Measuring distances, angles and dihedral angles, adding bonds A one-time process with many fields Dedicated window / panel Rendering window Options in the middle of an open or save flow Modal dialog (as before) Format options when opening a file, options when saving a scene A one-time confirmation or a destructive operation Modal dialog (as before) Confirmation when closing an unsaved scene, deleting atoms

Modal dialogs have not been abolished entirely. They are still used where interrupting the flow makes sense.

docs.title: Principle: create with default values, adjust afterwards
docs.text:
This is the central principle of CueMol3.

In CueMol2, even creating a single Renderer required deciding every field in a dialog first. CueMol3 works as follows.

  1. Only what is minimally required to create it is asked, through a light UI (the Renderer type, the target Object, and so on).
  2. Everything else is created immediately with default values.
  3. Fine adjustments are made afterward in the inspector, while watching the result.
  4. If the result is not what you wanted, Undo (Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Z) reverts the whole creation.

Since mistakes can be reverted with Undo, there is no need to decide everything before creating.

docs.title: Settings in the property inspector
docs.text:
For persistent targets (Renderers, Objects and the scene), the property inspector is the only place for settings. The same fields are not duplicated in creation dialogs.

  • Changes are applied to the molecular view immediately (there are no OK / Apply buttons).
  • To revert a change, use Undo (there is no Cancel button).
  • When another element is selected in the scene tree, the inspector switches to show it.

→ Property inspector

docs.title: Carrying over the previous settings
docs.text: For processes that are "one-time but have many fields", such as export and rendering, the settings used last are remembered and serve as the initial values the next time. The output destination and frame rate of movie output are examples.

docs.title: Summary: where to perform CueMol2 operations
docs.text:
Operation in CueMol2 Operation in CueMol3 Open the Renderer property dialog Select the Renderer in the scene tree → inspector on the right Set values in the dialog and press OK Change the values in the inspector (applied immediately) Press Cancel in the dialog Undo with Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Z Mol bond editor dialog Add Bond tool in the tool palette Options preferences window Settings tab POV-Ray rendering dialog Rendering window (still image mode) Animation rendering dialog Rendering window (movie mode)

Last checked: 2026-08-10 / Verified against: development build (tritium)

docs.title: What is CueMol3
docs.text:
CueMol3 (development codename tritium) is software for visualizing the three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules such as proteins and nucleic acids. Molecular models obtained by X-ray crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy can be displayed together with electron density maps and molecular surfaces, and used to create figures for publications.

CueMol3 is the successor to CueMol2. It uses the same visualization engine (libcuemol2) as CueMol2, so scene files (.qsc) remain compatible. On the other hand, the GUI has been completely rebuilt, replacing the Mozilla XULRunner used by CueMol2 with Electron + React.

For what has changed from CueMol2, see Changes from CueMol2.

docs.title: Supported file formats
docs.text: These are the formats that libcuemol2 can read and write, and they are the same as in CueMol2. Depending on the build configuration, some formats may not be included.

docs.title: Molecular coordinates (read)
docs.text: Format Extensions PDB .pdb / .ent / .pdb.gz mmCIF .cif / .cif.gz SYBYL Mol2 .mol2 MOL / SDF .mol / .sdf

docs.title: Electron density and potential maps (read)
docs.text: Format Extensions CCP4 density map .map / .ccp4 / .mrc / .ccp4.gz XPLOR / CNS density map .map / .cns BRIX density map .brix / .omap MTZ structure factors .mtz mmCIF map coefficients .cif / .cif.gz APBS electrostatic potential map (OpenDX) .dx

docs.title: Molecular surfaces and others (read)
docs.text: Format Extensions MSMS surface files .face / .vert PLY polygon file .ply

docs.title: MD trajectories (read)
docs.text:
In CueMol3, MD simulation trajectories can be loaded with Open MD Trajectory... in the File menu. This item is part of the MD Tools plugin, which is disabled by default. Enable it in Settings > Plugins > Installed (→ Plugins).

Format Extensions AMBER topology .prmtop / .parm7 / .top AMBER NetCDF trajectory .nc DCD binary trajectory .dcd GROMACS coordinates / XTC / TRR .gro / .xtc / .trr NAMD coordinates .coor

docs.title: Scenes (read)
docs.text:
These are loaded with Open Scene... in the File menu (they do not appear in Open File...).

Format Extensions PyMOL session .pse CueMol scene .qsc

docs.title: Export
docs.text: Format Use CueMol scene (.qsc) Saving the whole scene. Compatible with CueMol2 PNG image Snapshot of the screen (Rendering > Export scene) Umbreon ray-traced image (PNG) High-quality image from the built-in ray tracer (the default rendering method) POV-Ray SDL (.pov) Scene description for external POV-Ray (an .inc file is also written) STL (.stl) Shape data for 3D printers, etc. Metasequoia (.mqo) For 3D modeling software PDB / MOL/SDF / PQR / XYZR Saving a single molecular Object (File > Save File As...)

docs.title: System requirements
docs.text:
OS Release assets Notes macOS (Apple Silicon / arm64) .dmg Ad-hoc signature only. The first launch requires extra steps Windows (x64) .exe (NSIS installer) Unsigned, so a SmartScreen warning appears Linux (x64) .AppImage / .deb

An environment where OpenGL is available for 3D display is required.

External tools (ffmpeg / APBS/PDB2PQR / POV-Ray for the legacy backend) are used only by some features. If they are not bundled with the release assets, specify the path to the executable in Settings (→ Configuring external tools). Ray tracing is done by the built-in Umbreon, so no external program is needed.

docs.title: Quick tour
docs.text: This tour follows the shortest path from launching CueMol3 to loading a structure, adjusting its display, exporting an image, and saving the scene. For details of each screen, see User interface; for details of each menu item, see the Menu reference.

docs.title: 1. Launch CueMol3
docs.text: Launching CueMol3 opens a single window. Scenes are lined up as tabs at the top of the window.

docs.title: 2. Load a structure
docs.text:
As an example, load the small protein crambin (PDB ID: 1CRN). For a structure whose PDB ID is known, File > Get PDB... is the easiest way to fetch it.

  1. Choose File > Get PDB... (the Get PDB toolbar button does the same)

  2. Enter 1CRN in PDB Accession Code and press Download

  3. An options dialog for loading appears. Choose simple from Renderer type and press Open

The whole molecule is displayed as a thin line drawing. simple is the lightest display method, drawing bonds as lines only, and is well suited for getting an overview first.

In addition to coordinates, electron density maps (cif.gz from RCSB, MTZ from EBI) can also be fetched. A download can be interrupted with Cancel in the progress dialog. To open a local file, use File > Open File... (the same options dialog appears).

docs.title: 3. Adjust the display
docs.text: A loaded structure is drawn in the molecular view (the 3D display area in the center) through Renderers (display methods). Multiple Renderers can be stacked on one Object.

docs.title: Add a Renderer
docs.text:
To show the secondary structure, add a ribbon.

  1. In the Explorer > Scene tree (scene tree) in the left side panel, right-click the Object (1crn) and choose New Renderer

  2. Choose ribbon from Renderer type and press Create

Over the line drawing, helices and sheets are drawn as flat ribbons and everything else as thin tubes.

Next, display only the Cys residues that form disulfide bonds with ballstick (a model that draws atoms as spheres and bonds as cylinders). A Renderer can narrow its target atoms with a selection expression (→ Selection expression syntax). Here, instead of writing the expression by hand, build it with the selection builder.

  1. In the same way, right-click the Object (1crn) and choose New Renderer
  2. Choose ballstick from Renderer type
  3. Check Selection
  4. Press the ▼ at the right end of the selection expression field to open the selection builder
  5. Switch to the Term tab and choose resn (residue name) from the keywords
  6. Open the candidates with the ▼ of the value field and choose CYS

  7. Press Set. resn CYS is entered in the selection expression field

  8. Press Create

Over the ribbon, only the six Cys residues are drawn as spheres and cylinders. In crambin, they form three disulfide bonds.

The initial line drawing is no longer needed, so click the eye icon on the simple1 row of the scene tree to hide it. The eye icon toggles the visibility of each Renderer at any time.

  • When a type is chosen, a Renderer is created immediately with default values, and detailed settings are adjusted afterward in the inspector (for this policy, see Changes in the interaction model)
  • Choosing a predefined combination (preset) creates a group of multiple Renderers at once

docs.title: Adjust the appearance
docs.text: Double-click ballstick1 in the scene tree, and its settings are shown in the property inspector on the right. Open the Ball and stick section and raise Atom radius (the radius of the atom spheres, in Å) from the default 0.3 to 0.5. The spheres become larger, giving a display that emphasizes the atoms. Changes to values are reflected in the molecular view immediately, and can be undone with Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Z.

docs.title: Change the colors
docs.text:
Colors are set in the Explorer > Color panel in the left side panel. Coloring can be set for each Renderer or on the molecular Object. The default color of a Renderer refers to the color of the Object ($molcol), so recoloring the Object is reflected in all Renderers that refer to it. Here, recolor the Object.

  1. Select 1crn (object) at the top

  2. Press the adjacent Coloring button and choose Rainbow coloring

The ribbon is recolored in rainbow colors from the N-terminus to the C-terminus, and the carbon atoms of the ballstick follow. Coloring comes in several kinds, such as Paint / CPK / B-factor / electrostatic potential (→ Coloring).

docs.title: Move the viewpoint
docs.text:
Mouse operations in the molecular view are as follows (defaults).

Operation Action Left drag Rotate Wheel Zoom Two-finger scroll on a trackpad Translate (when the pointing device setting is Mac trackpad / Auto-detect)

For details and for changing the settings, see Mouse and trackpad input.

docs.title: 4. Export an image
docs.text: There are two ways, depending on the purpose.

docs.title: Export the screen as is
docs.text: Choose Rendering > Export scene > PNG image... to specify the destination, size, DPI, and background transparency and write out a PNG.

docs.title: Produce a high-quality ray-traced image
docs.text:
Choose Rendering > Image rendering... to open a separate rendering window in Still mode.

  1. Choose the target view (Target). The backend can stay at the default Umbreon

  2. Set the quality and size

  3. Press Start Render. Progress is shown, and when it finishes the resulting image appears in the same window

To make a movie, use Movie mode of the same window via Rendering > Movie rendering... (→ Rendering window).

docs.title: 5. Save the scene
docs.text:
Save the scene to a .qsc file with File > Save Scene (Cmd+S / Ctrl+S). On the first save, as with Save Scene As..., a dialog appears for specifying the destination and options (embedding / compatibility / compression / encoding).

.qsc is compatible with CueMol2, so scenes created in CueMol2 can also be opened in CueMol3.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
CueMol3 is a development build

CueMol3 release assets can be downloaded by anyone from GitHub Releases, but they are work-in-progress versions. The assets are not signed with a certificate that identifies the publisher (Developer ID / Authenticode) and are not notarized, so the OS shows a security warning on first launch and a manual step is required to get past it.

If you need a stable version for daily work or for preparing papers, use the stable release of CueMol2. See the CueMol2 documentation site for how to get it.

docs.title: Code signing status of the release assets
docs.text:
OS Signing Warning at launch macOS Ad-hoc signature only (codesign --sign -). No Developer ID signature or notarization A Gatekeeper warning is shown → how to bypass it Windows None (Authenticode signing is future work) A SmartScreen warning is shown → how to bypass it Linux None No warning

An ad-hoc signature does not pass Gatekeeper

The macOS release assets are ad-hoc signed at build time. This is required to make the app launchable on Apple Silicon (an unsigned bundle is rejected as "damaged"), and it does not identify the publisher. Therefore the Gatekeeper warning is still shown for files downloaded from the web, as before.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
CueMol3 release assets are published on the Releases page on GitHub (alongside the CueMol2 release assets in the same releases).

  • Latest release — In the Assets section at the bottom of the page, download the file whose name starts with CueMol3- (files starting with cuemol2_... are CueMol2 release assets)
  • Release list and release notes — Downloads of past versions, and detailed changes for each release (for just the highlights, see the release history)

The development build can also be obtained in the following ways.

  • Artifacts generated by the CI (build2.yml) of the GitHub repository (requires a GitHub login)
  • Building the package from source yourself

docs.title: Release assets
docs.text:
OS Release asset (example: version 2.3.15.530) Installer format macOS (Apple Silicon / arm64) CueMol3-2.3.15.530-macOS-arm64-Installer.dmg Disk image Windows (x64) CueMol3-2.3.15.530-Windows-x64-Setup.exe NSIS wizard-style installer Linux (x64) CueMol3-2.3.15.530-Linux-x64.AppImage / CueMol3-2.3.15.530-Linux-x64.deb AppImage / Debian package

The file name contains the target OS and the version, which includes a 4-digit build number. Files with Installer / Setup in the name are installers.

The x86-64 builds require an AVX2-capable CPU

The Windows / Linux x86-64 builds are compiled with AVX2 instructions. Supported CPUs are Intel Haswell / AMD Zen and later (roughly 2013 onward). On older CPUs, the app crashes when a molecular surface is generated.

macOS (Apple Silicon) and ARM builds are not affected.

docs.title: File associations
docs.text:
CueMol3 registers the file formats it can handle (16 types, including .qsc / .pdb / .cif / .mol2 / .ccp4) with the OS. CueMol3 appears in "Open With" on macOS, "Open with" in Windows Explorer, and "Open With" in Linux file managers.

The registration is as a candidate only. CueMol3 does not take over the default application, so settings such as opening .qsc with CueMol2 and .pdb with another application remain as they are.

On Linux, the .deb package registers the associations. For the AppImage, this depends on your desktop integration tool.

docs.title: External tools
docs.text:
Movie encoding (ffmpeg) and electrostatic potential calculation (APBS / PDB2PQR) use external programs. If they are bundled with the release assets, they can be used as they are; for builds that do not bundle them, the executable paths must be specified in Settings.

Ray tracing is performed by the built-in Umbreon, so no external program is needed.

→ Configuring external tools

docs.title: Uninstallation
docs.text: OS Procedure macOS Delete /Applications/CueMol3.app Windows Uninstall CueMol3 from "Apps & features / Add or remove programs" Linux (AppImage) Delete the .AppImage file Linux (.deb) Remove it with a package manager, for example sudo apt remove cuemol3

docs.title: Configuring external tools
docs.text: Some features of CueMol3 work by calling external programs. If they are bundled with your distribution, you can use them as they are. In builds that do not bundle them, you need to specify the path to each executable in Settings.

docs.title: Opening the Settings tab
docs.text:
Settings does not open as a separate window. It opens as a tab in the content area.

OS Action macOS Application menu > Preferences... (Cmd+,) Windows / Linux Edit > Options (Ctrl+K) All Gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar on the far left

If a Settings tab is already open, that tab becomes active.

docs.title: Display > Rendering
docs.text:
Tools used by the rendering window.

Ray tracing needs no external tool

The default rendering backend of CueMol3 is the built-in ray tracer Umbreon, which is part of the library and needs no configuration. Of the tools below, POV-Ray and blendpng are used only when you choose POV-Ray, the older backend (see Rendering).

Setting Target Purpose POV-Ray Executable POV-Ray itself Ray tracing with the POV-Ray backend POV-Ray Include Directory Directory of the standard POV-Ray include files Same as above blendpng Executable blendpng Layer compositing of rendering results with the POV-Ray backend ffmpeg Executable ffmpeg Encoding of movie output. Required regardless of the backend

docs.title: Tools > APBS / PDB2PQR
docs.text:
Used for the electrostatic potential map calculation (Tools > APBS elepot calculation...).

Setting Purpose APBS Executable Path to APBS itself pdb2pqr Executable Path to pdb2pqr (assigns charges and radii) pdb2pqr Force Field Default force field used by pdb2pqr

Warning

If the paths to APBS and pdb2pqr are not set, the Start button in the APBS dialog cannot be pressed.

docs.title: Specifying paths
docs.text: Each input field has a file selection button. Use the button to choose a file (or a directory for POV-Ray Include Directory), or type the path directly. Settings are persisted in the application and kept the next time you start it.

docs.title: What is bundled
docs.text:
OS ffmpeg / APBS and PDB2PQR / POV-Ray macOS (CI build) Bundled Windows (CI build) Bundled Linux Not bundled (install separately) Builds you package yourself May not be bundled, depending on how they were prepared

Even if they are not bundled, the features work once you install the programs separately and set the paths above.

Umbreon is built into the library, so it is not listed in this table. With any OS distribution, ray tracing is available without additional installation.

docs.title: Installing on Linux
docs.text:
Target: Linux (x64). Two release assets are provided: CueMol3-<version>-Linux-x64.AppImage and CueMol3-<version>-Linux-x64.deb (for how to obtain them, see Download).

A CPU with AVX2 support is required

The x86-64 build is compiled with AVX2 instructions. An Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or later CPU (roughly 2013 or later) is required. On older CPUs, the program crashes when a molecular surface is generated (→ Installation).

docs.title: AppImage
docs.text:
Runs as a single file without installation.

chmod +x CueMol3-<version>-Linux-x64.AppImage
./CueMol3-<version>-Linux-x64.AppImage

To remove it, simply delete the file.

FUSE may be required

Running an AppImage requires FUSE. If it does not run, install the distribution's package (such as libfuse2), or run it with the --appimage-extract-and-run option.

docs.title: .deb package
docs.text:
On Debian / Ubuntu based systems, the .deb can be used.

sudo apt install ./CueMol3-<version>-Linux-x64.deb

The .deb also registers file associations, so CueMol3 is listed under "Open With" in the file manager (the default application is not changed → Installation). The AppImage contains the same information, but whether it is registered depends on your desktop integration tool.

Uninstall with the package manager.

sudo apt remove cuemol3

docs.title: Code signing
docs.text: Linux release assets are not signed, but no startup warning caused by code signing appears. As on macOS / Windows, this is a development version.

docs.title: Configuring external tools
docs.text:
The Linux release assets do not include ffmpeg / APBS / PDB2PQR / POV-Ray. To use the features that depend on them (movie output, electrostatic potential calculation, and POV-Ray for the legacy backend), install them separately, for example through the distribution's package manager, and specify their paths in Settings. Ray tracing is performed by the built-in Umbreon, so no separate installation is needed.

→ Configuring external tools

docs.title: Installing on macOS
docs.text:
Target: macOS / Apple Silicon (arm64). The release asset is CueMol3-<version>-macOS-arm64-Installer.dmg (see Download for how to obtain it).

Ad-hoc signed only; the publisher is not verified

The app carries an ad-hoc signature (codesign --sign -). This is required for the app to launch on Apple Silicon and does not verify the publisher. The app is not signed with a Developer ID and is not notarized, so a dmg downloaded from the web is given the quarantine attribute and cannot be launched as is. Use the procedure below to work around this.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Double-click CueMol3-<version>-macOS-arm64-Installer.dmg to mount it
  2. Drag the CueMol3.app that appears into the Applications folder to copy it
  3. Launch the app for the first time using one of the following methods (see below)

docs.title: Working around the first-launch warning
docs.text:
On first launch, a dialog appears saying, in essence, that "CueMol3" was not opened, and the only choices are "Move to Trash" and "Done". Either of the following methods launches the app.

\"Open\" from the right-click menu does not work

On macOS 14 and earlier, right-clicking the app (Ctrl + click) and choosing Open worked around this. That method was removed in macOS 15 (Sequoia) and later. Right-clicking offers only "Move to Trash". The same applies to macOS 26 (Tahoe).

docs.title: Method A: Allow from System Settings (recommended)
docs.text:
1. Double-click /Applications/CueMol3.app to try launching it once (when the dialog appears, click Done to close it. Do not click "Move to Trash")
  2. Open Apple menu > System Settings
  3. Select Privacy & Security and scroll down to the Security section
  4. Click Open Anyway next to the line saying "CueMol3" was blocked
  5. Authenticate with Touch ID or your login password
  6. If a confirmation dialog appears, click Open Anyway again

The button in step 4 does not appear unless step 1 has been done. If the button is not visible, start over from the launch attempt.

Once the app has been launched this way, it can be launched by double-clicking as usual from then on.

docs.title: Method B: Remove the quarantine attribute
docs.text:
Run the following in Terminal. Afterward, the app can be launched by double-clicking.

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CueMol3.app

This method also works when the message "CueMol3 is damaged and can't be opened" is shown and the button of Method A does not appear.

Note

A dmg built locally by yourself does not get the quarantine attribute, so this warning does not appear.

docs.title: Bundled external tools
docs.text:
The macOS release assets built by CI include ffmpeg, APBS/PDB2PQR and POV-Ray. For builds that do not include them, such as a locally packaged build, specify the paths in Settings. Umbreon, used for ray tracing, is built into the library and is therefore not part of the bundle.

→ Configuring external tools

docs.title: Updating
docs.text: From 2.4.0.546 onward, a new release can be installed from within the app (→ Update).

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text: Move /Applications/CueMol3.app to the Trash.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
The macOS (Apple Silicon) version of CueMol3 can check for new releases and replace itself from within the app. For the Windows / Linux versions, download the new release assets and reinstall (→ Download).

From 2.3.21.544 or earlier, install manually once

In-app updating was introduced in 2.4.0.546. CueMol3 2.3.21.544 and earlier do not have this mechanism, so install manually a build of 2.4.0.546 or later once. Subsequent releases can be installed from within the app.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Checking for new releases
docs.text:
• Check at startup: Shortly after launch, CueMol3 checks GitHub for a new release. If one exists, a notification is shown. If the check fails (for example, when offline), nothing is shown. The check can be turned off with Check for Updates at Startup in Settings > General > Updates (ON by default).
  • Manual check: Use Check for Updates... in the application menu, or Check Now in Settings > General > Updates, to check at any time. If you are already running the latest version, this is indicated.

On Windows / Linux, Help > Check for Updates... is also present, but it only displays "Updates are not available in this build."

docs.title: Installing the update
docs.text:
1. Click Update in the new-release notification (or in the Settings row). Click Release Page to open the release's page on GitHub.
  2. The download starts and its progress is shown (Cancel aborts it). The downloaded file is verified.
  3. The Install Update dialog shows the release notes. Click Restart and Update: after the check for unsaved scenes, CueMol3 quits, is replaced with the new version, and restarts. If you click Later, you can continue afterward from Restart to Update in the notification.
  4. After startup, "CueMol3 has been updated to <version>." is displayed.

If the new version fails to start, the original version is restored and restarted, and a notification reports this. The restored version is not offered again by the startup check.

Release assets fetched by the app do not get the quarantine attribute, so the first-launch warning does not appear.

docs.title: When Update is not shown
docs.text:
In the following cases the app cannot be replaced in place, so Update is not shown and only Release Page is available. Download the release assets and install manually.

  • The app does not have write permission for the folder it resides in
  • The app is running without having been moved from where it was downloaded (App Translocation). Move CueMol3.app to the Applications folder and launch it from there

docs.title: Notification center
docs.text: Update notifications are collected in the notification center, opened from the bell icon at the right end of the status bar. The bell is marked when there are unread notifications, and during a download its progress is shown next to the bell. New notifications also appear at the lower right of the screen.

docs.title: Settings > General > Updates
docs.text: Item Default Description Check for Updates at Startup ON Checks for a new release after startup and notifies if there is one. Manual checks are still possible when OFF Check for Updates — Shows the current version and status. It has Check Now / Release Page / Update buttons, from which the update can be run

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Installing on macOS
  • Release history — main changes for each release
  • Settings reference

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Installing on Windows
docs.text:
Target: Windows (x64). The release asset is CueMol3-<version>-Windows-x64-Setup.exe (an NSIS installer) (see Download for how to obtain it).

The release asset is unsigned

The current .exe is not code-signed with Authenticode. A SmartScreen warning is displayed when it is run. Use the procedure below to work around it.

A CPU with AVX2 support is required

The x86-64 build is compiled with AVX2 instructions. A CPU of Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or later (roughly 2013 or later) is required; on an older CPU, the program crashes when a molecular surface is generated (→ Installation).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
CueMol3-<version>-Windows-x64-Setup.exe is a wizard-style NSIS installer. When run, it proceeds as follows.

  1. Welcome page
  2. Choose the install location
  3. Run the installation (the program is installed for all users in C:\Program Files\CueMol3\, so a UAC elevation prompt is displayed)
  4. Finish

After installation, shortcuts are created in the Start menu and on the desktop, and CueMol3 is registered in "Apps & features / Add or remove programs". The file formats that CueMol3 can open are also registered under "Open with" in Explorer (the default application is not changed → Installation). Files can also be opened by double-clicking them or by passing them on the command line.

docs.title: Working around the first-run warning
docs.text:
When an unsigned .exe is run, "Windows protected your PC" (unknown publisher) is displayed.

  1. Click "More info" in the dialog
  2. Click the "Run anyway" button that appears

Future plans

This warning will go away once code signing is introduced (an EV/OV certificate or Azure Trusted Signing). Introduction is planned as future work.

docs.title: Bundled external tools
docs.text:
The Windows release assets built by CI include ffmpeg / APBS-PDB2PQR / POV-Ray. For builds that do not include them, specify the paths in Settings. Umbreon, which is used for ray tracing, is built into the library, so it is not among the bundled tools.

→ Configuring external tools

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text: Select CueMol3 in "Settings > Apps > Installed apps" (or "Add or remove programs") and uninstall it.

docs.title: Menu reference
docs.text: A list of every item in the CueMol3 menu bar. For items that were renamed, moved or removed since CueMol2, see also Merged, renamed and removed features.

docs.title: Differences between operating systems
docs.text:
The menu contents differ slightly depending on the OS.

macOS Windows / Linux Menu bar location System menu bar at the top of the screen (OS native) Top of the window Application menu Yes (see below) No Item that opens the settings Application menu > Preferences... Edit > Options Quit Application menu > Quit CueMol3 File > Quit About CueMol3 In the application menu In the Help menu Check for Updates... In the application menu In the Help menu Help menu Not shown (its only items are About and Check for Updates, and these are in the application menu) Shown

Read the modifier key Cmd on macOS as Ctrl on Windows / Linux. This reference uses Cmd and gives both where necessary.

docs.title: macOS application menu
docs.text:
On macOS, the menu named after the application (CueMol3) has the following items.

Item Description Shortcut About CueMol3 Shows the version information Check for Updates... Checks for a new release and, if there is one, updates in the app (→ Updating) Preferences... Opens the Settings tab (switches to it if it is already open) Cmd+, Services The macOS Services menu Hide CueMol3 Hides the window Cmd+H Hide Others Hides the windows of other apps Cmd+Option+H Show All Shows all windows again Quit CueMol3 Quits CueMol3. If there are unsaved scenes, a confirmation is shown Cmd+Q

docs.title: Menus
docs.text:
• File — Reading and writing scenes and Objects, tab operations
  • Edit — Undo, molecule editing, settings
  • Rendering — Image and movie output, scene export
  • Scene — Background color, scene properties
  • View — Projection mode, center mark, view properties
  • Tools — Analysis and calculation tools
  • Window / Help — Switching windows, version information

docs.title: Legend
docs.text:
The tables on each page use the following symbols.

Symbol Meaning In development The item exists in the menu but does not work in the current version. Choosing it does nothing (added in CueMol3) An item that did not exist in CueMol2 and was newly added in CueMol3 (renamed in CueMol3) An item whose name changed from CueMol2

Items that existed in CueMol2 but are no longer in the CueMol3 menus are not listed in this reference. Where they moved to, and alternatives, are summarized in Merged, renamed and removed features.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Edit menu
docs.text: This menu covers undoing operations, the clipboard, editing molecular structures, and application settings.

docs.title: Undo and redo
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Undo Undoes the last operation. Disabled when there is nothing to undo Cmd+Z Redo Redoes an undone operation. Disabled when there is nothing to redo macOS: Cmd+Shift+Z / Windows, Linux: Ctrl+Y

The shortcuts act on whichever element has focus. If you undo a typing mistake in a text field with Cmd+Z, scene operations are not rolled back. The Undo / Redo buttons on the toolbar always act on the scene, regardless of focus.

Undoing several steps at once

The toolbar's Undo / Redo buttons have a history dropdown, which lets you go back several steps at once (→ Toolbar and tool palette). You can check the operation performed in each step in the History panel of the Actions view (→ Recording and replaying operations).

docs.title: Clipboard
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Cut Cuts the selected item Cmd+X Copy Copies the selected item Cmd+C Paste Pastes the clipboard contents Cmd+V Select All Selects everything in the text field if one has focus; otherwise selects everything in the active selectable area (such as the log in the Output panel) Cmd+A

What Cut / Copy / Paste act on depends on where the focus is.

Focus Target Text field The text being entered (standard OS editing operations) Scene tree Object / Renderer / Renderer group / style set nodes Camera panel Cameras Paint table in the Color panel Table rows History panel in the Actions view Copies the operation of the selected step as a Console command (Copy only)

Cut in the scene tree was added in CueMol3. The selection is deleted only after it has been written to the clipboard, so the selection is never lost if writing fails, and the deletion can be reverted with a single Undo. The same operation is also available from the scene tree's context menu.

You can copy and paste between CueMol2 and CueMol3

Copying goes through the OS clipboard. You can copy a Renderer / Renderer group / Object / camera / style / Paint row in CueMol3 and paste it into CueMol2, or the other way around. Selections and colors are resolved again against the destination scene when pasting, so you can also paste into a different Renderer or a different scene.

Using the OS clipboard has two side effects: copying in CueMol3 replaces the text on the clipboard, and copying in another application discards what you copied earlier.

docs.title: Clearing history
docs.text: Item Description Shortcut Clear undo data Discards the Undo history. The Undo / Redo state is updated as well

docs.title: Editing molecular structures
docs.text:
All of these open a tool dialog.

Item Description Shortcut Merge molecule... Merges two molecule Objects into one Delete mol atoms... Deletes the selected atoms from a molecule Change chain ID... Changes the chain ID Change residue number... Changes the residue number

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Options Opens the Settings tab (switches to it if it is already open). Windows / Linux only (on macOS, use Preferences... in the application menu) Ctrl+K

Settings is a tab, not a dialog

In CueMol2, Options was a modal preferences window; in CueMol3 it opens as a tab in the content area, so you can work in the molecular view while looking at the settings. You can also open it from the gear icon at the bottom of the activity bar on the far left.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: File menu
docs.text: Reads and writes scenes and Objects, and manages tabs.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text: Item Description Shortcut New Tab Creates a new tab. In the dialog, choose New Scene (a new scene) or New View (another view of an existing scene). New Scene also lets you set the display settings of the new scene (Scene settings: Anti-aliasing / Ambient occlusion / Background / CMYK color proofing). The confirmed values become the defaults for subsequent new scenes (including those created at startup or by dropping a file). New View also lets you choose whether to inherit the current camera Cmd+T Close Tab Closes the current tab. If the scene is unsaved and only one view is showing it, you are asked whether to save Cmd+W

docs.title: Loading Objects
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Open File... Opens files such as molecular coordinates, density maps and molecular surfaces. The Renderer type and format-specific options can be set at load time Cmd+O Open MD Trajectory... Opens an MD simulation trajectory (added in CueMol3). It appears when the MD Tools plugin is enabled (→ Plugins) Get PDB... Fetches a structure from the network by PDB ID. Coordinates (RCSB CIF / PDB) and density maps (RCSB cif.gz, EBI MTZ) are supported. The data is loaded directly without a temporary file, and can be interrupted with Cancel in the progress dialog Open Recent Opens a file chosen from the list of recently opened files (up to 10). Clear Menu clears the history

For the list of supported formats, see Supported file formats.

For files whose format cannot be determined from the extension alone (such as .cif, where several formats share the same extension), the format is determined by reading the contents. Files whose header is long and whose coordinates start several hundred KB into the file, such as recent PDB mmCIF files, can also be opened.

When opening a CCP4/MRC density map, the options screen shows the grid size and the amount of memory required to load it. Map type specifies whether the map is treated as a crystallographic map or a cryo-EM map (the default is Auto (from header), which decides from the file header), and Subsample loads the map with the grid thinned out (→ DensityMap). For maps with too many grid points, a warning is shown and a Subsample value that fits in memory is suggested. Subsample discards grid points at load time, so the map cannot be made finer afterwards. Map type and Subsample are shown only when opening CCP4/MRC. For maps in other formats, Map type can be changed in the inspector after loading.

When opening a density map, the Renderer options show View after loading instead of an atom selection. Auto (by map kind) (the default) moves the view so that the whole map fits for cryo-EM maps (Move view center (fit the map)), and for crystallographic maps aligns the map display center with the current view center without moving the view (Set map center (keep the view)). Either behavior can also be selected explicitly.

Files can also be opened without the menu by dragging & dropping them from the OS onto the window (files of types that cannot be opened are refused before you drop them). MD trajectory files (.xtc / .dcd / .trr) contain only frames and cannot be opened on their own, so dropping one shows a message to open it with Open MD Trajectory... (if MD Tools is disabled, the message asks you to enable it first in Settings > Plugins). Files can also be opened by double-clicking them in the file manager or passing them on the command line (→ File associations).

For these two routes, Drag and drop opens into / File manager opens into in Settings > General > Files select whether files are loaded into the current scene or a new scene (the default for both is the current scene). Open File... and Open Recent always load into the current scene regardless of this setting (→ Settings).

docs.title: Saving Objects
docs.text: Item Description Shortcut Save File As... Saves a single Object to a file, not the scene. Only Objects that have a supported save format are eligible; if there are two or more of them, a screen for choosing the target appears. The save format used last becomes the default next time Save current view... Saves the camera of the current view to a .cam file

docs.title: Reading and writing scenes
docs.text: Item Description Shortcut Open Scene... Opens a CueMol scene file (.qsc). PyMOL sessions (.pse) can also be loaded from here. Cmd+Shift+O Reload Scene Reloads the scene from its original file. If there are unsaved changes, you are asked first. Cmd+R Save Scene Overwrites the scene file. If no save location is set, it behaves like Save Scene As.... A backup named <file name>.bak is created automatically before overwriting. Cmd+S Save Scene As... Saves the scene to a specified location. Save options (data embedding / compatibility / compression / character encoding) can be specified. Cmd+Shift+S

docs.title: Quit
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Quit Quits CueMol3. For tabs with unsaved scenes, you are asked whether to save; canceling aborts the quit. Windows / Linux only (on macOS it is in the application menu) Ctrl+Q

The window close button goes through the same confirmation

The close button at the top right of the window (top left on macOS) and Cmd+Q share the same confirmation process.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.20.539

docs.title: Rendering menu
docs.text: Output high-quality images and movies, and export the scene to various file formats.

docs.title: Open the rendering window
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Image rendering... (renamed in CueMol3) Opens the rendering window in still image (Still) mode Movie rendering... (renamed in CueMol3) Opens the rendering window in movie (Movie) mode

Changes from CueMol2

In CueMol2, these were separate windows named after the Renderer: "POV-Ray rendering..." and "Animation rendering...". In CueMol3 they are merged into a single rendering window, and the menu items now represent the type of output (still image / movie). The rendering backend is selected in the window (the default is Umbreon, the built-in ray tracer).

The rendering window is modeless (non-modal), so the molecular view can be operated while it is open. For details, see Rendering window.

The Render button on the toolbar also opens the same window, but does not change the mode.

docs.title: Export scene
docs.text:
Writes the current scene to various file formats. Select the format from the submenu.

Item Description PNG image... Writes a PNG image using the same rendering as the screen display. Size, resolution (DPI) and background transparency can be specified Umbreon ray-traced image... Writes a PNG ray-traced with Umbreon, the built-in ray tracer. The options are the same as for PNG image... POV-Ray SDL... Writes a scene description file (.pov) for rendering with external POV-Ray. An .inc file is also generated in the same location. No image is output STL... Writes shape data in STL format (.stl) Metasequoia (MQO)... Writes a Metasequoia object file (.mqo)

When some items are not displayed

Items for exporters that are not built into the library in use are hidden from the submenu by a check at startup. The distributed builds include Umbreon, but if you build CueMol yourself without enabling HAVE_UMBREON, Umbreon ray-traced image... is not displayed.

Export to LuxRender / Warabi / raw format / QSL, which was available in CueMol2, is not provided in CueMol3.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.7.489

docs.title: Scene menu
docs.text:
Settings that affect the whole scene.

Item Description Shortcut Background > White Sets the background color to white. A color swatch is shown next to the item, and the check mark follows the current background color Background > Black Sets the background color to black. A color swatch is shown next to the item, and the check mark follows the current background color Use color proofing Toggles color proofing (simulation of color reproduction in CMYK output). The check mark follows the current state. If no ICC profile is set, enabling it assigns the default profile; disabling it keeps the profile setting Properties... Opens the current scene in the property inspector

The background color can also be changed from the right-click menu

Right-click the scene row in the scene tree to use the Background submenu and the Use color proofing check item in the same way.

Items editable in Properties...

The scene Properties are not shown in a modal dialog as in CueMol2, but in the Properties tab of the property inspector. They include settings for ambient occlusion, anti-aliasing, background and color proofing, and changes are reflected in the molecular view immediately. For the list of items, see the Scene reference.

Use this also to specify an arbitrary background color (the Background menu items only switch between white and black).

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.12.517

docs.title: Tools menu
docs.text:
This menu collects tools for structure analysis and calculation.

Bond editing has moved to the tool palette

CueMol2's Tools > Mol bond editor... has been replaced in CueMol3 by the Add Bond tool in the tool palette at the left edge of the molecular view. There is no menu item (→ Toolbar and tool palette).

docs.title: Analysis and generation tools
docs.text:
See the page linked from each item name for details.

Item Description Shortcut Molecular superposition... Superposes two molecules (US-align / SSM / LSQ). The RMSD and other results are shown in the log of the Output panel Interaction... Detects interactions between atoms (distances and hydrogen bonds) and displays them as labels. You can specify the target molecule and selection, the distance range, and the maximum number of labels Reassign secondary str... Recalculates and reassigns the secondary structure of proteins Mol morphing animation... Creates a morphing animation that interpolates between two structures. Converts the target molecule to a MorphMol and adds the structures that serve as frames Mol surface generation... Generates a molecular surface (SES) Object. You specify the target molecule, selection, mesh density (Point density), probe radius, and generation algorithm (Algorithm) Mol surface cutter... Cuts a molecular surface with a plane. You can choose how the cut face is handled (main body only / cut face only / split into two Objects) APBS elepot calculation... Calculates an electrostatic potential map using APBS. Assigns charges and radii with pdb2pqr, runs APBS, and loads the result

APBS requires configuration

If the paths to the APBS and pdb2pqr executables are not set in Settings, the dialog's Start button cannot be pressed (→ Configuring external tools).

Molecular surface generation algorithms

Algorithm offers Auto / MeshMS / BALL. The default Auto selects MeshMS, and if MeshMS fails it switches to BALL automatically, so a surface is always generated (→ MolSurfObj (molecular surface)).

Measuring distances, angles and dihedral angles

Distances, angles and dihedral angles between atoms are measured not from a menu but with the Distance / Angle / Torsion tools in the tool palette at the left edge of the molecular view (→ Toolbar and tool palette).

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: View menu
docs.text: Settings that apply per view, such as the projection mode and the center mark of the molecular view.

docs.title: Projection
docs.text: Item Description Shortcut Perspective Switches to perspective projection. The current projection mode is checked Orthographic Switches to orthographic projection. The current projection mode is checked

docs.title: Center mark
docs.text:
Selects how the mark that indicates the rotation center is displayed.

Item Description Shortcut Center mark > Cross Shows a cross mark Center mark > Axis Shows the coordinate axes Center mark > None Hides the center mark

docs.title: Tool palette
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Tool palette Collapses / opens the tool palette on the molecular view. Checked while it is shown Cmd+Shift+P

When collapsed, only the handle at the top edge of the palette remains. Clicking the handle toggles it in the same way. The state is kept for the next launch (→ Toolbar and tool palette).

docs.title: View properties
docs.text: Item Description Shortcut View property... Opens the current view on the Generic tab of the property inspector

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
Item Description Shortcut Toggle Developer Tools Opens / closes the developer tools. Used when investigating problems

Also available from the side panel

The projection mode and center mark can also be switched from View > View in the left side panel. This panel also provides numeric controls for view operations such as rotation, translation, zoom and slab (→ Side panels).

Hardware stereo has been discontinued

View > Hardware stereo, which existed in CueMol2, is not provided in CueMol3 (→ Merged, renamed and removed features).

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.15.530

docs.title: Window menu
docs.text:
(Added in CueMol3)

CueMol3 has two top-level windows: the main window and the rendering window. This menu switches which window is brought to the front.

Item Description Shortcut Main Window Brings the main window to the front. If it is minimized or hidden, it is restored Rendering Window Brings the rendering window to the front. If it is not open, it is opened first and then brought to the front

Differences between operating systems

On macOS, the menu bar belongs to the OS (shared by the whole application), so this menu can be used to return to the main window even when the rendering window is in front.

On Windows / Linux, the menu bar is inside the main window, so to return to the main window from the rendering window, click the window directly (the rendering window is an independent window, not a child window).

Not the same as the CueMol2 Window menu

The CueMol2 Window menu (Show/Hide Topbar / Clear log contents / Restore default panel location) was removed because it does not correspond to the CueMol3 UI layout. The CueMol3 Window menu is a new menu dedicated to switching windows (→ Merged, renamed and removed features).

docs.title: Help menu
docs.text:
Shown on Windows / Linux only. On macOS, the items (About and Check for Updates) are merged into the application menu, so this menu itself is not shown.

Item Description Shortcut About CueMol3 Shows version information Check for Updates... Checks for a new release. In-app update is currently available only in the macOS (Apple Silicon) build; on Windows / Linux, a message saying it is unavailable is shown (→ Updating)

Mozilla-specific items were removed

About plugins... / About config... / Addon manager... / Console in the CueMol2 Help menu were all features specific to Mozilla XULRunner, so they were removed from the Electron-based CueMol3. Check for updates has been rebuilt with a mechanism specific to CueMol3.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
This chapter is an exhaustive collection of settings and syntax. It gathers reference material for readers who already know how to use the software and need to look up a specific item.

To learn by following the flow of operations, see the Quick tour or the Tutorials.

Some pages are still being written

Only the outline and part of the content are done. Pages marked "In preparation" are skeletons with headings only; their content will be added over time.

docs.title: Recording and replaying operations (Actions)
docs.text:
For each Undo step, CueMol3 records the operations (ops) performed in it. The record can be viewed in the Actions view on the activity bar. It can be saved to a qax file, replayed later, or applied to another Object as a macro.

The Actions view has two panels.

Panel Contents History The Undo history of the active scene and the operations performed in each step Actions Presets bundled with the app and operations you have saved (User Actions)

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Recorded operations
docs.text:
Most edits made in the GUI, and edits made from the Console (native mode and PyMOL-compatible mode), the MCP Server and the AI Agent, are recorded as operations that can be saved and replayed. These include property changes, file loading and fetching, Renderers and styles, coloring and Paint, selections, molecular editing, superposition, labels and measurements, crystal symmetry, morphing, animation, camera, style sets, electrostatic potential calculation, and copy & paste.

Edits to MD trajectories are not recorded yet.

The Undo / Redo display (including the Undo / Redo dropdown on the toolbar) is also built from the recorded operations. It shows details such as which Renderer was created and which property was changed.

docs.title: History panel
docs.text:
Shows the Undo history of the active scene, one step per row.

  • The Initial state row at the top is the start of the history.
  • A step containing two or more operations can be expanded, which lists the operations performed, one per row.
  • The right side of each row shows where the edit came from (gui / cmd / pym / mcp / ai / qax).
  • Undone steps (on the Redo side) are shown in gray italics, and the row at the current position is shown in the accent color.
  • Click a row to select it; Shift / Cmd / Ctrl + click selects multiple rows.

docs.title: Panel operations
docs.text:
The following operations are available from the toolbar at the top of the panel and from the right-click menu on a row.

Operation Description Go to step (Go to This Step / Go to Initial State in the right-click menu) Repeats Undo / Redo until the state of the selected row is reached Copy as commands Copies the operations of the selected steps as Console (native mode) commands. Edit > Copy (Cmd+C / Ctrl+C) in the panel does the same Save as qax Saves the selected steps to a qax file Save to Actions Saves the selected steps to User Actions in the Actions panel (→ Saving as a macro) Show in Inspector (right-click only) Shows the selected step in the property inspector

docs.title: Display in the inspector
docs.text:
Double-click a step row (or press Enter), or click an expanded operation row, and the inspector shows its contents read-only. You can check the Undo label, the source of the edit, the time, the state (Done / Undone), and the name, command and arguments of each operation. Showing a step does not change the Undo position.

Steps for edits with no recorded operations (such as edits to MD trajectories) cannot be saved to qax.

docs.title: Actions panel
docs.text:
A list of operations that can be replayed. There are two groups.

  • Presets — presets bundled with the app
  • User Actions — qax files you have saved. They are placed in the actions folder inside the user data folder

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
Select an item in the list and press Run on the toolbar (or Run in the right-click menu). Double-clicking does not run it.

  • A macro is applied to the Object selected in the scene tree. If a Renderer is selected, its Object is the target. If nothing is selected and the scene has only one Object, that Object is the target. The target is shown in Target at the top of the panel.
  • Running with multiple Objects selected is treated as a single Undo. Objects that could not be applied to are skipped and listed at the end.
  • A qax file that is not a macro is applied by name to the Object it was recorded on.

docs.title: Right-click menu
docs.text: Item Description Run Runs it Copy to User Actions Copies a preset macro to User Actions Rename... / Move to Trash Renames a User Actions file / moves it to the trash Open in Editor Opens the qax file in an editor Reveal in Finder Opens the location of the qax file

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Preset Description Cartoon + ligand Shows the protein as a rainbow cartoon and ligands and ions as ball & stick (water is not drawn) Ligand site Shows the ligand and the residues within 5 Å of it as ball & stick, and centers the view on the site B-factor cartoon Shows the protein as a cartoon colored by B-factor Transparent surface Overlays a semi-transparent molecular surface on the protein Electrostatic surface Shows a molecular surface colored by electrostatic potential (APBS). Requires APBS and pdb2pqr to be configured (→ Configuring external tools) Ligand contacts Shows contacts and hydrogen bonds between the ligand and everything else as labeled lines Symmetry mates Shows the symmetry mates that fill the unit cell and the unit cell box. Targets an Object with crystal information White background Sets the background to white (for print figures) Black background Sets the background to black (for slides) Render image Renders the view at the scene's rendering size and saves it to the desktop as cuemol_render.png 360 degree spin Adds and plays an animation that rotates the view once Front, side and top cameras Saves the current view as front and the views rotated 90° around the y axis and x axis as side / top in the camera list

The seven presets from Cartoon + ligand to Symmetry mates are macros applied to an Object, and the five from White background onward can be run without selecting an Object.

docs.title: Saving as a macro
docs.text:
Select steps in the History panel and press Save to Actions to open a dialog for saving them to User Actions under a name.

  • With Run on the selected object (save as a macro) ON, it is saved as a macro. A macro is applied to the Object selected when it is run.
  • With it OFF, it is saved as an operation applied by name to the Object it was recorded on.

In the following cases the steps cannot be saved as a macro, and the dialog shows the reason.

  • The selected steps span two Objects
  • The selected steps operate on a Renderer that was not created within them (also select the step that creates that Renderer)

docs.title: qax files
docs.text:
A qax file is a file in which recorded operations are written in XML (extension .qax).

  • Save it with Save as qax or Save to Actions in the History panel.
  • In native mode of the Console, replay it with run file.qax (or @file.qax). Each recorded operation becomes one Undo. list_actions shows the history, and export_actions file[, first[, last]] writes it to a qax file. open_log also records subsequent operations to a qax file.
  • From a terminal, replay it with tritium_cli file.qax (→ tritium_cli).
  • qax files cannot be run in PyMOL-compatible mode.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Edits to MD trajectories are not recorded.
  • Only operations that take no arguments or exactly one Object can be made into macros.
  • The History panel shows only the history of the active scene.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Side panels — Where the Actions view fits
  • Console / MCP Server / AI Agent
  • Edit menu — Undo / Redo

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
A camera is a named, saved state of the view (position, orientation, zoom and slab). Cameras are listed in View > Camera in the side panel, and can be recalled at any time to return to the same view.

In preparation

The information a camera holds, loading .cam files, and the items for editing display flags will be added later.

docs.title: Working with cameras
docs.text:
Cameras are managed in the Camera panel, which appears when View is selected in the activity bar (→ Side panels). The six most common commands are toolbar buttons; the rest are in the right-click menu of a row.

In the table below, the "Right-click menu" column gives the menu item name and the "Toolbar" column gives the button tooltip.

Right-click menu Toolbar Description New Camera... New camera from view Creates a new camera from the current view. If a camera with the same name exists, it is overwritten without confirmation Save from view Save from view Overwrites the selected camera with the current view Save from scene (with vis flags) Save from view with show/hide Same as above, and also saves the visibility flags Apply to view Apply to view Returns to the saved view Apply to scene (with vis flags) Apply to view with show/hide Same as above, and also restores the visibility flags. Double-clicking a row does the same Delete Delete Deletes the camera. The Del / Backspace keys do the same Rename... — Renames the camera. F2 does the same Copy / Paste Camera — Copies and pastes cameras. Also available from the Edit menu and with Cmd+C / Cmd+V Camera file > Load... / Reload / Save / Save As... — Reads and writes camera files (.cam). Reload is available only for cameras loaded from a file Edit vis flags... / Clear vis flags — Edits or clears the visibility flags. Clear vis flags is available only for cameras that have flags

The order of the list can be changed by dragging rows, and is saved in the scene file. __current is pinned at the top and cannot be reordered.

CueMol2 (UXP version) does not preserve camera order

Camera order was introduced in CueMol3. If a scene with a custom order is saved again in CueMol2, the cameras return to alphabetical order.

docs.title: Camera files (.cam)
docs.text: The camera of the current view can be written to a .cam file with Save current view... in the File menu (→ File menu).

docs.title: Visibility flags
docs.text: A camera can carry flags that specify whether each Renderer is shown when the camera is applied. Use them to switch the visible elements from one view to another.

docs.title: Color syntax
docs.text:
Colors are usually specified with the color picker, but they can also be written directly as text. Colors in scene files (.qsc) and style files are written in the syntax described here.

Entering colors as text

The CueMol3 GUI is centered on the color picker, but the syntax described here can also be used for finer adjustment. In particular, colors with modifiers cannot be specified from the GUI.

docs.title: HTML notation
docs.text: Same as the # color notation used in HTML and CSS.

docs.title: 6-digit notation
docs.text:
#UVWXYZ

U to Z are digits 0-9 or letters A-F. UV is the red intensity, WX the green intensity, and YZ the blue intensity.

Examples:

#1234AB

Red=0x12 (=18/255), Green=0x34 (=52/255), Blue=0xAB (=171/255).

#FFFFFF

Red=0xFF, Green=0xFF, Blue=0xFF gives white.

docs.title: 3-digit notation
docs.text:
#XYZ

X is a digit 0-9 or a letter A-F. Equivalent to #XXYYZZ.

Example:

#CCC

Red=0xCC (=204/255), Green=0xCC, Blue=0xCC gives gray.

docs.title: RGB notation
docs.text:
rgb(X,Y,Z)

X, Y and Z are real numbers from 0 to 1 and represent the red, green and blue intensities.

Example:

rgb(1.0, 0.5, 0.5)

This gives pink.

docs.title: Notation with alpha (opacity)
docs.text:
rgba(X,Y,Z,W)

X, Y, Z and W are real numbers from 0 to 1. W is the opacity; 0 is fully transparent.

docs.title: HSB notation
docs.text:
hsb(X,Y,Z)

X is a real number from 0 to 360 and represents the hue (0 is red and 180 is light blue). Y and Z are real numbers from 0 to 1 and represent the saturation and the brightness.

docs.title: Notation with alpha (opacity)
docs.text:
hsba(X,Y,Z,W)

W is the opacity; 0 is fully transparent.

docs.title: Name notation
docs.text:
NAME

NAME is a color name made of letters, digits, _, + and -. Specifies a color by a color name defined in a style file. Names are case-insensitive. The system default style file defines the same kind of color names as those available in HTML / CSS (CSS Color Module Level 3).

Example:

antiquewhite

This is the same color as #faebd7.

docs.title: Molecule color notation
docs.text:
$molcol

Can be used in the color settings of Renderers that refer to a molecular Object. Besides molecular structure Renderers, it also works for Solid coloring of molecular surfaces (molsurf / dsurface) and isosurfaces (isosurf). It refers to the color specified on the corresponding molecular Object.

When the coloring of the molecular Object is changed, the color of Renderers that use $molcol follows. Use it when several Renderers should share the same coloring. → Coloring

docs.title: Modifiers
docs.text:
Written in curly braces ({}) after any of the color specifications above. Multiple modifiers are separated by semicolons.

<color>{<modifier1>;<modifier2>;...}

A modifier consists of a key and a value.

modifier := <key> : <value>

The following keys are available. The key determines the kind of value that can be specified.

material Specifies the material. The value is a string naming the material → Material alpha Specifies the opacity. The value is a real number from 0 to 1 mod_h Change in hue. The value is any real number mod_s Change in saturation. The value is any real number mod_b Change in brightness. The value is any real number

Modifiers can be used with the rgb, hsb, # and color name notations alike, but apart from material there is little point in using them with anything other than the color name notation or the molecule color notation.

Examples:

rgb(1,0,0){material: shadow; alpha: 0.5}

Specifies red with the material changed to shadow (flat fill without shading) and the opacity changed to 0.5.

$molcol{mod_s: -0.2}

Specifies the molecule color with the saturation (1 is the pure color; the smaller the value, the whiter the color) decreased by 0.2. That is, the color is slightly whiter than the coloring specified on the molecule side.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Coloring
  • Material

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.15.530

docs.title: Coloring
docs.text:
Coloring determines the rule by which a Renderer is colored. You set it per Renderer (or per Object) in the Color panel of the side panel.

This page is a reference covering the parameters of each Coloring. For how to use the panel, see Side panels.

docs.title: Coloring types
docs.text:
Type Description Applies to Paint Specify pairs of a selection and a color in a table All Solid Paint with a single color All CPK Assign a color to each element All Bfac/Occ Gradient according to values such as temperature factor or occupancy All Rainbow Change colors across the rainbow along residue numbers, etc. All Electrostatic potential Color by the values of an electrostatic potential map Molecular surfaces only Multi-gradient Gradient passing through multiple colors Map Renderers and molecular surface Renderers Reset to default style Return to the coloring of the default style All

Renderers that cannot handle color (selection highlight, atom labels, atomintr, etc.) do not appear in the target list of the Color panel.

In preparation

Details of the parameters of each Coloring will be added later.

docs.title: Paint
docs.text:
Specify pairs of a selection and a color in a table. Rows are evaluated from the top, and the color of the first matching row is used.

Choosing Paint as the Coloring type opens a submenu. Default is a Paint that starts from the standard per-secondary-structure coloring (four rows: sheet / helix / nucleic / *), followed by color schemes defined as styles (Woody / Red, etc.). Molecule color is a style that makes the Renderer's color follow the molecule-side coloring; it is not a Paint (see Molecule-side coloring).

For color notation, see Color syntax; for how to write selections, see Selection expression syntax.

docs.title: Solid
docs.text:
Paints the whole Renderer with a single color. It can be used in the same way on molecular surfaces (molsurf / isosurf / dsurface).

If you specify $molcol as the color, the Renderer follows the coloring of the molecule Object (see Molecule-side coloring). This gives the same result as placing a single row (*, $molcol) in a Paint.

Choosing $molcol is no longer a one-color fill that ignores atoms

Molecular surface Renderers have a mode that paints with one color without referring to any atoms. Choosing $molcol in Solid switches to a mode that looks up the color of each atom, so the Renderer leaves that mode. To go back, use Reset to default style. For an isosurface (isosurf), you can also go back with Solid color in the Density map panel.

docs.title: CPK
docs.text: Assigns predetermined colors to each element. You can specify a color for each of C / N / O / S / P / H and for other elements.

docs.title: Bfac/Occ
docs.text: Changes the color continuously according to values such as the temperature factor (B-factor) or occupancy.

docs.title: Rainbow
docs.text: Changes the hue continuously along the order of residue numbers, etc.

docs.title: Electrostatic potential
docs.text:
Colors a molecular surface according to the values of an electrostatic potential map (ElePotMap). It can be selected only for molecular surface Renderers.

APBS / PDB2PQR are required for the calculation (see Configuring external tools).

docs.title: Multi-gradient
docs.text:
Paints with a gradient that passes through multiple colors according to map values. It can be selected for map Renderers such as density maps and for molecular surface Renderers (molsurf / dsurface).

The settings area shows a histogram of the target map and a gradient bar, and you edit the stops (color breakpoints) on the bar directly.

  • Drag a stop to move it. Click an empty spot on the bar to add one, and drag a stop downward to delete it
  • The value and color of the selected stop can also be edited in the input fields
  • You can also start from a preset (Rainbow / Resmap / Heatmap)

Edits are reflected immediately in the molecular view, and each operation can be reverted with Undo.

docs.title: Reset to default style
docs.text: Returns the Renderer's coloring to the state defined in the default style (see Styles).

docs.title: Molecule-side coloring ($molcol)
docs.text:
You can also keep the coloring on the molecule Object rather than on each Renderer, and share it among multiple Renderers. In this case, use $molcol in the Renderer's color specification (see Color syntax).

For molecular surface Renderers, choosing $molcol as the color of Solid gives this form.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Color syntax
  • Selection expression syntax
  • Styles
  • Side panels

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.15.530

docs.title: Scene file (.qsc)
docs.text:
Reference for the structure of the CueMol scene file .qsc. It is compatible with CueMol2, so scenes created in CueMol2 can be opened in CueMol3.

In preparation
