docs.title: Embedding data and external references
docs.text: When saving a scene, you can choose whether to embed the data of molecular coordinates and density maps in the scene file itself, or to keep only a reference to the original file (see Save Scene As... in the File menu).

docs.title: Compression and character encoding
docs.text: In the save options, you can specify the compression method and the character encoding.

docs.title: NPR (ink-style rendering)
docs.text:
Umbreon (NPR) is a rendering backend that expresses shading with hatching (collections of lines or dots) instead of photorealistic ray tracing. The result looks like a figure drawn in ink on paper.

Because it uses the built-in Umbreon, no external program or path setting is needed, just as with Rendering.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Select Umbreon (NPR) in Backend on the run bar of the rendering window. A Hatching section appears in the Render tab, and a Detail tab is added to Render Settings.

First choose the overall feel with Style in Hatching, and if needed adjust the density and thickness of lines and dots with Mark density and Mark width. If this is not enough, edit the contents of the style in the Detail tab.

docs.title: Hatching (Render tab)
docs.text:
Item Default Description Style richardson Template for the drawing feel (see below) Coloring Style default How ink and paper colors are combined (see below) Mark density 1.0 (0.25-4) Multiplier that divides the spacing of lines and dots. At 2, the number of lines and dots doubles Mark width 1.0 (0.25-4) Multiplier for line thickness and dot size Custom ink color / Ink color OFF / #000000 The ink color is specified explicitly only when ON Custom paper color / Paper color OFF / #ffffff The paper color is specified explicitly only when ON Default contour edges ON Draws contour lines also for Renderers that have no edge lines configured

Mark density and Mark width are multipliers applied uniformly to the per-layer values of the style. Even for a style made of several layers, the ratio of spacings between layers is preserved.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
The first three (richardson / ink-cross / manga) each define a complete look, including how tones are built and the ink colors. The remaining six define only how marks are arranged; the paper and ink colors are chosen with Coloring.

Style Description richardson Jane Richardson-style colored-pencil ribbon figure. An ink in the Object's color on a paper base, three pencils of the same hue, and bright areas left as bare paper (default) ink-cross Plain pen drawing. Black cross-hatching on white paper manga Flat fill for each part + screentone dots and hard ink lines pen-cross Three layers of hard cross-hatching lines (45 / -45 / 0 degrees), no wobble pencil Two layers of soft pencil lines. Wobble, width variation, tapered strokes, paper grain engraving Engraving style with single-direction lines divided finely stipple Scattered dots of uniform size, with tone expressed by the number of dots (stippling for scientific figures) screentone-60 45-degree halftone dot screen manga-square 45-degree square-dot screen

docs.title: Coloring
docs.text:
The combination of ink and base (paper / fill) is chosen independently of the style.

Coloring Description Style default Leaves it to the style's own settings (default) Ink on paper Black ink on paper. Pen drawing Colored ink on paper Colored ink on paper. Colored-pencil drawing Ink on color fill Black ink over a flat fill in the Renderer's color. Comic style Colored ink on color fill Colored ink over a flat fill. Printed-matter style

If you choose anything other than Style default, the style's colors are not used

richardson has its own warm paper and per-part ink colors. Choosing an explicit combination in Coloring overrides them. Conversely, using a Style that defines only how marks are arranged (pen-cross and below) with Style default fixes the combination to black ink on white paper.

docs.title: Differences in Quality
docs.text:
The Quality section of Umbreon (NPR) differs from the photorealistic Umbreon in the following points.

  • Lighting has only two options, Raytrace only (default) and Ambient Occlusion. Global illumination is disabled when hatching is used, so there is no GI lighting axis.
  • Supersampling has the same meaning. The minimum hatching spacing is determined not by the output pixels but by the grid after supersampling, so raising it is effective for fine styles.

The other individual settings (Lights / Ambient Occlusion / Shadows / Edges / Transparency) are the same as in Rendering (only the Lights defaults differ from the photorealistic Umbreon: Light intensity 1.55 / Flash fraction 0.6).

docs.title: Detail tab
docs.text:
The Style selected in the Render tab is loaded as a template, and its contents can be edited. Style template: <style name> is shown at the top of the tab.

  • An Edited badge appears once you edit.
  • Reset to style returns to the state of the template.
  • When you switch the Style in the Render tab, the edits are discarded without confirmation.

Edits are saved in the scene

Edits in the Detail tab are saved in the scene, like the other rendering settings (→ Saving settings). An unedited style is rendered through exactly the same path as before this feature existed.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
Hatching is built by stacking several layers. Each layer has one grid, on which lines or dots are placed. Layers can be added with the Line / Dot buttons in the section header, and duplicated or deleted from each layer's header.

Item Default Range Description Kind Line (lines) / Dot screen (halftone dots) / Stipple (stippling) Angle 45 -180 to 180 degrees Orientation of the grid Spacing 10 0.25-64 px Spacing of the grid Width 1.1 0.1-8 px Line thickness (Line only) Dot scale 1 0.1-8 Dot size (Dot screen / Stipple only) Tone high 0.95 0-1 Brightness at which the first mark appears Tone low 0.55 0-1 Brightness at which the last mark appears. No more marks are added below this Fade (0 = auto) 16 0-64 How quickly a mark grows to its maximum size after appearing. 0 means automatic Opacity 1 0-1 Opacity of the layer Ink darkness 1 0-1 Darkness of the ink

Opening Randomness / Advanced shows the wobble settings that give a hand-drawn look, and finer shape settings. Items unrelated to the Kind are not shown.

Kind Items in Randomness / Advanced Common Edge softness / Seed / Position jitter / Paper tooth / Tooth scale Line / Dot screen Nesting levels Line Wobble / Wobble wavelength / Width jitter / Stroke length / Stroke gap / Stroke taper / Angle jitter / Length jitter Dot screen / Stipple Shape exponent / Aspect / Dot angle Dot screen Merge to solid

Nesting levels is the number of nesting levels of the grid. As the tone gets darker, new marks are inserted between the existing marks. Marks never disappear or move, so there is no flicker even when the brightness changes continuously.

docs.title: Shading
docs.text:
Determines how much ink a given brightness is converted into. Two items are always shown.

Item Default Range Description Strength 1 0.25-3 Overall increase or decrease of the amount of ink. Raising it darkens the whole image Curve 1 0.5-2 How the midtones are shifted

Advanced contains the settings for how tones are built (Diffuse weight / Ambient / Wrap / Contour darkening / Contour power / Contour light bias / Contact AO / Shape AO / Black point / White point / Highlight knee / Highlight softness / Gamma / Specular cut / Tone levels) and the ink model (Mode / Base / Ink / Ink color / Paper color / Min contrast / Ink shade / Tone fog / Fill posterize).

If the whole image is too light, raise Strength

Lighting in the molecular view is bright and flat, so with some styles the default leaves the hatching sparse. Adjust Strength first, then Curve.

docs.title: Settings that have no effect are not shown
docs.text:
Items that do not affect the image are either hidden or disabled.

  • Items that do not apply to the Kind (such as Stroke length for Dot screen) are not shown.
  • Items that are disabled by other values remain visible but cannot be changed (such as Contour power when Contour darkening is 0, or Seed when wobble is not used).
  • A layer whose Spacing has reached the minimum spacing after supersampling (2 px) displays a note to that effect. Raising Supersampling resolves it.

docs.title: Display of effective values
docs.text: Mark density and Mark width remain multipliers on the Render tab side and are not baked into the layer values. When the multiplier is not 1, the Detail tab also shows the values after the multiplier is applied. This keeps edits reversible.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Rendering — Settings for Umbreon (photorealistic)
  • Rendering window — Layout and operation of the window
  • Edge lines — Contour line settings on the Renderer side

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.14.525

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
Settings for ray-tracing output in the rendering window. The default rendering backend of CueMol3 is the built-in ray tracer Umbreon.

Umbreon is built into the visualization library (libcuemol2), so no external program and no path setting are needed. For how to open the window and run a render, see Rendering window.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
Select the backend with Backend in the run bar at the bottom of the rendering window.

Backend Description Umbreon Built-in ray tracer. Default. No external program required Umbreon (NPR) Same ray tracer, with ink-drawing-style output in which shading is expressed by hatching → NPR (ink-style rendering) POV-Ray Legacy backend. Deprecated

Distributed builds include Umbreon, so Umbreon is already selected when the window opens. A backend you switch manually is saved in the scene, like the other settings (→ Saving settings).

This page covers the settings of Umbreon, which produces photorealistic output. For the Hatching group and the Detail tab of Umbreon (NPR), see NPR (ink-style rendering) (the Lighting and Supersampling in Quality and the individual settings are shared).

POV-Ray will be kept for the time being

POV-Ray has been used as a backend since CueMol2, but it is deprecated in CueMol3. It requires a separate external POV-Ray installation and lacks the shading features of Umbreon (ambient occlusion / global illumination). It remains as an option for reproducing past scenes with the same appearance, but use Umbreon for new images.

To use POV-Ray, set the path to the executable in Settings (→ Configuring external tools).

docs.title: Common settings not used by Umbreon
docs.text:
Of the settings in the Image tab and Camera, the following items are not used by Umbreon. While Umbreon is selected, the setting fields themselves are hidden.

Item Why it is hidden Stereo mode / Stereo depth Umbreon does not support stereoscopic output CPU threads Umbreon renders in parallel within the process, so it does not accept a thread count Post-render alpha blending Umbreon composites transparency itself, so the external blendpng is not used Pixel labels A POV-Ray-only feature

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
This section is at the top of the Render tab. Quality is not a single slider but a combination of mutually independent axes, so each axis has its own dropdown.

Lighting How shading is applied. The default is Global Illumination Supersampling Base image quality. The default is 3x AO quality Quality of ambient occlusion. Shown only when Lighting is Ambient Occlusion GI lighting Distribution of light for global illumination. Shown only when Lighting is Global Illumination Shadows How shadows are cast. The default is Off

Each dropdown rewrites the values of the individual settings below in one go. Conversely, if you change an individual setting by hand, no level matches the new value, so the display of that axis changes to Custom.

docs.title: Lighting
docs.text:
Select how to give a sense of depth by darkening the concave parts of a molecule and brightening the protruding parts.

Lighting Description Raytrace only No shading. The fastest, with a flat appearance Ambient Occlusion Computes shading from occlusion by the surroundings Global Illumination Computes shading by tracing light bounces (default)

Only one of Ambient Occlusion and Global Illumination can be selected, because both achieve the same purpose (a sense of depth through shading) by different methods.

Why Global Illumination is the default

Global Illumination has a built-in denoiser, so the result looks clean even with a small number of samples. For a comparable sense of depth, it takes far less time than Ambient Occlusion at High.

docs.title: Supersampling
docs.text:
Render at an integer multiple of the output size and then downscale, which reduces jagged outlines.

Supersampling Description 1x (off) No enlargement. The fastest 2x 3x Default 4x Highest quality

The amount of computation grows with the square of the factor (4x is 16 times 1x).

The quality of edge lines is also determined by this factor. If edge lines look jagged, raise it first. This is why the default is 3x.

docs.title: AO quality
docs.text:
Shown when Lighting is Ambient Occlusion.

AO quality Description Low For drafts, with fewer samples Medium Standard (default) High Computes shading exactly for each point

High takes an extremely long time

Low and Medium compute in batches per output pixel, but High recomputes for each shading point, so it can be tens of times slower than Medium. Medium is sufficient except for the final image.

docs.title: GI lighting
docs.text:
Shown when Lighting is Global Illumination. Select, in levels, how much of the energy of the frontal light (headlight) is moved to the global-illumination bounce light. The strength of the key light from diagonally above does not change at any level.

GI lighting Description 0 (raytrace match) Same light distribution as Raytrace only. The global-illumination bounce is minimal 1 2 3 4 (max GI) Turns the headlight off completely and shades with only the key light and the bounce (default)

Changing the level does not change the average brightness. What changes is how the shading appears. Low noise is determined not by this axis but by the individual setting GI samples. The level rewrites the individual settings Light intensity / Flash fraction / Ambient fraction in one go, and changing any of them by hand changes the display to Custom.

docs.title: Shadows
docs.text:
Cast shadows from the light source. This can be set independently of Lighting.

Shadows Description Off No shadows (default) Hard Shadows with sharp outlines Soft Blurred shadows Very soft More blurred shadows

Shadows fall only on meshes

Parts drawn as spheres or cylinders (the atoms and bonds of cpk and ballstick) receive no shadows. For molecular representations Lighting alone gives a sense of depth, so the default is Off.

docs.title: Individual settings
docs.text: An accordion below the Quality section. Open it when the presets are not enough. Changing a setting here changes the display of the corresponding axis to Custom.

docs.title: Antialiasing
docs.text: Item Default Range Description Supersampling 3 1-8 Same value as Supersampling in Quality

docs.title: Lights
docs.text:
Light source settings that apply regardless of the Lighting method. Umbreon (NPR) has the same group.

Item Default Range Description Light intensity 1.3 0-3 Overall strength of the light sources Flash fraction 0 0-1 Fraction of the direct light assigned to the headlight from the viewpoint direction. The rest becomes the key light from diagonally above. The smaller it is, the sharper the shading

When Lighting is Global Illumination, the GI lighting level rewrites these two. Selecting Raytrace only or Ambient Occlusion returns them to 1.55 / 0.6. The defaults of Umbreon (NPR) are also 1.55 / 0.6. If you switch back to Global Illumination from there, GI lighting re-enters at the default level (4).

docs.title: Ambient Occlusion
docs.text:
Shown only when Lighting is Ambient Occlusion.

Item Default Range Description AO samples 64 1-256 Samples per point. More is smoother but slower AO distance (0 = auto) 0 0-1000 Radius within which occluders are searched. 0 determines it automatically from the size of the scene AO intensity 1.0 0-1 Strength of the shading AO on direct light 1.0 0-1 Fraction by which shading is also applied to direct light. At 0, the shading becomes almost invisible Multi-scale AO ON Combines large and small radii to emphasize both fine bumps and the overall shape Bent normal ON Applies ambient light taking the direction of occlusion into account Low-discrepancy sampling ON Spreads samples evenly to reduce noise AO gather Per output pixel Unit of the shading computation. Per output pixel is per output pixel (fast); Per shading hit is per shading point (exact, slow)

Leave AO distance at 0 (auto)

At 0 the radius is derived from the size of the whole scene, so shading looks the same for a small peptide and for a large complex. Enter a positive value only when you want to fix a specific radius.

docs.title: Shadows
docs.text:
Item Default Range Description Cast shadows OFF Whether shadows are cast Shadow samples 1 1-64 Number of shadow samples. More is smoother but slower Light radius (deg) 0.0 0-30 Apparent size of the light source (degrees). Values above 0 give blurred shadows

The larger the Light radius, the wider the shadow edges blur and the more noise appears, so increase Shadow samples as well.

docs.title: Edges
docs.text:
Umbreon-specific settings for how edge lines are drawn. Whether edge lines are drawn, and their thickness and color, are specified with the common properties on the Renderer side.

Item Default Range Description Crease angle (deg) Off Off / 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 90 / 120 Lower limit (degrees) of the fold angle of faces drawn as crease lines. Effective when Edge type is Edges; the larger the angle, the fewer folds are drawn, leaving only distinct ones. Off draws no crease lines Contact edges ON Draws the lines where Renderers with different edge-line settings intersect (see below) Outline far depth 0.2 0-1 When Edge type is Silhouette, the depth at which outlines behind faces faded by fog start to be drawn. A fraction of the fog range: 0 is the view center and 1 is the end of the fog

Contact edges draws the intersection lines where the shape of one Renderer pierces the surface of another (for example, a ballstick bond going into a ribbon). Renderers with the same edge-line settings (type, thickness, color) are treated as one group, and intersection lines are drawn only between groups (not between the Renderers that make up a single cartoon). In a scene where all Renderers have the same edge settings (for example, all left at the defaults), no intersection lines are drawn. The molecular view does not draw these intersection lines. If you turn this setting OFF, intersection lines are no longer drawn, and for Renderers whose Edge type is Silhouette the outline is interrupted where they touch other Renderers.

docs.title: Transparency
docs.text:
How overlapping translucent Renderers are composited. Available in both Umbreon and Umbreon (NPR) (not in POV-Ray). Collapsed by default.

Item Default Description Per-pixel transparency ON Composites translucency pixel by pixel

Each translucent Renderer is drawn as if opaque and then composited. When ON, the weights are determined only by the layers that actually cover the pixel, so the weight of the background never becomes negative. OFF is the conventional layer-by-layer compositing: in a pixel where translucent layers whose opacities sum to more than 1 overlap, the weight of the background becomes negative, and dark things behind them are inverted to bright (for example, black edge lines seen through a translucent surface appear white).

A pixel covered by only one translucent layer looks the same whether ON or OFF. The difference appears only where layers overlap. The rendering time is the same either way. Turn it OFF only when you need the same result as blendpng or POV-Ray.

docs.title: Global Illumination
docs.text:
Shown only when Lighting is Global Illumination.

Item Default Range Description GI samples 32 8 / 32 / 64 / 256 Samples per pixel. More reduces noise but is slower Denoise OIDN Noise removal method. OIDN / A-trous / None Ambient fraction 0.6 0-1 Fraction of the total light gathered as global-illumination bounce. Rewritten by the GI lighting level Sky gradient ON Makes the sky, which is the light source of the bounce, a gradient that is white at the top and approaches Ground color toward the bottom. The brightness of the bounce then varies with the orientation of the surface (the overall brightness does not change) Ground color #666666 Ground-side color of Sky gradient

With Denoise set to None, the image is grainy unless GI samples is made large. Normally leave it at OIDN.

docs.title: Edge lines and materials
docs.text:
Some of the common properties on the Renderer side affect only ray-tracing output.

Material Umbreon resolves the surface appearance from the material name. Some appearances differ from POV-Ray Edge lines In Umbreon, the Silhouette Edge type is a mode that draws only the outer outline. Renderers with the same edge-line settings (type, thickness, color) form one group with a single outer outline, and no lines are drawn where they overlap. Edges also draws the inner crease lines in addition to the outline. Edge lines are also drawn in the molecular view, and are adjusted to look as similar as possible

docs.title: Rendering from the command line
docs.text:
Images can also be written from a scene file (.qsc) without using the GUI. Both routes use Umbreon.

cuetty --input scene.qsc --render out.png --width 1920 --height 1080

python -m cuemol.umbreon_render scene.qsc out.png -W 1920 -H 1080

--camera (-c) specifies a camera saved in the scene. If omitted, the current view (__current) that the GUI writes when saving the scene is used.

Both render using the rendering window settings saved in the scene (→ Saving settings) as they are. A scene with no saved settings is rendered with the defaults (Lighting is Global Illumination, 1200×1200 px), and the projection follows that of the camera. --width / --height (-W / -H) override the saved size.

Text such as atom labels is not rendered

If you need a figure with labels, use the rendering window.

docs.title: Saving settings
docs.text:
The rendering window settings (the Backend selection and the contents of the Image / Render / Detail tabs) are saved in the scene and read and written together with the scene file (.qsc). When you switch Target, the settings of that scene are shown. Only values changed from the defaults are written.

Changing settings is an edit of the scene and can be undone. In the rendering window as well, Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y on Windows / Linux) work (when a text field has focus, they undo within the field).

The history of render results records the settings used at run time. The history arrows switch only the image; pressing the Use settings button restores the settings used when that image was rendered to the editor and the scene (this can be undone with a single Undo) (→ Rendering window). The output destination settings for movies are held by the application, not the scene, and remain the next time the window is opened.

docs.text:

  • NPR (ink-style rendering) — settings of the Umbreon (NPR) backend

docs.title: Scene
docs.text:
A Scene is the top-level element of the scene tree. It holds Objects, Renderers, the camera, style sets, and animations. Display settings that apply to the whole scene are also stored as Scene properties.

One scene is shown per tab. The same scene can also be shown in multiple tabs (views) (→ New Tab in the File menu). The display settings for a new scene (anti-aliasing / ambient occlusion / background color / color proofing) can be specified under Scene settings in the New Tab dialog, and the confirmed values become the defaults for subsequent new scenes. "Default" below means the factory value.

docs.title: Opening the properties
docs.text:
Choose Properties... from the Scene menu, or select the scene row in the scene tree. The properties appear in the Properties tab of the property inspector (→ Property inspector). Changes are applied to the molecular view immediately. Sections are not collapsible; all of them are shown at the same time.

There is no modal dialog as in CueMol2.

docs.title: Ambient occlusion
docs.text:
Settings for screen-space ambient occlusion (GTAO). It casts shadows into recessed parts of a molecule to emphasize depth.

Enabled Enables or disables ambient occlusion. The default is disabled Preset Preset for how the shading is applied. Not selectable while disabled Preset Description Low Shading reaches a short distance, emphasizing fine surface detail (default) Medium Intermediate High Shading reaches a long distance, emphasizing the overall shape of the molecule

A preset bundles the shading reach, the number of samples, and the intensity into one set. When the reach is increased, the number of steps is increased so that sampling does not become coarse, and the intensity is lowered so that wide areas do not become too dark.

Medium and High are computationally expensive, so they are computed at half resolution only while the view is being moved, and redrawn at full resolution when the view stops. Image export always uses full resolution.

Individual adjustments are in the Generic tab

Individual values such as radius, intensity, number of slices, number of steps, and half-resolution rendering do not appear in the Properties tab. They can be edited in the Generic tab of the inspector. When a value is changed in the Generic tab, the Preset display changes to Custom.

The items that can be edited in the Generic tab are as follows.

Property Default Description aoEnabled false Enable / disable (same as Enabled in the Properties tab) aoRadius 4.0 Radius of the sphere in which shading is computed aoIntensity 2.2 Contrast. The larger the value, the lighter the shading aoSlices 9 Number of horizontal slices. Larger values are smoother but slower aoSteps 3 Number of samples per slice aoHalfRes false Computes at half resolution only while the view is moving, and redraws at full resolution when it is still. Export always uses full resolution. The Medium / High presets enable this

docs.title: Anti-aliasing
docs.text:
Settings for the post-processing that reduces jagged edges in the molecular view. They can be set independently of ambient occlusion.

Quality Anti-aliasing quality Quality Description Off No post-processing (direct rendering with hardware MSAA) Standard (FXAA) Edge smoothing with FXAA (default) High (FXAA + 8x SS) FXAA plus 8-sample supersampling Ultra (FXAA + 32x SS) FXAA plus 32-sample supersampling

Supersampling takes effect once the view is still

The supersampling of High / Ultra accumulates samples only while the view is still. Rendering while the view is moving does not become heavier; image quality improves progressively after you stop. Moving the view restarts the accumulation.

The items that can be edited in the Generic tab are as follows.

Property Default Description aa_method fxaa Method. Choose from none / fxaa / smaa aaJitterLevel 0 Supersampling level. 0 is disabled; 1 to 5 correspond to 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 samples aaSmaaThreshold 0.05 Edge detection threshold for SMAA. The smaller the value, the more edges are processed

SMAA is not included in the Quality presets, so to use it, set aa_method to smaa in the Generic tab. The Quality display then changes to Custom.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Color Background color. The default is black

The Scene menu and the right-click menu of the scene tree have a white / black toggle, but to specify an arbitrary color, set it here (→ Scene menu).

docs.title: Color proofing
docs.text:
A display that simulates color reproduction in CMYK output. It lets you check on screen how colors will look when printed.

Enabled Enables or disables color proofing. The default is disabled. If it is enabled while no ICC profile is set, the default CMYK profile is assigned Profile ICC profile to use Intent Rendering intent. Choose from Perceptual (default) / Relative colorimetric / Saturation / Absolute colorimetric

The profile and intent settings are retained when proofing is disabled again.

docs.title: Scene information
docs.text:
The following items are read-only and are shown in the Generic tab.

Property Description name Scene name src Path the scene was loaded from srctype Format of the source basePath Directory used as the base for resolving relative paths

docs.title: Selection expression syntax
docs.text:
Reference for the syntax of selection expressions, which specify a part of a molecule. The syntax is shared with CueMol2 selection expressions, and compatibility with scene files (.qsc) is preserved.

A selection expression consists of selection literals and selection operators. Some selection literals take a name list or a number list as an argument.

Where to enter selection expressions

  • Selection panel — Type a selection expression directly and apply it. The expression is validated as you type, and expressions used before can be reused from History. The selection builder, which assembles an expression in the GUI without writing it, is also available (→ Selection builder)
  • The sel property of a Renderer — In the property inspector, or in the Selection field of the New Renderer dialog, specifies the range that the Renderer draws
  • Selection fields in dialogs — Specify the target for molecular surface generation, interaction detection and so on

→ Side panels

docs.title: Selection literals
docs.text: A selection literal works as a selection command by itself. It can be combined or modified with the operators described below.

docs.title: Select all
docs.text:
all
*

Selects all atoms in the molecule.

docs.title: Select none
docs.text:
none

Selects nothing.

docs.title: Selection by element
docs.text:
elem [name list]
e; [name list]

Atoms whose element name is given in the name list are selected. e; is an abbreviation of elem. With an abbreviation, the whitespace after the ; can be omitted (the same applies to the other abbreviations below).

Example:

e; C,N,O

Selects the carbon, nitrogen and oxygen atoms in the molecule.

docs.title: Selection by atom name
docs.text:
name [name list]
n; [name list]

All atoms whose atom name is given in the name list are selected.

Example:

n; CA,N,O

Selects all atoms in the molecule named CA, N or O. These are usually the α carbon, amide nitrogen and carbonyl oxygen atoms of the protein main chain.

docs.title: Selection by residue name
docs.text:
resn [name list]
r; [name list]

All atoms in residues whose name is given in the name list are selected.

Example:

r; ARG,LYS

Selects the ARG (arginine) and LYS (lysine) residues in the molecule.

Regular expressions can also be used in the name list (→ Name list).

r; /^A/

Selects residues whose name starts with A, such as ARG, ALA and ASN.

docs.title: Selection by residue number
docs.text:
resi [number list]
resid [number list]
i; [number list]

All atoms in residues whose number is given in the number list are selected.

Example:

i; 3,5,10:20

Selects all residues numbered 3, 5, and 10 to 20.

docs.title: Selection by chain name
docs.text:
chain [name list]
c; [name list]

All atoms in chains whose name is given in the name list are selected.

Example:

c; A,B

Selects chains A and B.

docs.title: Hierarchical notation
docs.text:
A notation with parts separated by dots, as follows.

chain name.residue number.atom name

Selects atoms that have the given atom name (multiple names can be specified in name list form), in the residues in the range of the given residue number (multiple values can be specified in number list form), in the chains with the given chain name (multiple names can be specified in name list form). If * is specified, all chains / residues / atoms become targets.

This notation has exactly the same meaning as

chain "chain name" and resid "residue number" and name "atom name"

Examples:

A.1:100.CA,CB

Selects the α and β carbons of residues 1 to 100 in chain A.

*.5,6,7.*

Selects all atoms in residues 5, 6 and 7 of all chains. This is equivalent to resid 5,6,7.

docs.title: Selection by residue property
docs.text:
rprop [name1]=[name2]

All atoms in residues whose residue property given by [name1] has the value given by [name2] are selected.

Example:

rprop secondary=helix

Selects all atoms in residues whose residue property secondary is helix.

docs.title: Selection by B-factor
docs.text:
bfac <comparison operator> <number>
<comparison operator> := "<" | ">" | "="

Atoms whose B-factor satisfies the condition given by the comparison operator and the number are selected. The number can be a real number.

Example:

bfac>50

Selects atoms with a B-factor greater than 50.

docs.title: Selection by occupancy
docs.text:
occ <comparison operator> <number>
<comparison operator> := "<" | ">" | "="

Atoms whose occupancy satisfies the condition given by the comparison operator and the number are selected.

Example:

occ>0.5

Selects atoms with an occupancy greater than 0.5.

docs.title: Selection by alternate conformation
docs.text:
alt [name list]

Atoms whose alternate conformation ID is given in the name list are selected.

Examples:

alt A,null

Selects atoms with alternate conformation A, and atoms without an alternate conformation (blank in the PDB file). Note that if, for example, only the side chain of a residue has alternate conformations, only the side chain is selected unless the expression is written like this.

A.7.* & alt B, null

Within residue 7 of chain A, selects atoms with alternate conformation B and atoms without an alternate conformation.

docs.title: Selection by atom ID
docs.text:
aid [number list]

Atoms whose internal atom ID is given in the number list are selected. The atom ID is a serial number assigned internally when a molecule is loaded, and it is not guaranteed to be preserved when the scene is saved and reloaded. Normally, use the other selection literals above.

docs.title: AND operator
docs.text:
[expr1] and [expr2]
[expr1] & [expr2]

Creates a selection that is the intersection of the selections represented by expr1 and expr2. When written as &, the spaces before and after can be omitted.

Example:

chain A and resn ALA
c;A&r;ALA

Selects only the ALA residues belonging to chain A in the molecule.

docs.title: OR operator
docs.text:
[expr1] or [expr2]
[expr1] | [expr2]

Creates a selection that is the union of the selections represented by expr1 and expr2.

Example:

chain A or resn ALA

Selects the whole of chain A and all ALA residues in the molecule.

docs.title: NOT operator
docs.text:
not [expr1]
! [expr1]

Creates a selection that is the complement of the selection represented by expr1.

Example:

not resn ALA

Selects everything in the molecule except ALA residues.

docs.title: AROUND operator
docs.text:
[expr1] around [real value]
[expr1] around ["molecule name"] [real value]
a; ... (abbreviation of around)

Selects atoms within the given distance (in Å) of the selection represented by expr1. Note that the selection of expr1 itself is not included.

In the second form, selects atoms in the other molecule given by the molecule name that are within the given distance (in Å) of the selection represented by expr1.

Examples:

chain A around 3

Selects the set of atoms within 3 Å of chain A. Chain A itself is not selected.

chain A around ["1CRN.pdb"] 3

Selects the set of atoms within 3 Å of chain A in the molecule named 1CRN.pdb (the selection is empty unless the same scene contains a molecule Object named 1CRN.pdb).

docs.title: EXPAND operator
docs.text:
[expr1] expand [real value]
ex; ... (abbreviation of expand)

Selects atoms within the given distance (in Å) of the selection represented by expr1. Note that, unlike AROUND, the selection of expr1 itself is also included.

Example:

chain A expand 3.5

Selects chain A itself and the set of atoms within 3.5 Å of it.

docs.title: BYRES operator
docs.text:
byres [expr1]
br; [expr1]

Extends the selection of expr1 to whole residues.

Example:

byres name SD

Extends the set of atoms named SD to whole residues. For proteins, this selects all methionine (Met) residues.

docs.title: BYSIDECH operator
docs.text:
bysidech [expr1]

Restricts the selection of expr1 to side chains only. For proteins, the region selected by bysidech also includes Cα, to make the display easier to read.

Example:

bysidech A.10:100.*

Selects only the side chains (and Cα) of residues 10 to 100 in chain A.

docs.title: BYMAINCH operator
docs.text:
bymainch [expr1]

Restricts the selection of expr1 to the main chain only.

docs.title: NEIGHBOR / EXTEND operators
docs.text:
neighbor [real value]
extend [real value]

These are accepted by the grammar, but the selection processing is not implemented, so the result is always an empty selection. Do not use them.

docs.title: Named macros
docs.text:
Frequently used selection expressions have predefined names. The names can be written as they are in a selection expression.

Name Definition Meaning protein rprop type=prot Protein nucleic rprop type=nucl Nucleic acid water rprop type=water Water molecules sugar rprop type=pyranose Sugar (pyranose) ligand !rprop type=prot and !rprop type=nucl and !rprop type=water Anything other than protein, nucleic acid and water hydrogen elem H Hydrogen atoms helix rprop secondary=helix α helix sheet rprop secondary=sheet β sheet coil !rprop secondary=helix and !rprop secondary=sheet Anything other than helix and sheet

Example:

protein and !hydrogen

Selects the non-hydrogen atoms of the protein.

docs.title: Name list
docs.text:
name [, name, ...]

A name list consists of a name, or a list of names separated by commas. Any number of spaces, including none, may appear before and after a comma.

The first character of a name is a letter, a digit or an underscore (_). From the second character on, a prime (') and an asterisk (*) can also be used in addition to these. Letters are case-insensitive.

If a name contains any other character (such as a dot), it must be enclosed in " (double quotation marks). Note that when enclosed in double quotation marks, letters are case-sensitive.

Primes and asterisks in nucleic acid atom names

Atom names in the sugar part of nucleic acids are written either with a prime, as in C1', or with an asterisk, as in C1* in old PDB files. If you write the selection expression with a prime, it also matches atoms named with an asterisk. Conversely, an expression written with an asterisk does not match atoms named with a prime.

docs.title: Regular expressions
docs.text:
Regular expressions can be used as a name list.

/^A[0-9][0-9]$/

The above selects three-character names such as A01, whose first character is A and whose remaining two characters are digits. To match the whole name, ^ (matches the beginning of the line) must be added at the start and $ (matches the end of the line) at the end, as in this example.

Comma-separated notation of an ordinary name list and regular expressions can be mixed.

ABC,/^A[0-9][0-9]$/

Selects ABC and A followed by a two-digit number.

Note that letters in a regular expression are case-sensitive.

docs.title: Number list
docs.text:
<range> [, <range>, ...]
<range> := <number> | <number1>:<number2>

A number list consists of a range, or a list of ranges separated by commas. A range is either a single integer (number) or two integers in the form number1:number2. The latter represents the range of integers from number1 to number2, inclusive.

1, 3:10, 51

The above represents the set of integers 1, 3, 4, ..., 9, 10 and 51.

docs.title: Special case for residue numbers (insertion code)
docs.text:
When specifying residue numbers, an insertion code can be included. For example, to select residue numbers 20A and 20B, write

i; 20A, 20B

A range notation such as 20A:20Z is also possible. However, the ordering of residue numbers that include insertion codes is subtle, so unexpected residues may be selected.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text:
A list of the items in the Settings tab. Open it from Preferences... (Cmd+,) in the application menu on macOS, or from Edit > Options (Ctrl+K) on Windows / Linux.

Choose a category in the tree on the left, then edit the values on the right.

docs.text: Item Default Description Dark Mode ON Switches between the dark and light themes

docs.text:

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
Paths of the external tools used by the rendering window. If they are bundled with the release assets, the default values work as they are (→ Configuring external tools).

Item Description POV-Ray Executable Path to the POV-Ray executable POV-Ray Include Directory Directory containing the standard POV-Ray include files blendpng Executable Path to blendpng, which composites the layers of a rendering result ffmpeg Executable Path to ffmpeg, used to encode movies

No setup is needed for the default rendering

The default rendering backend, the built-in ray tracer Umbreon, is built into the library, so it has no items in Settings. POV-Ray and blendpng in the table above are used only when the legacy POV-Ray backend is selected (→ Rendering).

docs.title: Mouse & Navigation
docs.text:
Item Default Description Pointing device Auto-detect How scroll input is mapped to view operations. Mouse zooms with the wheel; Mac trackpad translates with two-finger scrolling and zooms with pinch; Auto-detect infers the device from the characteristics of the scroll input XY Rotation Sensitivity 0.8 Sensitivity of rotation around the X / Y axes (0.1 to 5.0) Pick Precision 10 px Tolerance radius when picking atoms or Objects by clicking (1 to 50 px) GPU Picking ON Picks from the rendered shapes themselves. When OFF, picking reverts to the earlier method based on atom positions. This is a fallback for slow machines. Switching takes effect immediately Hover Info ON Shows what is under the pointer in a corner of the molecular view. When OFF, the picking calls themselves stop Hover Highlight ON Highlights the element under the pointer in the molecular view. Requires both GPU Picking and Hover Info

→ Picking and hover display

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Specifies, for each route, whether a loaded file is added to the current scene or opened in a new scene.

Item Default Description Drag and drop opens into Current scene Destination of files dragged and dropped onto the window. Current scene adds them to the scene of the active tab. New scene opens them in a dedicated tab File manager opens into Current scene Destination of files opened from the file manager (Finder / Explorer), specified on the command line, or passed from another instance while CueMol3 is running
  • File > Open File... and Open Recent always load into the current scene, regardless of this setting. When choosing from the menu you are looking at the scene, so a different destination would be more surprising than helpful.
  • Scene files (.qsc) are not affected by this setting and are opened by the usual rules.
  • Even when New scene is selected, if the active scene is empty (nothing has been loaded and nothing has been changed), the file is loaded into that scene.
  • Multiple files opened together share a single scene.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Checking for new releases and in-app updates. Only the macOS (Apple Silicon) version can be updated.

Item Default Description Check for Updates at Startup ON Checks for a new release after startup and notifies you if there is one. Manual checks are still possible when OFF Check for Updates — Shows the current version and status. It has Check Now / Release Page / Update buttons

For details, see Updating.

docs.text:
Settings for the external tools used to calculate electrostatic potentials (→ Configuring external tools).

Where settings are stored

The atom label and view navigation values are saved as a user style when the window is closed, and the others are saved as application settings. The only exception is API keys, which are encrypted and stored in the secure storage of the OS.

docs.title: Styles
docs.text: A style is a preset that specifies a set of Renderer properties at once. Because a Renderer has many properties, frequently used combinations can be given a name and applied together.

docs.title: Value precedence
docs.text:
A property value is determined from three layers. Lower layers take priority.

  1. Default value — the value fixed at the implementation level. It cannot be changed
  2. Style value — applying a style replaces the default value with the value defined in the style
  3. User-specified value — a value set directly in the inspector. Both the default value and the style value are ignored

For example, if a property's default value is 0.5, the style defines it as 0.1, and 1.0 is set in the inspector, the value actually used is 1.0.

When the display does not change after applying a style

The property has a user-specified value, which overrides the style value. Reset the property to its default value, and the style value takes effect. Each item in the inspector can be reset to its default value individually (→ Property inspector).

docs.title: Types of styles
docs.text:
Styles for shape and styles for Coloring are defined independently and can be applied separately.

Shape styles A set of properties related to the shape of a Renderer. Applied by right-clicking the Renderer in the scene tree. For example, ribbon has Default / Fancy1 / Round Coloring styles A set of properties related to coloring. Applied from the Color panel (→ Coloring)

In preparation

A list of the styles defined in the system will be added later.

docs.title: Working with styles
docs.text:
Styles can be applied, created and edited from the right-click menu of the scene tree. Style sets also appear as nodes in the scene tree, and can be read from and written to files (→ Side panels).

Problems have been reported with Edit style / Create style

This is under investigation → Development status and unimplemented features

docs.title: Animation
docs.text:
Animation changes how the scene looks over time. The timeline is shown in the Animation panel in the bottom panel, and an animation is built by arranging animation elements (anim obj) on it (→ Bottom panel).

The finished animation can be exported as a movie in the movie mode of the rendering window (→ Rendering window).

docs.title: List of types
docs.text:
The following elements can be added from the add menu of the Animation panel.

Add menu Class Description Simple spin SimpleSpin Rotates the view around a given axis Camera motion CamMotion Moves the view to a saved camera Show / Hide ShowHideAnim Fades a Renderer in / out Slide in / Slide out SlideInOutAnim Slides a Renderer in and out Mol morphing MolAnim Morphs between two structures by interpolation No operation — An element that does nothing. Used to leave a gap in time

docs.title: Common properties
docs.text:
Every type of element has the following settings. They are shown in the inspector when an element is selected in the scene tree or on the timeline.

Name Name of the element. It cannot be empty or the same as the name of another element Disabled When ON, the element is not played Relative to Reference for the start time. (absolute) means an absolute time from the beginning of the timeline; if another element is selected, the end time of that element is the reference. A setting that makes the references circular is rejected with a reason. If the element used as the reference is removed, (missing: name) is shown and the animation cannot be played until this is fixed Start time Start time. While dragging, the strip on the timeline follows, and releasing it counts as a single Undo (→ Entering times) Duration Duration. It is entered in the same way as Start time Quadric Degree of acceleration and deceleration of the change over time. Changing the value makes the motion start gently and end gently instead of proceeding at a constant speed

docs.title: MolAnim (structural change)
docs.text:
Interpolates between two different structures of the same molecule and displays the morph as an animation. It uses linear interpolation, which makes it well suited to animating local structural changes.

A morph pair (MorphMol) is created with Mol morphing animation... in the Tools menu (→ Morphing structural changes). The target molecule is converted to a MorphMol, and the structures that serve as frames are added (→ Making an animation and exporting a movie). Morphs in scenes created with CueMol2 can also be loaded and played or edited as they are.

In preparation

docs.title: Object
docs.text:
An Object holds data such as a molecular structure or an electron density map. An Object does not draw anything on screen by itself. Display is handled by the Renderers attached to the Object.

Each Object has a name that is unique within the scene. The name is set when the Object is created, for example by loading a file. If an Object with the same name already exists, an error occurs.

docs.title: List of types
docs.text:
Class Description How to create Main Renderers MolCoord Molecular structure (atomic coordinates) File > Open File... / Get PDB... ribbon and all other molecular Renderers DensityMap Scalar field such as an electron density map File > Open File... / Get PDB... contour / isosurf ElePotMap Electrostatic potential map Tools > APBS elepot calculation... / loading an OpenDX file contour / isosurf MolSurfObj Molecular surface (SES) Tools > Mol surface generation... / loading an MSMS or PLY file molsurf

DensityMap and ElePotMap are both kinds of scalar field (ScalarObject), and the Renderers for density maps can be attached to either.

docs.title: Working with Objects
docs.text:
• Create — load a file from the File menu, or use one of the generating tools in the Tools menu (→ File menu, Tools menu)
  • Save — File > Save File As... writes a single Object to a file. Only Objects that have a corresponding save format can be saved
  • Delete, rename and copy — right-click menu of the scene tree (→ Side panels)
  • Edit properties — property inspector (→ Property inspector)

docs.title: DensityMap (density map)
docs.text:
An Object that holds a three-dimensional scalar field such as an electron density map.

In preparation

The list of properties will be added later.

docs.title: Creating
docs.text: Load a density map file or a structure factor file with Open File... in the File menu, or fetch one with Get PDB... (→ File menu).

docs.title: Map type
docs.text:
Crystallographic maps (periodic) and cryo-EM maps (non-periodic) are handled separately. The type is detected automatically from the file header, and it determines the default display range (→ Region of contour / isosurf), the unit of the contour level (see below), and the default style applied to the Renderer (Default / Cryo-EM).

To change the detected type, specify Map type on the options screen shown when opening the file (for CCP4/MRC) as one of Auto (from header) / Crystallographic (periodic) / Cryo-EM (whole map, level of detail) (→ File menu). After loading, it can be changed with Map type in the Density map section of the Properties tab of the property inspector. The detection result is shown in Effective kind in the same section. When Map type is changed, the contour / isosurf styles are also switched between Default and Cryo-EM (a Renderer that you have set to a different style is left unchanged).

The contour level is held in a unit that depends on the map type. For crystallographic maps it is σ (the unit in which the standard deviation of the map is 1; default 1.1), and for cryo-EM maps it is the top percentage of grid point values to be enclosed (default: top 1 %). Level in the Density map panel accepts either this unit or an absolute value (→ Side panels).

The ORIGIN of MRC files is also read, so a map whose origin is not 0 overlaps correctly with a model fitted to it.

docs.title: Supported Renderers
docs.text:
contour / isosurf / gpu_mapmesh

The display range and contour level can also be adjusted from the Density map panel (→ Side panels).

docs.title: MolSurfObj (molecular surface)
docs.text:
An Object that holds the polygon data of the solvent-excluded surface (SES) of a molecule.

In preparation

This page is only a skeleton. The list of properties will be added later.

docs.title: Creating
docs.text:
Generate it from a molecule with Mol surface generation... in the Tools menu, or load an MSMS surface file (.face / .vert) or a PLY file (→ Generating a molecular surface).

After generation, the surface can be cut by a plane with Tools > Mol surface cutter... (→ Cutting a molecular surface), and regenerated from the right-click menu of the scene tree.

docs.title: Generation algorithm (Algorithm)
docs.text:
The generation and regeneration dialogs let you choose how the SES is calculated.

Algorithm Description Auto Uses MeshMS (default) MeshMS A new implementation that builds the SES mesh analytically BALL The implementation CueMol has used so far

Both are built into the distributed builds. With Auto, if MeshMS fails on the input, it automatically falls back to BALL, so a surface is always generated.

Even with the same density and probe radius, the meshes produced by the two algorithms do not match. MeshMS applies a single target edge length to the whole surface and merges vertices before computing normals, so the result is generally smoother. The density scale is calibrated to BALL, so the same density value gives a comparable level of detail.

Each time a surface is generated, one line is written to the log in the Output panel showing which algorithm ran, the elapsed time, and the numbers of vertices and faces.

Regeneration that changes only the density is faster

On regeneration, the results of the density-independent part of the calculation are cached. If you change only the density in the Regenerate dialog, only the meshing is redone. The cache is invalidated when any of the coordinates, the selection, or the atomic radii change, so an outdated surface is never reused.

Existing scenes look the same

The scene file format has not changed, so saved scenes are loaded as before. The surface changes only when it is regenerated.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
A plugin is a self-contained feature that can be turned on and off. Experimental features and features used by only a few people are provided this way. Plugins are toggled in Settings > Plugins > Installed (→ Settings).

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Switchable plugins
docs.text:
Plugin Description Default What is added when enabled AI Agent A chat panel that builds a scene from instructions written in text. It uses OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google (Gemini) models; you provide your own API key OFF The AI Agent view in the activity bar and the Plugins > AI Agent page in Settings (→ AI Agent) MD Tools Opens and plays MD simulation trajectories (topology + DCD / XTC / TRR) OFF File > Open MD Trajectory... and the Trajectory tab in the bottom panel Console A command line that runs CueMol operations as commands. The PyMOL compatibility mode is also available ON The Console tab at the left end of the bottom panel, CLI in the status bar, and the Plugins > Console page in Settings (→ Console) MCP Server Allows AI clients on the same computer (such as Claude Code) to operate CueMol3 via MCP OFF MCP in the status bar and the Plugins > MCP Server page in Settings (→ MCP Server) Component Catalog A catalog of UI components. An internal tool for developing and reviewing the CueMol3 UI OFF The Component Catalog view in the activity bar

MD Tools, Console, and MCP Server are experimental features; their descriptions begin with Experimental.

Always-on features are not listed

Get PDB (File > Get PDB... and the toolbar button) and Sequence Panel (the Sequence tab in the bottom panel) are also plugins internally, but they cannot be toggled, so they do not appear in the Installed list. They take the form of plugins only to keep each feature in one place; they are not meant to be removable.

docs.title: How settings are saved
docs.text: Only the plugins you have toggled yourself are recorded. A plugin you have never touched follows the default each time. As a result, if a default changes in a later version, the change reaches environments where you have not touched the setting.

docs.title: MD trajectories are now disabled by default
docs.text:
In versions before 2.3.15.530, File > Open MD Trajectory... and the Trajectory tab in the bottom panel were always shown. They are now part of the MD Tools plugin, which is disabled by default. To use them, enable MD Tools in Settings > Plugins > Installed.

Even when disabled, a Trajectory already in the scene is drawn as before, and is also loaded from scene files (.qsc). Only the GUI is disabled. If the plugin is disabled during playback, the tab closes and playback stops.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: • On macOS, the menu items added by plugins may not appear in the menu bar for a short time right after launch.

docs.title: AI Agent
docs.text:
A chat panel in which a model builds a scene by calling CueMol3 operations in sequence, based on a text description of the state you want to see. This plugin is disabled by default, and an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google (Gemini) is required to use it (usage costs are borne by the user).

In preparation

This page is a skeleton. How to write instructions and a list of what the agent can do will be added later.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Enabling the plugin
docs.text: Enable AI Agent in Settings > Plugins > Installed (→ Plugins). Once enabled, an AI Agent icon is added to the activity bar. The panel can be opened only from this activity view (not from a menu or a command).

docs.title: Model and API key settings
docs.text:
The settings are in Settings > Plugins > AI Agent (this page appears when the plugin is enabled).

Item Default Description Model openai:gpt-5.6 The model to use, in the form provider:model-name. Choose from the candidates, or enter an ID available to your account directly. The provider part (openai / anthropic / google) determines which of the API keys below is used Reasoning effort low How long the model thinks before answering. Higher values are slower and cost more Pressing Enter start a new line What happens when Enter is pressed in the message box. With start a new line, messages are sent with Cmd+Enter / Ctrl+Enter. Choosing send the message reverses this OpenAI API key (not set) Key used for openai: models Anthropic API key (not set) Key used for anthropic: models Google AI API key (not set) Key used for google: models (a Gemini API key issued in Google AI Studio)

Where API keys are stored

API keys are encrypted and stored in the OS secure storage (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows, the desktop keyring on Linux), and are not written to the settings file in plain text. If no stored key exists, the environment variables OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY are used.

Leaving a field empty does not delete a stored key. To delete it, press Clear. In environments where the OS cannot encrypt keys, keys are not stored and you are directed to use environment variables.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
• Type an instruction such as "Load 1CRN and show it as a cartoon" in the input box and send it. By default, Enter inserts a line break and Cmd+Enter / Ctrl+Enter sends (this can be swapped with Pressing Enter above).
  • While a task is running, Send changes to Stop, which stops it midway.
  • The Model at the top of the panel switches the model to use. It is the same setting as Model in Settings. The list shows only the models that can be used with the saved keys, among the providers whose API key is saved, and is updated immediately when a key is saved or cleared. The model cannot be switched while a task is running.
  • Up / Down recall previously sent instructions.
  • One instruction is grouped into one Undo. A single Cmd+Z undoes all the changes made by that instruction. The operations performed by an instruction are recorded in the History panel of the Actions view.
  • Clear chat at the top right of the panel clears the conversation.

docs.title: What it can do
docs.text: The model can view the current view as an image (capture_view) and proceeds while checking the results of its own operations. That image is shown as a reduced thumbnail in the tool row of the log. Only the latest image is kept in the conversation.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Only one scene is targeted. Operations apply to the scene that was active when the instruction started. Even if you instruct "in a new scene", the data is loaded into the current scene.
  • Scene files (.qsc) cannot be opened. Open them with File > Open.
  • Changes you make by hand while a task is running are included in the Undo of that instruction.
  • While a Console command or an MCP Server call is running, instructions you send are not executed (conversely, while an instruction is running, Console and MCP Server operations are rejected).
  • The conversation is lost when the application is quit.
  • The behavior when the provider is switched in the middle of a conversation has not been verified.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Plugins / Console / MCP Server
  • Settings reference
  • Side panels

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text:
A plugin that lets an AI client running on the same computer (Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity, etc.) operate CueMol3 through MCP (Model Context Protocol). It is disabled by default.

The client can call the same operations as the Console commands as tools. No API key is needed on the CueMol3 side; model usage follows the client's own settings.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Enabling it
docs.text:
Enable MCP Server in Settings > Plugins > Installed (see Plugins). Once enabled, MCP appears at the right end of the status bar and the server starts accepting connections.

The settings are in Settings > Plugins > MCP Server.

Item Default Description Accept connections ON Accepts connections. Turning it OFF closes the port (MCP stays in the status bar, and you can turn it back ON from there) Port 27182 The port to listen on (1024-65535). The value is applied when you press Enter or move focus away (Esc restores the original value). A value out of range shows an error and is not applied. The listening state is shown below the field, and when the value is not the default you can restore it with Reset to 27182. After changing it, register the client again

docs.title: MCP in the status bar
docs.text:
MCP in the status bar shows the state of the server. While a tool is running, it shows MCP: <tool name>.

State Meaning Off Not accepting connections Starting Opening the port Ready Waiting for connections from a client Running Running a tool Error The server could not be started (for example, the port is in use by another program)

The popover that opens when you click it contains the following.

  • A toggle switch at the top (the same setting as Accept connections) and a gear button that opens the settings page
  • Status - the state, the address being listened on (127.0.0.1:<port>), and the name of the running tool
  • Set up... under Clients - opens the dialog for registering a client
  • Regenerate under Token - regenerates the token used for connections. Clients registered with the old token must be registered again

docs.title: Registering a client
docs.text:
In the Connect a client dialog opened with Set up..., choose the client type (Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Other) to see the command or the configuration file entry used for registration. Use what you copy with Copy.

  • While displayed, the token is hidden as <token>; the actual value is filled in when you copy with Copy.
  • For Claude Code, run the displayed command (claude mcp add --transport http cuemol ...) in a terminal.
  • For Codex, add it to ~/.codex/config.toml; for Antigravity, add it to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json. The Codex configuration includes tool_timeout_sec so that long-running renders are not cut off midway.
  • For Other, the URL (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp) and the header to send (Authorization: Bearer <token>) are shown. Any MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP and can send headers will work.

When you change the token or the port, register the client again.

docs.title: What it can do
docs.text:
• Every operation corresponding to a Console command can be called as a tool. There is also capture_view, which returns the current view as an image.
  • You can list, create, switch and close scenes (list_scenes / create_scene / switch_scene / close_scene). close_scene does not close a scene with unsaved changes (specify discardChanges to discard the changes and close it). You can also save with save_scene and open a .qsc file.
  • One tool call is grouped into one Undo step (the Undo name is MCP: <tool name>). Calls are recorded in the History panel of the Actions view.
  • While an AI Agent instruction or a Console command is running, tool calls are refused. If the client cancels a call, the running operation stops as well.
  • Errors are returned in a form the client can read ({ok: false, error}).

Argument names changed in 2.4.0.546

Coloring and Paint operations (add_paint / set_paint / clear_paint / set_default_color / set_renderer_coloring, etc.) take nodeId and nodeType (renderer or object) instead of rendId. The argument molId, which refers to an Object, is now objId (fromMolId of add_morph_frame is now fromObjId).

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The server listens only on 127.0.0.1 (inside this computer).
  • A token is required to connect. The token is stored in CueMol3's user data folder as a file readable only by the user.
  • Requests from web pages are rejected.
  • While listening, the port and token are written to ~/.cuemol/local-api.json (a file readable only by the user). tritium_cli also uses the same server.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Console / AI Agent
  • Plugins / Settings

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
The Console is a command line for operating CueMol with commands. It is a plugin that is enabled by default and is used from the Console tab of the bottom panel. tritium_cli, which runs the same commands from a terminal, is also bundled (→ tritium_cli).

There are two command modes, switched in the panel.

Mode Prompt Description native mode (default) CueMol> Commands for operating CueMol itself. Selections are written with CueMol's selection expressions. Described on this page PyMOL compatibility mode PyM> PyMOL-compatible commands (→ PyMOL compatibility mode)

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Enabling the plugin
docs.text:
Because it is enabled by default, the Console tab is the first tab of the bottom panel. This tab stays in front until another tab is selected. To stop using it, disable Console in Settings > Plugins > Installed (→ Plugins).

Renamed from PyM Console

The PyM Console plugin up to 2.3.20.539 became Console in 2.3.21.544. If you had disabled PyM Console, Console is enabled anyway, so disable it again if you do not use it. The input history of the PyMOL compatibility mode is carried over.

docs.title: Switching modes
docs.text:
• Use CueMol | PyMOL at the left end of the toolbar. CueMol is the native mode.
  • Typing just native or pymol on a line and running it also switches the mode.
  • The selected mode is remembered, and the next launch starts in that mode.
  • The input history is separate for each mode.

docs.title: Input and completion
docs.text:
Action Behavior Enter Runs the command Shift+Enter Inserts a line break Tab Completes the part before the cursor. The part after the cursor is left as is. When there are multiple candidates, a list is shown just above the prompt. Pressing it again while the list is shown opens a menu for choosing a candidate Up / Down Steps through the input history (when the cursor is on the first / last line)
  • In the candidate menu, Tab / Shift+Tab / the arrow keys move between candidates, and Enter confirms the choice (the command is not run). Esc restores the input as it was before Tab was pressed. Any other key confirms the selected candidate and is then typed. A candidate can also be confirmed by clicking it.
  • Pressing Tab on a word containing * or ? expands it to all matches.
  • In file name completion, names starting with . become candidates only when . is typed. If nothing matches, the search is retried without distinguishing upper and lower case. For cd, only directories are candidates.
  • In native mode, Tab completes command names, help topics, argument values (choices and true / false), Object and Renderer names, named selections, color names, Renderer types, property paths, the name= of arguments not yet specified, and file paths (only for arguments that take a path).
  • One execution is grouped into one Undo.
  • Clear on the toolbar clears the log area, and Help runs help for the current mode.
  • While a command is running, Stop is shown next to "Running...". Pressing it stops before the next command. What has been executed up to that point remains.

docs.title: Writing native-mode commands
docs.text:
zoom 1crn, chain A and resid 10:20
set 1crn/cartoon1.width, 2
create_renderer 1crn, ballstick, name=bs1
  • Write arguments after the command name, separated by commas. An argument can also be given by name in the form name=value.
  • Command names take the form "verb_target" (list_cameras / add_paint, etc.). Commands that are just a noun, such as props / view / slab, display their contents when typed without a value and set it when given a value.
  • An Object is specified by name (1crn), and a Renderer by ObjectName/RendererName (1crn/cartoon1). A Renderer name alone is also accepted if it is unique in the scene. Any element can be specified by uid, such as #12. If a name is ambiguous, the command is not run and the candidate uids are displayed.
  • A property follows the element after a . (1crn/cartoon1.width, view.centerMark). Scene properties are specified by name only.
  • help shows the list of topics, help <topic> shows the list of commands in that topic, and help <command> or <command> ? shows the syntax and the argument table of that command. help syntax explains how to write commands.

docs.title: Multiple targets and wildcards
docs.text:
Object, Renderer and property paths, and the paths of files to load, can be listed multiple times separated by spaces. The wildcards * and ? can also be used.

hide 1crn 2abc/cartoon1
set */simple1.width, 0.7
load *.pdb ~/pdb/1c*.pdb
get_prop *.visible
  • The command is run once for each target. A target that fails produces a warning, and the remaining targets are still run. A pattern that matches nothing produces a no matches found: <pattern> warning.
  • Even when multiple targets are listed, the whole line is grouped into one Undo.
  • A name containing a space is enclosed in quotation marks ("my mol"), or the space is preceded by \ (my\ mol). A literal * is written \*.
  • props (list_node_props) and get (get_prop) display their results in a table. With multiple targets, the results are combined into one table.

Names containing spaces need quotation marks

Up to 2.3.21.544, Object names, Renderer names and paths containing spaces could be written without quotation marks. From 2.4.0.546, spaces are read as separators.

docs.title: Supported commands
docs.text: The native-mode commands are collected by help topic in the Console command list.

docs.title: Scripts and logs
docs.text:
• run file or @file runs a text file with one command per line. The whole script is grouped into one Undo.
  • run file.qax (or @file.qax) replays a file of recorded operations (qax). When it is the only thing on the line, each recorded operation becomes one Undo, and replay stops at an operation that fails. When run from inside a script, it is included in the Undo of the whole script (→ Recording and replaying operations).
  • open_log opens a file (log.qax by default), and from then on the operations performed by subsequent executions are recorded as qax. Executions that did not change the scene are not recorded. A statement written with log is included as a note. close_log ends the recording.
  • list_actions displays each Undo step and the operations performed in it, oldest first. export_actions file[, first[, last]] writes that range to a qax file.
  • A .pml file (a PyMOL script) cannot be run in native mode. Switch to PyMOL compatibility mode to run it.

docs.title: Using from a terminal (tritium_cli)
docs.text: tritium_cli is a client that runs Console commands from a terminal. It is bundled with CueMol3. For usage, connection and adding it to PATH, see tritium_cli.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Scene commands (create_scene / switch_scene / close_scene) and quit / exit cannot be used inside a script.
  • Python is not accepted. .py / .pym scripts and lines starting with / are rejected.
  • Commands cannot be run while an AI Agent instruction or an MCP Server call is being executed.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Console command list / tritium_cli
  • PyMOL compatibility mode / MCP Server / AI Agent
  • Plugins / Settings reference
  • Selection expression syntax
  • Recording and replaying operations
  • Bottom panel

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: tritium_cli
docs.text: tritium_cli is a client that runs Console commands from a terminal. It is bundled with CueMol3 and can also be installed on its own from npm (Install from npm). Commands are run on the active tab of the running CueMol3.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
tritium_cli [--dialect native|pymol] [--echo] [--no-launch] [-c COMMANDS | SCRIPT]
  • Started without arguments, it enters interactive mode. The prompt is CueMol <directory> ❯ (pymol <directory> ❯ in PyMOL compatibility mode). Tab completes, Ctrl+C stops the running command, native / pymol switches the mode, and exit or Ctrl+D quits. quit quits CueMol3 first and then tritium_cli as well.
  • Tab completion works the same as in the panel, and a second Tab opens the candidate menu. The output of help is wrapped to the terminal width (it is printed as Markdown when piped).
  • Passing commands with -c, or a script file as the argument, runs them and exits. Passing a .qax file replays the recorded operations. Input can also be piped in. The exit status is 1 on failure.
  • --echo prints each command before its output as it is run.
  • Relative paths are resolved against the directory where tritium_cli was run.
  • Commands that were run are also shown in the Console tab of CueMol3 with a [cli] prefix.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
If CueMol3 is not running, tritium_cli launches it and waits (use --no-launch to suppress this). In this case, command-line access is allowed for that run only.

A tritium_cli installed from npm looks for an installed CueMol3 and launches it. It searches the standard install locations (/Applications etc. on macOS, the installer's install location on Windows, the .deb install location on Linux). If CueMol3 is elsewhere (an AppImage, for example), set the environment variable CUEMOL3_APP to the path of the app. If CueMol3 cannot be found, tritium_cli shows the download location and exits.

To connect to a CueMol3 that is already running, turn Command line access ON in Settings > Plugins > Console (OFF by default). The port and token to connect to are read from ~/.cuemol/local-api.json.

docs.title: Adding to PATH
docs.text:
The path of the bundled tritium_cli is shown in Command line tool under Settings > Plugins > Console (it can be copied with Copy).

OS Method macOS Link the displayed path into a directory on PATH (ln -s "<path>" ~/.local/bin/tritium_cli) Windows Add the directory containing the displayed tritium_cli.cmd to PATH Linux (.deb) Installed at /usr/bin/tritium_cli Linux (AppImage) Not available. To use tritium_cli, install the .deb

docs.title: Install from npm
docs.text:
With Node.js (18 or later), tritium_cli alone can be installed from npm. The tritium_cli command is added to PATH.

npm install -g @cuemol/tritium-cli

A tritium_cli installed from npm is updated separately from CueMol3. If the version of the communication protocol between it and CueMol3 does not match, a warning to update the older one is shown when interactive mode starts (some commands may not work).

Note

The npm version has been verified only in combination with an installed CueMol3 on macOS.

docs.title: CLI in the status bar
docs.text: While Console is enabled, CLI is shown on the right side of the status bar. Clicking it shows the state of the command-line connection (Off / Starting / Ready / Running / Error), the same toggle switch as Command line access, and a button to copy the tritium_cli path (Copy path).

  • Recording and replaying operations / Settings

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.1.547

and images (files) fetch_pdb (fetch) / fetch_url / load_file (load) / load_pdb / load_msms / load_namd / load_amber / save_scene (save) / save_object (write) / export_scene / export_image / docs.title: Notes on individual commands
docs.text:
• load detects the format and loads the file in the same way as File > Open. A .qsc file is opened as a scene. Format-specific commands such as load_pdb accept the options used when opening a file as named arguments (load_pdb f.pdb, build2ndry=false).
  • fetch retrieves the file in mmCIF format by default.
  • render runs rendering (GI or NPR). It can be stopped with Stop while running.
  • calc_elepot performs the same processing as the electrostatic potential calculation in the Tools menu and uses the APBS path set in Settings. cut_surface cuts a molecular surface, and add_morph_frame and the like perform the same processing as the tool for creating morphing animations.
  • superpose superposes with US-align by default (algo can also select SSM / LSQ). pivot specifies the atom that US-align uses to represent each residue (auto / CA / C3' / C4' / P) (→ Superposing molecules).
  • animate plays, pauses and stops an animation and moves to a given time.
  • The scene commands (create_scene / switch_scene / close_scene) open, close and switch tabs. close_scene does not close a scene with unsaved changes. Add discardChanges=true to discard the changes and close it.
  • quit exits CueMol3. If there are unsaved changes, a confirmation is shown. quit force=true (or quit -f) exits without confirmation. exit is the same as quit.
