docs.title: PyMOL compatibility mode (Console)
docs.text:
The PyMOL compatibility mode of Console interprets a subset of the PyMOL command language. Commands you used in PyMOL, such as fetch 1crn or bg_color white, can be typed as they are. Up to 2.3.20.539 this was a separate plugin called PyM Console.

Full compatibility with PyMOL is not a goal. The aim is that commands you already know work. Command parsing and Tab completion are ported from the PyMOL implementation, and the error messages are the same.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Enabling it
docs.text: The Console plugin is enabled by default, and the Console tab is the first tab of the bottom panel (→ Plugins). Choose PyMOL with the switch at the left end of the toolbar, or type just pymol on a line and run it, to enter PyMOL compatibility mode (→ Switching modes).

docs.title: Input and completion
docs.text:
The prompt is PyM>.

Action Behavior Enter Runs the command Shift+Enter Inserts a line break Tab Completes the part before the cursor; the part after the cursor is left as it is. When there are multiple candidates, a list is shown just above the prompt. Pressing the key again while the list is shown opens a menu for choosing a candidate (→ Input and completion) Up / Down Browse the input history (separate from the history of native mode)
  • The behavior of Tab follows PyMOL. It does not complete when the command name is already settled, and falls back to file name expansion when nothing matches.
  • Confirming a Japanese input conversion with Enter does not run the command.
  • One run is grouped into one Undo step.
  • Clear on the toolbar clears the log area, and Help shows the list of PyMOL compatibility mode commands.
  • While a command is running, Stop appears next to "Running...". Pressing it stops before the next command and cancels a download in progress. Whatever has already been executed is kept.

docs.title: Scripts and logs
docs.text:
• @file.pml or run file.pml runs a .pml script. A script can call another script. The whole script is grouped into one Undo step.
  • log_open opens a file (log.pml by default), and the commands typed at the prompt afterwards are recorded. log_close ends the recording. The recorded file can be re-run as it is with @. Commands run from a script are not recorded.
  • A file of operations recorded in native mode (.qax) cannot be run in PyMOL compatibility mode. Switch to native mode to run it (→ Recording and replaying operations).

docs.title: Supported commands
docs.text:
The arguments of each command can be checked with help <command>.

Category Commands Loading and saving load / fetch / save / png / ray / run Object delete / set_name / enable / disable / get_names / get_chains Selection select / indicate / deselect / count_atoms Display show / hide / as (show_as) / color / spectrum / set_color / bg_color / label Map isomesh / isosurface / isolevel Measurement distance / angle / dihedral Superposition align / super / pair_fit View zoom / center / orient / reset / turn / move / view / get_view / set_view / refresh Animation mplay / mstop / rewind / frame / count_states Settings set / get / unset Scripts and logs @ / run / log_open / log_close / log Others undo / redo / cd / pwd / ls / help / quit / exit
  • load accepts structure and map files, http(s):// URLs, .qsc / .pse scenes, and .pml scripts. A .qsc is opened in a new tab unless the current scene is new and empty.
  • fetch downloads from RCSB. type=pdb1 and similar fetch biological assemblies, and type=2fofc / type=fofc fetch density maps. Writing 1abcA or 1abc_A keeps only that chain.
  • save decides the format by the extension. Molecules (optionally only the selected part) are saved as .pdb / .sdf / .mol / .pqr, scenes as .qsc, and views as .png / .pov / .stl.
  • ray draws the view with rendering (GI). It can be stopped with Stop while running, and the following png saves that image (if the view or scene was changed in the meantime, the normal view is saved). png with ray=1 renders and saves on the spot.
  • align / super / pair_fit display the RMSD. Both align and super superpose with US-align and do not perform a sequence alignment. Along with the RMSD, the number of aligned residues and the TM-score are also displayed. pair_fit is a least-squares superposition that pairs atoms in order.
  • get_view / set_view use the same 18-number format as PyMOL.
  • label accepts PyMOL expressions (such as "%s%s" % (resn, resi)).
  • With cutoff or mode, distance lists the contacts between two selections and labels them.
  • PyMOL keyword and positional arguments such as quiet=1 and async=0 are also accepted. Arguments that have no effect produce a warning and are ignored.
  • PyMOL settings that have an equivalent quantity in CueMol, such as stick_radius / transparency / line_width / solvent_radius / label_size / label_color, are mapped to the corresponding properties. Values set before show also apply to what is displayed afterwards.
  • quit / exit quit CueMol3. If there are unsaved changes, a confirmation is shown. quit force=true (or quit -f) quits without confirmation.

docs.title: Translation of selection expressions
docs.text: A PyMOL selection expression is translated into a CueMol selection expression before it is run (it is not passed through as it is). The operator precedence is the same in both, but some symbols have different meanings. Object names can also be used inside a selection expression (such as 1abc and chain A).

docs.title: Corresponding terms
docs.text:
Kind PyMOL CueMol Terms that take a value name (n.) / elem (e. / element / symbol) / resn (r. / resname) / chain (c.) / alt (altloc) Terms with the same name resi (i. / resid / resv) resi (ranges: see below) id aid ss H / ss S / ss L helix / sheet / coil Comparison b / q with < / > / = (==) bfac / occ Macros all / * / none * / none protein (polymer.protein) / nucleic (polymer.nucleic) / polymer protein / nucleic / (protein) or (nucleic) water / solvent water hydro / hydrogens hydrogen hetatm / organic ligand backbone / sidechain / guide An expression listing the backbone atom names / its negation / (protein) and (name CA) Operators and (&) / or (\|) / not (!) / byres (br.) / around (a.) / expand (x.) The same operators Forms taking two selections s1 within D of s2 (w.) (s1) and ((s2) expand D) s1 near_to D of s2 (nto.) (s1) and ((s2) around D) s1 beyond D of s2 (be.) (s1) and not ((s2) expand D)
  • hetatm is a PDB record type, but CueMol does not keep it, so it is replaced with ligand (anything that is not protein, nucleic acid, or water). Different atoms are selected for modified residues.
  • backbone is N / CA / C / O / OXT for proteins, and P / OP1 / OP2 / O5* / C5* / C4* / C3* / O3* for nucleic acids.

docs.title: + and -
docs.text:
A selection expression is split into terms by spaces and parentheses, and the meaning of + and - depends on whether they stand alone as a term.

Notation Meaning CueMol name CA+CB (+ inside a term) List of values name CA,CB resi 1-10 (- inside a term) Range of residue numbers resi 1:10 resi -5--1 Range of negative residue numbers resi -5:-1 chain A + chain B (standalone +) Union (or) (chain A) or (chain B) protein - chain A (standalone -) Difference (protein) and not (chain A)

docs.title: Object names and named selections
docs.text:
• A selection expression is translated for each molecule. An Object name is replaced with all in that molecule and with none in the other molecules. When a selection expression contains an Object name, only that molecule is targeted.
  • A term that is not an Object name is treated as a CueMol named selection. Writing %name has the same effect.

docs.title: What cannot be translated
docs.text:
The following terms cause an error that names them.

Kind Terms Operators in / like / neighbor (nbr.) / extend / first / last / bound_to / byobject / bysegi / bychain / bycalpha / bymolecule / gap Properties segi (s.) / index (use id instead) / model (m.; use an Object name instead) / x / y / z / flag (f) / rep / color / pepseq (ps) / text_type / numeric_type / stereo / rank / partial_charge / formal_charge Macros inorganic / metals / donors / acceptors / visible / enabled / bonded / masked / protected / center / origin Comparison <= / >= / != (CueMol comparisons are only < / > / =) Notation Slash notation such as /1abc//A/10/CA (write chain A and resi 10 and name CA), within without a left-hand selection, around without a distance, within without of

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Raw Python is not accepted. Python scripts (.py / .pym) are rejected with a message that names them.
  • volume and isodot are not implemented.
  • A selection specification that is not supported is rejected with the reason and the offending term named, instead of silently selecting different atoms.
  • Measurements (distance / angle / dihedral) produce one label per command. A selection is treated as its single centroid. Measurement is possible only within one molecule (when distance lists contacts, it can also measure between two molecules).
  • show / hide do not affect Renderers created in the GUI. These commands operate only on Renderers whose names start with pym:.
  • zoom / center / orient and map clipping work on one molecule.
  • Not supported: MD trajectory commands (load_traj / intra_fit / smooth, etc.), commands that depend on picking (edit / drag, etc.), h_add / cealign, and so on. Saving to .cif and .pse is not possible.

docs.title: Renderer
docs.text:
A Renderer determines how the data of an Object is drawn. Multiple Renderers can be attached to a single Object, for example ribbon for the main chain and ballstick for the active site.

Renderers are created by right-clicking an Object row or a Renderer group row in the scene tree and choosing New Renderer (→ Side panels). Settings are edited in the property inspector (→ Property inspector).

docs.title: List of types
docs.text:
Type Target Object Description New Renderer simple Molecule Lightest display; draws bonds as lines ○ trace Molecule Connects the main-chain pivot atoms (Cα, etc.) with lines ○ tracestick Molecule A trace drawn with spheres at the main-chain pivot atoms and cylinders between them ○ spline Molecule Draws the main chain as a smoothed curve ○ ballstick Molecule Draws atoms as spheres and bonds as cylinders ○ cpk Molecule Space-filling model drawn with spheres of van der Waals radii ○ anisou Molecule Draws anisotropic temperature factors as ellipsoids (ORTEP style) ○ tube Molecule Draws the main chain as a smooth tube ○ ribbon Molecule Ribbon / plate / tube display according to secondary structure ○ cartoon Molecule Schematic secondary-structure display with helices drawn as cylinders ○ nucl Molecule Nucleic acid main-chain tube + base display ○ atomintr Molecule Displays distances, angles and interactions between atoms ○ disorder Molecule Displays disordered regions, bridging the gaps with dotted lines ○ dsurface Molecule Molecular surface computed directly from the molecule ○ dsurf2 Molecule Molecular surface using a distance field — molsurf Molecular surface Draws an already generated molecular surface Object ○ contour Density map Contour mesh display ○ isosurf Density map Isosurface display ○ gpu_mapmesh Density map GPU implementation of the contour mesh —

Types with "—" in the New Renderer column do not appear in the list in the New Renderer dialog.

  • atomintr is created automatically when you use the measurement tools in the tool palette (Distance / Angle / Torsion) or Interaction... in the Tools menu
  • atomintr and disorder do not appear in the Renderer type list shown when opening a file. Right after loading there is nothing for them to draw (no measurements have been created yet, and there is no main-chain Renderer for disorder to follow). Create them with New Renderer after the Object has been added to the scene
  • gpu_mapmesh was removed from the choices for new Renderers because its line width cannot be changed and it is slower than contour. Those contained in existing scenes are displayed as before, and their settings can still be changed
  • dsurf2 has been merged into dsurface. Distance-field meshes are chosen with Algorithm in dsurface. Those contained in existing scenes are loaded as dsurface (→ dsurf2)

Internal Renderers (selection highlight, atom labels, symmetry mates, unit cell, etc.) are also not shown in the list. Of these, the atom label Renderer is described in namelabel.

docs.title: Property structure
docs.text:
Renderer properties are divided into those common to all types and those specific to each type.

  • Common properties — name, selection, show / hide, material, opacity, and edge lines (edge lines only for Renderers that have faces) → Common Renderer properties
  • Type-specific properties — see the page for each Renderer

Properties that do not appear in the Properties tab of the inspector can be edited in the Generic tab.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
The New Renderer dialog also offers presets, which create several Renderers at once. Choosing a preset creates a set of Renderers, each assigned its target by a selection expression, as a single group.

Preset Composition Default preset 1 ribbon (protein) + nucl (nucleic acid) + ballstick (everything else) Default preset 2 cartoon (protein) + nucl (nucleic acid) + ballstick (everything else) Simple preset 1 trace (protein and nucleic acid) + simple (everything else)

docs.title: cartoon
docs.text:
A Renderer dedicated to proteins. It draws helices as cylinders, sheets as plates, and coils as tubes. Target Object: molecule (MolCoord). The implementation class is Ribbon2Renderer.

The display is similar to ribbon. By default, however, ribbon passes through the Cα atoms everywhere except in β sheets, whereas cartoon is smoothed so that it emphasizes only the fold of the molecule (you can also force it to pass through them by setting Smoothing or Anchor, described below).

The figures below show cartoon (left) and ribbon (right) for the same molecule with default parameter values.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties. The meaning of the cross-section settings (Section type / Section width / Tuber / Sharpness) is the same as in ribbon.

docs.title: Cartoon
docs.text: Axial detail Number of polygon subdivisions along the chain Smooth color Whether to color the transition between adjacent residues as a gradient Pivot atom name Name of the atom that the backbone display passes through (default: CA) Start cap / End cap Shape of the ends (sphere / flat / none) Anchor selection Selection expression for residues that should pass through their Cα as closely as possible. When you show side chains on a cartoon display, the backbone display does not pass through the Cα positions, so the side chains appear to float in the air. This setting helps in that case. The figures below show the case where Coil Smoothing = -1 (default) and the residue A.76.* at the tip of a loop is specified in Anchor selection It works well for about one residue in a loop or sheet, but with many residues it ends up the same as lowering Smoothing, so to make the display pass through many Cα atoms it is better to adjust Smoothing Anchor weight Strength with which the residues specified in Anchor selection are pulled toward their Cα

docs.title: Helix
docs.text:
Smoothing

Specifies the smoothness of the helix cylinder as a real number. The default is 3.0, which is fairly straight.

  • Decreasing it brings the cylinder closer to a helix that follows the Cα atoms
  • Increasing it makes the cylinder almost straight

The figures below show 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0 from the left At 4 and above the cylinder is almost straight and there is little difference. At 1 and below it takes on a twisted, wrung-out shape. Negative and fractional values can also be specified, but the reasonable range is about 2 to 4

Width mode By default the cylinder has a constant thickness equal to the average. If you switch this, the thickness varies according to how far the Cα atoms deviate from the center line of the cylinder Width smooth Effective only when Width mode is set to variable; specifies the smoothness of the cylinder thickness. The larger the value, the smoother it is. The default is 5.0, which is almost the same as a constant thickness; lowering it makes the thickness variation appear. The figures below show 0.0, 1.0, and 2.0 (the others are fixed at variable width, Smoothing = 3.0) The appearance also changes considerably with the value of Smoothing Add width Depending on the structure, the coil may stick out at the junction between a helix cylinder and a coil. Increasing this value enlarges the cylinder radius by that amount, so you can adjust it to hide the coil. The figures below show 0.0 and 0.5 The default is the same as the coil thickness of 0.2, which hides it in most cases. You can also deliberately specify a negative value to get a thin cylinder display Extend Amount by which the helix segment is extended forward and backward

docs.title: Sheet
docs.text: Smoothing Smoothness of the sheet display. The default is 3.0, a setting that captures the curvature of the sheet while making it reasonably straight. The figures below show -5.0, 0.0, and 3.0. At -2 and below it passes roughly through the Cα atoms, and at 3 and above it becomes almost straight Width smooth Smoothness of the change in sheet width

docs.title: Coil
docs.text: Smoothing Smoothness of the coil display. The default is -1.0, a setting that captures the curvature of the coil while giving a clean appearance. The figures below show -5.0, -2.0, -1.0, and 0.0. At -2 and below it passes roughly through the Cα atoms, and at 0 and above it may deviate too far from the actual Cα positions

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• If you display only part of a secondary structure element with a selection expression, it may not be drawn as intended. When showing a partial display, adjust the selection so that it breaks at a coil segment.

About detailed cross-section settings

Some properties of the cross-section (TubeSection) and the junction (JctTable) are edited not on the Properties tab but on the Generic tab (→ Property inspector).

docs.title: contour (contour mesh)
docs.text:
A Renderer that draws a scalar field such as an electron density map as a contour mesh. Target Objects: density map (DensityMap), electrostatic potential map (ElePotMap).

In preparation

This page is only a skeleton. Details of each property will be added later.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties.

docs.title: Contour
docs.text:
Map kind The kind of this map (Crystallographic / Cryo-EM). Read-only; it shows the detected Map type of the DensityMap Region The range to display. Auto (default) becomes Box around center for crystallographic maps and Full map for cryo-EM maps. Box around center draws only the area around the view center and follows the movement of the viewpoint. Full map draws the whole map Level of detail How many grid points to skip between reads. Auto (default) picks the smallest value (a power of 2) for which the number of grid points in the drawn range fits within the LoD budget. You can also specify a value directly, from 1 (full resolution) to 8. It is not used when Region is Box around center (all grid points are always drawn) LoD budget The number of grid points that Auto Level of detail tries to fit within. The unit, 1 Mcell, is about one million grid points. Increasing it gives finer detail but makes drawing heavier (the default is 2 Mcell). Shown only when Region is Full map Refine on zoom When ON (default), the drawn range is narrowed to the area around the viewpoint and redrawn in finer detail accordingly. When zoomed out, the whole map is coarse, and the zoomed-in part becomes finer. Shown only when Region is Full map

Buffer size and Use periodic boundary are shown only when Region is Box around center.

docs.title: disorder
docs.text:
A Renderer that displays the backbone of disordered regions in proteins and nucleic acids. Target Object: molecule (MolCoord).

Parts of a crystal structure that are invisible because of disorder can be shown as a dotted line (Bezier curve) that connects smoothly to a backbone display such as ribbon.

Can be created only after the Object is in the scene

disorder does not work on its own; it needs a backbone Renderer to target. For this reason, it is not listed among the Renderer types shown when opening a file. It can be created from the New Renderer dialog, in which case the first of the tube / ribbon / cartoon / nucl Renderers in the scene is set as the Target.

docs.title: Detecting disordered regions
docs.text: If residue numbers are not consecutive within the same chain (so that the backbone display of ribbon or similar is broken), the gap is judged to be disordered and becomes a target of the dotted display. If the chain differs before and after the gap, nothing is displayed.

docs.title: Color
docs.text: Colors are set in the Color panel, as with other Renderers. The dotted line is colored with the colors of the residues at both ends of the disordered region; if the two ends differ in color, the line forms a gradient between them.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties.

The displayed part can be restricted with a selection expression (sel). By default it is *, which targets all disordered regions in the molecule. If it is changed to, for example, A.1:100.*, only the disordered regions within residues 1 to 100 of chain A are targeted. This can be used to attach several disorder Renderers to one molecule and change the shape of the dotted line for each. The figure below is an example in which separate Renderers were created for the right and left disordered regions, with different dot sizes and spacing.

As with other Renderers, an outline can be drawn with edge lines, and the material can be changed to nolighting (flat fill).

docs.title: Disorder
docs.text: Target The Renderer on which the dotted line of the disordered region is displayed. At creation, it is chosen automatically from the Renderers that exist at that time, such as ribbon / cartoon / nucl. If an unintended Target has been chosen, change it here Detail Polygon subdivision level of the dots (spheres) of the dotted line. Larger values give a finer, smoother result Dot size Size of the dots (spheres) of the dotted line. The default is 0.3. In the figure below, the left is 0.1 and the right is 0.5 Dot separation Spacing of the dotted line. In the figure below, the left is 0.6 and the right is 1.8 Loop size How the disordered part connects to the backbone. A larger value gives a smoother, more protruding shape (it affects the positions of the Bezier curve control points). The default is 2.0. In the figure below, the left is 1.0 and the right is 6.0 Loop size 2 How the disordered part connects to the C-terminal side of the backbone (for proteins). The default is -1, in which case the Loop size value is used for both the N-terminus and the C-terminus. If a value of 0 or more is given, Loop size sets the smoothness of the connection on the N-terminal side and Loop size 2 on the C-terminal side. The figure below shows Loop size = 0.5 and Loop size 2 = 4. On the N-terminal side (the near β-sheet), the value is very small, so the connection is discontinuous, as if bent; on the C-terminal side (the far β-sheet), the value is large, so the connection is smooth Color Default color

docs.title: dsurf2 (molecular surface, distance field)
docs.text:
Merged into dsurface

The distance-field molecular surface is now one of the choices for Algorithm (Distance field) in dsurface. For this reason, dsurf2 no longer appears in the New Renderer list. To create one, choose dsurface and set Algorithm to Distance field.

The two were originally the same Renderer with the same properties, differing only in how the mesh was built. With both in the list, there was nothing to tell you which one to choose.

docs.title: Existing scenes
docs.text:
Scene files (.qsc) that contain dsurf2 still open as before. When loaded, they become a dsurface with Algorithm set to Distance field. This is exactly the rendering that dsurf2 performed, so the appearance does not change.

On the other hand, scenes originally saved with dsurface open with Algorithm set to Distance field (the new default). The previous dsurface was a voxel-based implementation, so the look of the mesh and the effect of Detail change. To get the previous appearance back, set Algorithm to EDTSurf (voxel).

docs.text:

  • Renderer list

docs.title: dsurface (molecular surface, direct calculation)
docs.text:
A Renderer that calculates a molecular surface directly from a molecule Object and draws it. Target Object: molecule (MolCoord). There is no need to generate a separate surface Object. Coloring is set in the Color panel. Besides Solid coloring, electrostatic potential and Multi-gradient can also be chosen (→ Coloring).

In preparation

Example figures will be added later.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties.

docs.title: Surface
docs.text: Item Default Description Drawing mode Fill Fill the surface (Fill) / mesh (Wireframe) / points (Dots) Line/Point size 1.2 px Line width for Wireframe and point size for Dots. Not used with Fill Algorithm Distance field How the mesh is built (see below) Surface type Solvent excluded Type of surface. van der Waals (van der Waals surface) / Solvent accessible (solvent-accessible surface) / Solvent excluded (solvent-excluded surface) Detail 6 Fineness of the mesh. Chosen from fixed steps (1 / 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 16 / 24 / 32)

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
Selects how the mesh is built. Whichever is chosen, the meaning of the surface type (Surface type) is the same; what differs is how the mesh is built and how fast.

Algorithm Supported Surface type Description Distance field vdW / SAS / SES Places a distance field on a grid and meshes it (default) MeshMS (analytic SES) SES only Meshes the solvent-excluded surface analytically. At fine settings it is much faster than the distance field EDTSurf (voxel) vdW / SAS / SES The conventional implementation, using voxels and a distance transform

The Detail scale is aligned across the three. At the default of 6, all algorithms give almost the same number of vertices.

If MeshMS cannot be used, it falls back to the distance field

Even if MeshMS (analytic SES) is selected, the mesh is built with the distance field instead when Surface type is anything other than Solvent excluded, or when generation fails. The switch and its reason appear in the Output panel as lines starting with DirectSurfRend>. The values you set are not changed.

docs.title: Atom radii
docs.text:
Radius of each element used in the surface calculation (in Å).

Item Default Carbon 1.70 Nitrogen 1.55 Oxygen 1.52 Sulfur 1.80 Phosphorus 1.80 Hydrogen 1.20 Others 1.70

docs.title: Click and hover
docs.text: When Drawing mode is Fill, clicking or hovering over the surface targets the atom at that position. Wireframe and Dots are not targeted. Rectangle selection and lasso selection do not target the surface (→ Picking and hover display).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Renderer list
  • molsurf
  • dsurf2
  • cpk
  • Material / Edge lines

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.15.530

docs.title: Edge lines
docs.text:
Edge lines draw lines (edge lines) along the outlines of rendered objects. This is a common property of all Renderers, set in the Common section of the property inspector. However, this setting is not shown for Renderers that have no faces and therefore no outline to draw (simple / trace / spline / contour / gpu_mapmesh, selection highlights, unit cells, namelabel).

Also shown in the molecular view

Edge lines are drawn in both the molecular view (real-time display) and the rendering result. The two use different drawing methods, but they are tuned to look as similar as possible. Details do not match exactly, so check the rendering result for the final appearance.

docs.title: Edge type
docs.text:
None No edge lines (default) Edges Draws edge lines Silhouette Draws silhouette lines. Lines are drawn only along the outline

The lines for each setting look as follows.

  • Edges (0.06 Å)
  • Silhouette (0.03 Å)

docs.title: Width
docs.text:
Specifies the line width in Å. Because the unit is not pixels, lines get thicker accordingly when the image size is increased at rendering time.

Commonly used widths are as follows.

Width Value Example Normal 0.06 Å Thick 0.15 Å Thin 0.03 Å

docs.title: Color
docs.text: Specifies the line color. Black is usually used, but any color can be specified, such as white lines on a black background.

docs.title: Edge line accuracy and the detail value
docs.text:
How accurately edge lines are extracted and drawn depends largely on the Renderer's polygon subdivision (the detail value). The figures below use a line width of 0.1 Å and show, from left to right, the ballstick detail value increased to 2, 5, 10 and 20.

The larger the detail value, the smoother and more continuous the lines. With a small detail value, lines tend to be broken, and this is more noticeable the thicker the line is. When making lines thicker, also increase the detail value.

The default detail value of ballstick is 5, but the example above shows that with a line width of 0.1 Å, a value of 10 or more is preferable.

docs.title: Setting by style
docs.text: Edge line settings are also provided as styles, and can be applied together from the right-click menu of the scene tree (→ Styles).

docs.title: gpu_mapmesh (contour, GPU)
docs.text:
A Renderer that draws the contour mesh on the GPU (with shaders). Target Objects: density map (DensityMap), electrostatic potential map (ElePotMap).

GPU implementation of contour

The display is equivalent to contour, and the same properties appear in the GPU contour section of the Properties tab. The display settings can also be adjusted from the Density map panel (see Side panels).

No longer offered when creating a new Renderer

It cannot change the line width and is slower than the CPU version, contour, so it has been removed from the New Renderer list. Existing ones in a scene are still displayed, and their settings can still be changed.

In preparation

docs.title: isosurf (isosurface)
docs.text:
A Renderer that draws a scalar field such as an electron density map as an isosurface (surface). Target Objects: density map (DensityMap) and electrostatic potential map (ElePotMap).

In preparation

This page is only a skeleton. Details of each property will be added later.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties.

docs.title: Isosurf
docs.text:
Map kind The kind of this map (Crystallographic / Cryo-EM). Read-only; it shows the result of the Map type detection of the DensityMap Region The range to display. Auto (default) becomes Box around center for crystallographic maps and Full map for cryo-EM maps. Box around center draws only the area around the view center and follows the movement of the viewpoint. Full map draws the entire map Level of detail How many grid points to skip between reads. With Auto (default), when Region is Full map it picks the smallest value (a power of 2) at which the number of grid points in the drawn range fits within LoD budget; when Region is Box around center it uses all grid points. You can also specify a value directly, from 1 (full resolution) to 8 LoD budget The number of grid points that Auto Level of detail tries to stay within. The unit, 1 Mcell, is about one million grid points. A larger value gives finer detail but makes drawing slower (default: 16 Mcell). Shown only when Region is Full map Refine on zoom When ON (default), the drawn range is narrowed to the area around the viewpoint and redrawn in finer detail accordingly. When zoomed out, the whole map is drawn coarsely, and the part you zoom in on becomes finer. Shown only when Region is Full map Cap mode Whether to close with a face the places where the isosurface is cut at the boundary of the displayed range. With Auto (default), the surface is closed when Region is Full map and for generated surface Objects, and is left open when Region is Box around center. On always closes it, and Off always leaves it open

Max grid size and Use periodic boundary are shown only when Region is Box around center.

The default color is light gray (contour, the contour mesh, is blue).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Renderer list
  • contour
  • Material / Edge lines

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.13.523

docs.title: Material
docs.text:
Separately from color, you can specify a material (surface finish) for the 3D objects drawn by a Renderer. It is a common property of all Renderers, and is set in the Common section of the property inspector.

Effective only in ray tracing

The material is reflected in the ray-traced output of the rendering window. It is ignored in the molecular view (real-time OpenGL display).

docs.title: Material types
docs.text:
The following materials are available. The specified color applies to every material.

Name Appearance default The default finish. Plastic gloss matte A matte finish spec_metal A metallic finish with very strong shininess diff_metal A matte metallic finish metallic_chrome Chrome-like metal with sharp reflections metallic_copper Copper-like metal, somewhat rough stone35 A rough matte finish like stone wood31 A slightly glossy finish like wood shadow A shadow-like finish with no shininess nolighting Flat fill with no shading toon1 / toon2 Toon-style shading

shadow has no highlights (shininess), so it is suitable for making an object translucent and overlaying it on other objects.

Metallic materials reflect the surrounding ambient light, so they may look dark depending on the environment.

If a material name that does not exist is specified, default is used.

The appearance differs from the POV-Ray backend

The table above describes the finishes in the default rendering backend, Umbreon. The deprecated POV-Ray backend differs in the following points (see Rendering).

  • stone35 / wood31 are drawn as stone-grain and wood-grain patterns. Umbreon has no ability to generate patterns, so they become matte finishes of different roughness.
  • metallic_chrome / metallic_copper / stone35 / wood31 ignore the color specification.
  • metallic_chrome / metallic_copper look like plastic instead of metal.

docs.title: For the whole Renderer
docs.text: Specify it in Material in the Common section of the property inspector. It is empty (unspecified) by default, in which case the default material is applied.

docs.title: Per color
docs.text:
You can specify the material as a modifier of a color.

<color>{material: <material name>}

To set the color to yellow and the material to shadow, specify as follows (the three differ only in how the color is written; all are the same pure yellow).

yellow{material:shadow}
rgb(1,1,0){material:shadow}
#FF0{material:shadow}

If you specify a different material for each Paint row in Coloring, you can also change the finish for each secondary structure.

Sheet SteelBlue{material:stone35} Helix khaki{material:wood31} Others (*) FloralWhite{material:metallic_chrome}

A material cannot be specified on its own, so always specify it together with a color.

Fineness of patterns in POV-Ray

When you use wood31 or stone35 with the POV-Ray backend, the wood-grain and stone patterns are fine, so you cannot see them unless you zoom in considerably. Umbreon does not draw the patterns at all.

docs.title: namelabel (name label)
docs.text:
A Renderer that attaches name labels to atoms in the molecular view. Target Object: molecule (MolCoord).

Created automatically when you add a label

namelabel is an internal Renderer that is created automatically when you click an atom in the molecular view to show its name. In the scene tree it appears as an unnamed (*namelabel) row (→ Loading and displaying a structure). It is not listed in the New Renderer dialog.

In preparation

Example figures will be added later.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The label text is flat text drawn on the screen and has no 3D shape. For this reason, the edge line settings are not shown in the property inspector.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties.

docs.title: Name label
docs.text:
Item Default Description Format (empty) Format of the label text. When empty, it takes the form {chain} {resn}{resi} {name} Color Yellow Color of the label text Label on top OFF When ON, the label is always visible and is not hidden by shapes in front of it Max labels 50 Upper limit on the number of labels (1 to 1000). When exceeded, the oldest ones disappear first Horizontal align Left Which position of the label is aligned to the atom (horizontal: Left / Center / Right) Vertical align Bottom Which position of the label is aligned to the atom (vertical: Top / Middle / Bottom) Offset X / Offset Y 0 px Amount by which the label is shifted on the screen from the atom position (-100 to 100 px)
  • In Format, list item names enclosed in {}, as in {resn}{resi} {name}. The available item names are the same as the words of the selection expression: name (atom name), resn (residue name), resi (residue number), chain (chain name), elem (element symbol), bfac (B-factor), occ (occupancy), alt (altloc), aid (atom ID), and molname (molecule name). You can add a numeric format after :, as in {bfac:.2f}.
  • Format is the default text for labels that have no format of their own. If a label has its own format or text (for example, one added with the Console label command), that is used instead.
  • The default for Horizontal align / Vertical align (Left / Bottom) is the conventional placement, with the lower left of the label at the atom. The reference point is the atom position shifted by Offset X / Offset Y.

docs.title: Font
docs.text:
Item Default Description Font size 12 pt Size of the text (1 to 72 pt) Font name sans-serif Choose from the list of fonts installed on the system Font style Normal Normal / Italic Font weight Normal Normal / Bold

The default color and font for newly created labels can be changed in Atom Labels under Settings (→ Settings reference).

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The alignment (Horizontal align / Vertical align) is also reflected in POV-Ray output, but not in output to the LW viewer, where labels remain bottom-left aligned.
  • In command-line rendering, labels are not drawn.

docs.title: nucl (nucleic acid)
docs.text: A Renderer dedicated to nucleic acids such as RNA and DNA. Target Object: molecule (MolCoord). In addition to a backbone tube display like tube, it can display base residues in a variety of shapes, such as sticks.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties.

docs.title: Nucleic acid
docs.text:
Show tube Whether to display the backbone tube. By turning the tube display OFF and showing the backbone with a separate tube Renderer, you can create more complex displays. The left figure below shows Show tube turned OFF, and the right shows an example that combines two different backbone displays using a separate tube Renderer Connect base pair When residues form a base pair, whether to display the two residues with a single stick (ON) or with two separate sticks (OFF). The figure below shows the OFF case Base type

The display shape of the base part.

basepair Displays residues as sticks (default) simple1 Displayed as sticks like basepair, but with a shape that bends at the N-glycosidic bond between the base and the sugar. The left figure below is Connect base pair = ON, and the right is OFF detail1 A mode in which the base part is displayed as a plate (the display does not change depending on base pairing) detail2 A mode in which, in addition to detail1, the ribose part is also displayed as a plate Detail The fineness of the residue display. Larger values give a smoother display, but increase the number of polygons and make processing heavier. In ray tracing, it is ignored except when edge lines are used Base size The size of the residue display. Specifies the radius of the cylinders of the stick-like parts, in Å Base thick The thickness of the plate-like bases and so on when Base type is detail1 / detail2. At 100%, the plate thickness equals the stick thickness; for example, at 50% the plate thickness is halved (the figure below is for detail2)

docs.title: Tube / Section / Putty
docs.text:
The backbone display is the same as tube, so the settings are also shared with it. Only the items that are often changed in nucl are shown here.

Pivot atom name The name of the atom the tube passes through. The default is P (the phosphorus atom of the backbone phosphate), but with this the tube tends to swing too wide of the actual residues. In some cases, changing it to C5' (the 5' carbon of the ribose) or similar gives a better appearance (especially depending on Base type)

docs.title: Base pair detection
docs.text:
When a PDB file is loaded, the structure is checked, and if two residues are judged to form a Watson-Crick base pair, they are automatically marked as forming a base pair. The judgment takes into account the hydrogen bond distance and the planarity of the two bases.

The nucl Renderer displays base pairs only for those judged to form base pairs at load time. You cannot manually force specified residues to form a base pair, or delete a base pair.

  • Material / Edge lines

docs.title: ribbon
docs.text:
A Renderer that draws the backbone of a protein or polypeptide as a ribbon along a spline curve. Target Object: molecule (MolCoord).

  • Helices are drawn as ribbons
  • Sheets are drawn as flat plates
  • Coils are drawn as tubes

For the ribbon to be drawn correctly, secondary structure must be assigned to the protein molecule. Secondary structure is normally assigned automatically when a file is loaded. To reassign it manually, use Reassign secondary str... in the Tools menu (see Assigning secondary structure).

If you create a ribbon for a chain polymer other than a protein, such as RNA or DNA, it is simply drawn as a tube, the same as tube.

docs.title: Preset styles
docs.text:
Commonly used ribbon settings are provided as styles. Right-click the Renderer in the scene tree and choose a style from the list to apply it (see Styles).

Default The default ribbon display. Coils are thick tubes; helices and sheets are plate-like ribbons with a rectangular cross-section (figure below, left) Fancy1 A Molscript-style ribbon display. The inside of helices and the sides of sheets are colored whitish, and the cross-section of helices is dumbbell-shaped (figure below, center) Round Coils are thin tubes; helices and sheets are rounded ribbons with an elliptical cross-section (figure below, right)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties (name, visibility, material, edge lines, etc.), see Common Renderer properties.

docs.title: Ribbon
docs.text: Section detail Number of polygon divisions in the cross-section direction. The larger the value, the finer the division and the smoother the display, but the slower the rendering Axial detail Number of polygon divisions along the chain. The larger the value, the finer the division and the smoother the display, but the slower the rendering Smooth color When the colors of adjacent residues differ, ON makes the coloring between residues a gradient (figure below, left), and OFF makes the color change at the midpoint (figure below, right) Pivot atom name Name of the atom that the ribbon or tube passes through. For proteins it defaults to CA (Cα carbon atom), and normally you do not need to change it Cap type Shape of the ends. sphere gives a spherical end (figure below, left), flat gives a flat end (figure below, center), and with none no polygons are generated at the ends, so they look open (figure below, right) Segment-end fade out Whether to fade out the ends of segments

docs.title: Helix
docs.text:
Settings for the cross-section shape of helices and for the connection shape at the start (Tail) and end (Head).

Section type Cross-section shape. From the left in the figure below: Elliptical (ellipse), Rectangle (rectangle), Round rectangle (rectangle without corners), Fancy (dumbbell) Back color Color of the inside of the helix. When OFF, the inside and outside have the same color. The default is OFF Width Thickness of the helix. The unit is Å Tuber Width of the helix, specified as a multiple of Width Sharpness The meaning depends on Section type. For Round rectangle, it is how much the corners of the rectangle are rounded off. At 1 the shape is almost angular, and the closer to 0, the rounder the shape. For Fancy, it is the size of the circles at both ends of the dumbbell. A value close to 0 makes the section thinner with a pronounced edge (figure below, left, value = 0); closer to 0.5 gives a shape close to Round rectangle (figure below, center, value = 0.5); above 0.5 gives a shape like the figure below, right (value = 0.75) Smoothness At 0 the helix is a curve passing through the position of the pivot atom (Cα atom by default); at lower values it becomes a smooth curve that does not pass through the pivot atom Head type / Tail type Shape of the end (Head) and start (Tail) of the helix. Round (smooth connection, figure below, left), Flat (discontinuous, figure below, center), Arrow (arrow-shaped, figure below, right) You will rarely make the end of a helix an arrow. For the arrow settings, see Sheet below Head power / Tail power Smoothness of the connection. The figure below shows the values 1, 1.5 and 3 with the type set to round (for round, values of 1 or less have no effect) Head arrow height / width Effective only when type is arrow. Specifies the height and width of the arrow (see Sheet)

docs.title: Sheet
docs.text:
The settings are the same as for helices, and their meanings are also almost the same, so see Helix. Only the settings whose meaning differs for sheets are described below.

Side color For sheets, the color of the sides, not the back, changes Smoothness For sheets, 0 makes the ribbon wave too much, so the default is 0.5 (giving an extended β sheet). However, when side chains are displayed, 0.5 makes the side chains look as if they float, so it may be better to change it to 0 Head type = Arrow The tip of the β sheet becomes arrow-shaped (you will rarely make the Tail an arrow). In this case Head power affects how sharp the arrow tip is. The figure below shows 0.5 on the right, 1 in the center and 2 on the left Head arrow width Width of the arrowhead. At 100% the arrow is three times as wide as the body of the sheet, and at 0% its width equals the body of the sheet (that is, there is no arrowhead) Head arrow height Height of the arrowhead. Decreasing the value reduces the height of the arrowhead

docs.title: Coil
docs.text: Coils have no concept of Head / Tail, so there are only settings for the cross-section shape. Each setting has the same meaning as the cross-section settings in Helix.

docs.title: tube
docs.text: A Renderer that displays the backbone of proteins and nucleic acids as a smooth tube. Target Object: molecule (MolCoord). The backbone is drawn as a uniform tube regardless of the secondary structure assignment.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: For the common properties, see Common Renderer properties.

docs.title: Tube
docs.text: Axial detail Number of polygon subdivisions along the chain. Larger values give a smoother tube but slow down rendering Smoothness At 0, the tube is a curve passing through the positions of the pivot atoms. Below that, it is a smooth curve that does not pass through the pivot atoms Smooth color When the colors of adjacent residues differ, ON makes the coloring between residues a gradient Pivot atom name Name of the atom the tube passes through. The default for proteins is CA (Cα carbon atom). The figure below compares different pivot atoms Start / End type Shape of the ends (sphere / flat / none)

docs.title: Section
docs.text:
Settings for the cross-section shape of the tube.

Type Shape of the cross section. The default is elliptical. The other options are round_square (rectangle with rounded corners, left in the figure below) and rectangle (rectangle with sharp corners, right in the figure below) Detail Number of polygon subdivisions around the cross section. Larger values give a smoother surface but increase the load (minimum 2). If the rendered image looks angular, increasing this together with Axial detail fixes it Width1, Width2 Thickness of the tube in Å. Width1 is the radius in the horizontal direction and Width2 is the radius in the vertical direction. Left: Width1 (0.5 Å) > Width2 (0.1 Å). Right: Width1 (0.1 Å) < Width2 (0.5 Å) (Type is elliptical) Tuber Flatness of the tube. Specifies the ratio of the thickness in the normal direction to that in the binormal direction. A value other than 1 gives a tube with an elliptical cross section. Left in the figure below: tuber = 3 (width = 0.35). Right: tuber = 0.3 (width = 1.16). Cases that use tuber < 1 are rare Sharpness Effective only when Type is round_square. Specifies how rounded the corners are. At 1, the shape is as angular as rectangle; close to 0, it approaches elliptical. In the figure below, left is 0.1 and right is 0.9

docs.title: Putty
docs.text:
Putty is a display setting that varies the thickness of the tube according to a parameter such as the B-factor. At the maximum value of the parameter, the thickness becomes High scale times larger; at the minimum value, it becomes 1/Low scale of the original. Parts with values in between change continuously (linear interpolation).

Mode off does not use putty (constant thickness). Linear and Scaling vary the thickness according to the parameter specified in Target Target The parameter that drives the thickness. B-factor or Occupancy can be selected Low scale Thickness scaling value at the minimum value of the parameter. At the residue with the smallest parameter value, the tube thins to 1/Low scale of its thickness. The default is 1/3 High scale Thickness scaling value at the maximum value of the parameter. At the residue with the largest parameter value, the tube thickens by a factor of High scale. The default is 3

docs.title: Calculating the electrostatic potential (APBS elepot calculation)
docs.text:
Calculates the electrostatic potential map of a molecule using APBS. Open the APBS electrostatic potential dialog with Tools > APBS elepot calculation.... The calculated map becomes an ElePotMap (electrostatic potential) Object and can be used for coloring molecular surfaces and other purposes.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
The calculation uses APBS and pdb2pqr, which assigns charges and atomic radii. Both are bundled with the macOS / Windows release assets, so no setup is normally needed. For builds that do not bundle them, specify the executable paths in Settings > Tools > APBS / PDB2PQR (→ Configuring external tools).

If the paths are not set, a warning is shown at the top of the dialog and Start cannot be pressed.

To use a surface for coloring, generate the molecular surface first.

docs.title: Target
docs.text: Item Default Description Molecule — Molecule to calculate Use selection / selection OFF When ON, only the part specified by the selection expression is calculated. To exclude water molecules and ions, specify something like protein Elepot name pot_<molecule name> Name of the resulting electrostatic potential map Object. Filled in automatically when a molecule is chosen

docs.title: Charge method
docs.text:
Item Default Description Method Use PDB2PQR How charges are assigned (see below) Force field Value in Settings (default charmm) With Use PDB2PQR, the force field used to assign charges (charmm / amber / tyl06 / peoepb / swanson) Use hydrogen atoms OFF With Use internal, uses the hydrogen atoms in the molecule
  • Use PDB2PQR: Assigns charges and atomic radii with pdb2pqr, then runs the calculation.
  • Use internal: Uses CueMol's own charge assignment. pdb2pqr is not required, but the N and C termini of proteins are not handled correctly, and when the molecule has no hydrogen atoms, charges are assigned by a simple method that adds the charges of hydrogens to the atoms they are bonded to, so this is not recommended. If the molecule has hydrogen atoms, turning Use hydrogen atoms ON avoids this problem.

docs.title: APBS options
docs.text:
Calculation conditions for APBS. They normally do not need to be changed. See the APBS documentation for details.

Item Default Description Solve non-linear PBE OFF Solves the non-linear Poisson-Boltzmann equation Temperature (K) 298.15 Temperature Max grid size (A) 1.0 Grid spacing (Å) Water dielectric 78.54 Dielectric constant of the solvent Protein dielectric 2.0 Dielectric constant of the molecular interior

docs.title: Running and results
docs.text:
Press Start to begin the calculation; progress is displayed (pdb2pqr runs first, then APBS). Large molecules take longer. Stop cancels a running calculation.

When the calculation finishes, an electrostatic potential map Object is added to the scene and the dialog closes. The addition can be reverted with a single Undo.

  • The map comes with a unitcell Renderer that outlines the calculated region. Once you have confirmed that the region is large enough, it can be hidden or deleted.
  • The calculated map is saved together with the scene when the scene is saved to .qsc.

docs.title: Coloring a molecular surface
docs.text: In the Color panel, select a molsurf Renderer, choose Electrostatic potential as the Coloring type, and specify the calculated map. Turn By SAS ON and set High / Low to about ±2 (in kT/e) to make the distribution easier to see. For the detailed procedure, see Coloring a molecular surface by electrostatic potential; for the settings, see Coloring.

docs.title: Using from the Console
docs.text: In the native mode of the Console, calc_elepot performs the same operation (→ Console command list).

  • ElePotMap (electrostatic potential)

docs.title: Extracting interactions (Interaction)
docs.text:
This tool automatically extracts intramolecular and intermolecular atomic contacts (candidate interactions such as hydrogen bonds) and displays them as lines and labels of a measurement display (atomintr). Open the Interaction analysis dialog with Tools > Interaction....

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Molecule
docs.text:
Item Default Description Molecule / selection — The molecule to extract interactions from, and the part of it to target. If the selection is empty, all atoms are targeted Second molecule OFF When ON, you can choose a second molecule. Interactions between the first selection and the second molecule are extracted Second selection OFF When ON, you can specify a second selection. Only interactions spanning the first selection and the second selection are extracted

The second selection applies to the second molecule if Second molecule is ON, and to the first molecule if it is OFF. If you choose the same molecule as the first one for the second molecule, the second molecule setting is ignored.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Item Default Description Min distance (A) 2.5 Minimum distance (Å) to count as an interaction Max distance (A) 3.5 Maximum distance (Å) to count as an interaction. Must be larger than Min distance Max labels 30 Maximum number of interactions to extract (1 to 1000) Hydrogen bond (N, O) only OFF When ON, pairs involving carbon atoms are excluded (in proteins, only pairs of atoms such as N and O remain) Label set name measure Name of the atomintr Renderer to which the interactions are added. It is created if it does not exist

Each time you open the dialog, all items other than the molecule return to their defaults.

Hydrogen bond geometry is not considered

What is extracted is the set of atom pairs that satisfy the distance condition; hydrogen bond geometry and the like are not taken into account.

docs.title: Running and results
docs.text:
When you press OK, the atom pairs that meet the conditions are added to the atomintr Renderer (named by Label set name) of the first molecule. If the Renderer does not exist, it is created, and the interactions are displayed as dotted lines with distance labels. The addition can be undone with a single Undo.

  • If no matching interaction is found, "No interaction was found" is shown and the dialog stays open.
  • Interactions beyond Max labels are not added. If that is not enough, Undo, increase Max labels, and run again.

The extracted interactions are the same as measurements made with the Distance tool in the tool palette. The display settings can be changed in the properties of atomintr.

docs.title: Example: extracting interactions between two chains
docs.text:
To extract the interactions between chain A and chain B in PDB entry 1OX1 (trypsin and a substrate analog):

  1. Specify chain A as the first selection.
  2. Turn Second selection ON and specify chain B as the second selection.
  3. Leave the other items at their defaults and press OK.

Candidate interactions between chain A and chain B are added to measure.

docs.title: Using it from the Console
docs.text: In the native mode of the Console, analyze_interactions performs the same processing (see Console command list).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Tools menu
  • atomintr (measurement display)
  • Toolbar and tool palette — measuring distances, angles and dihedral angles

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Generating a molecular surface (Mol surface generation)
docs.text:
Generates a molecular surface (solvent-excluded surface, SES) from a molecule. Choose Tools > Mol surface generation... to open the Mol surface generation dialog. The generated surface becomes a MolSurfObj (molecular surface) Object and is displayed by the molsurf Renderer.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Target
docs.text:
Item Default Description Molecule — The molecule to build the surface for Use selection / selection OFF When ON, the surface is built only for the part specified by the selection expression. The ▼ at the right end gives access to named selections, history and the selection builder

Exclude water molecules

Crystal structures and similar data may contain water molecules. Unless a selection is used, the surface is calculated for all atoms, including waters and substrates. To build it for the protein only, turn Use selection ON and specify protein; for chain A only, specify chain A.

docs.title: Surface
docs.text:
Item Default Description Object name sf_<molecule name> Name of the surface Object to be created. Filled in automatically when a molecule is chosen Point density (/A) 2 Fineness of the surface (1 to 10). A higher value gives a finer surface, but the calculation takes longer and memory use and file size also increase Probe radius (A) 1.4 Radius (Å) of the probe used to calculate the surface. The default is the radius of a water molecule Algorithm Auto Method used to calculate the surface (Auto / MeshMS / BALL)
  • For a small molecule of about 10 kDa, raising Point density to about 5 gives a smoother surface. For a large molecule over 100 kDa, a lower value calculates faster.
  • For the differences between the Algorithm options, see MolSurfObj generation algorithm. The default Auto uses MeshMS and switches to BALL if it fails.

docs.title: Running and the result
docs.text:
Pressing OK creates the surface Object (MolSurfObj) and the molsurf Renderer that displays it. The generation can be reverted with a single Undo.

  • The molsurf Renderer refers to the source molecule and is colored with CPK. From the Color panel, the coloring can be changed to Paint / CPK / Rainbow and so on, in the same way as for other molecule Renderers (→ Coloring).
  • Each time a surface is generated, the algorithm used, the elapsed time, and the numbers of vertices and faces are written to the log in the Output panel.
  • The generated surface is saved together with the scene when the scene is saved as .qsc.

docs.title: Regenerating a surface (Regenerate surface)
docs.text:
Right-click a MolSurfObj in the scene tree and choose Regenerate surface… to open the Regenerate surface dialog. The same surface can be regenerated with a different Point density (/A) and Algorithm.

  • The source molecule, selection and probe radius are only displayed and cannot be changed. To change them, create a new surface with Mol surface generation.
  • If the source molecule is not in the scene (for example, a surface loaded from a file), the items cannot be selected.
  • Regenerating with only the density changed finishes quickly (→ MolSurfObj).

docs.title: Using from the Console
docs.text: In the native mode of the Console, a surface is generated with create_surface and regenerated with recalc_surface (→ Console command list).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Tools menu
  • MolSurfObj (molecular surface) / molsurf
  • Cutting a molecular surface / Calculating the electrostatic potential
  • Coloring a molecular surface by electrostatic potential

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Morphing structural changes (Mol morphing animation)
docs.text:
Displays the change between two different structures of the same molecule (morphing) as an animation. It uses linear interpolation, so it is suited to animating local structural changes.

A morph is built in two steps.

  1. In Tools > Mol morphing animation..., convert a molecule (MolCoord) to a MorphMol and add the structures to interpolate (frames). This is described on this page.
  2. Add a MolAnim element to the Animation tab in the bottom panel and decide when, and over how long, the morph is played (→ MolAnim (structural change)).

For a worked example, see Making an animation and exporting a movie.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Preparation: superpose the structures
docs.text: Morph interpolation uses the coordinates as they are. If the two structures are not aligned in space, first align them with molecular superposition.

docs.title: Morph animation tool dialog
docs.text:
Open the Morph animation tool dialog with Tools > Mol morphing animation.... Operations in the dialog are applied to the scene immediately, and each operation can be undone. Close the dialog with Close (there are no OK / Cancel buttons).

Choose the target molecule in Target.

docs.title: Converting a MolCoord to a MorphMol
docs.text:
When the selected molecule is not yet a MorphMol, a Convert to MorphMol button appears in Setup. Pressing it converts the molecule to a MorphMol.

  • The converted molecule becomes the start structure of the change (the reference frame).
  • The molecule is replaced in the scene, but its name and Renderers are kept as they are.
  • The conversion can be undone.

docs.title: Adding and deleting frames
docs.text:
When you select a MorphMol, Frames shows the list of structures (frames) it holds. Immediately after conversion, only the reference frame (this) is present.

Button Description Add PDB file... Choose PDB files (.pdb / .ent / .pdb.gz) and add them as frames. You can choose several. The files are not loaded into the scene Add mol... Add another molecule in the scene as a frame. Choose the molecule in Molecule to add and press Add as frame Delete Delete the selected frame. (this) cannot be deleted

An added frame is inserted after the row selected in the list. If no row is selected, it is added at the end. The first frame in the list is the start of the interpolation, and the last frame is the end.

To edit a MorphMol later, choose the MorphMol as Target in the same dialog.

docs.title: Correspondence between structures
docs.text:
If corresponding residues or atoms do not exist among the start, end and intermediate frames, those atoms are excluded from the morphing calculation.

  • If an atom in the reference frame (this) is missing from other frames, that atom stays still during the animation.
  • If an atom is present in other frames but not in the reference frame, it is ignored when the frame is loaded.

For this reason, morphing between structures of the same molecule determined in different states is easy, but morphing between similar but different homologs does not work as it is. If you build a model structure with matching residue numbers, for example by homology modeling, it can be morphed correctly.

docs.title: Large structural changes
docs.text: Linear interpolation has difficulty representing very large, domain-level changes. You can create an animation by generating several intermediate structures with other software and lining them up as frames to connect them.

docs.title: Using from the Console
docs.text: In the native mode of the Console, the same operations are available with convert_to_morph / list_morph_frames / add_morph_frame / remove_morph_frame (→ Console command list).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Tools menu
  • MolAnim (structural change) — the animation element for morphing
  • Making an animation and exporting a movie

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Assigning secondary structure (Reassign secondary structure)
docs.text:
Renderers such as cartoon and ribbon draw their shapes based on the secondary structure of the protein. This page explains how secondary structure is assigned and how to change the assignment with Tools > Reassign secondary str....

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Assignment when a file is loaded
docs.text:
When the Calculate secondary structure option in the <format>-specific options shown while opening a PDB / mmCIF file is ON (the default), the secondary structure is calculated automatically from the coordinates after loading. The calculation uses the DSSP algorithm (see Loading and displaying a structure).

When it is OFF, the secondary structure is set according to the HELIX / SHEET records in the file. For a file that has no such records, no secondary structure is assigned.

docs.title: The Reassign secondary structure dialog
docs.text:
Open the Reassign secondary structure dialog with Tools > Reassign secondary str.... Choose the target molecule in Molecule, and the operation in Mode.

Mode Description Recalculate (default) Redoes the automatic secondary structure assignment Assign Assigns the specified secondary structure to the selected part

docs.title: Recalculate (rerun the automatic assignment)
docs.text:
Recalculates the secondary structure with the same DSSP algorithm as when a file is loaded.

Item Default Description Ignore β bulge OFF Ignores β bulges in the calculation Helix gap-fill angle (°) / Angle OFF / 120 The angle used to fill gaps in helices. Angle can be set only when the switch is ON

docs.title: Assign (manual assignment)
docs.text:
Item Description Selection The selection expression for the part whose assignment is to be changed. The ▼ at the right end gives access to named selections, history and the selection builder Type The secondary structure to assign. The default is Coil

The following can be chosen for Type.

Type Description Coil Removes the secondary structure β strand Makes it a β strand α helix Makes it an α helix 3-10 helix Makes it a 310 helix π helix Makes it a π helix

For example, with the selection * and Type set to Coil, all secondary structure information is removed. If you do not like the automatic assignment, you can use this method to change regions to β strands or α helices.

Avoid extreme assignments

You can make a region that is not geometrically a β strand into a β strand, but cartoon and ribbon may then take on abnormal shapes. Avoid extreme changes such as making the whole molecule β strands, and save the scene before changing the assignment.

docs.title: Running and the result
docs.text:
When you press OK, the secondary structure of the molecule is rewritten and the change is reflected in displays such as cartoon. Both Recalculate and Assign can be undone with a single Undo.

A manually changed secondary structure is saved along with the scene when you save it to a .qsc file, and is kept the next time the scene is opened.

docs.title: Using it from the Console
docs.text: In the native mode of the Console, set_secondary_structure performs the same operation. If the selection is omitted, the automatic assignment is redone; if a selection is given, type (coil / strand / helix / helix310 / helixpi) is assigned to that part.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Tools menu
  • cartoon / ribbon
  • Selection expression syntax

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Superposing molecules (Molecular superposition)
docs.text:
Superpose two molecules. Open the Molecular superposition dialog with Tools > Molecular superposition..., then specify the molecule that stays fixed (Reference) and the molecule to be moved (Moving). Superposition changes the coordinates of the Moving molecule.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Superposition methods
docs.text:
Method under Algorithm offers three methods.

Method Applies to Characteristics US-align (default) Proteins and nucleic acids (RNA / DNA) Automatically matches the structurally similar parts and superposes them. No need to worry about the selection ranges SSM Proteins only Automatically determines the corresponding parts from the secondary structure and superposes them LSQ Any molecule Pairs the selected atoms in order and superposes them by least squares. The atoms to superpose must be specified correctly

docs.title: US-align
docs.text:
US-align automatically finds and matches the structurally similar parts, then superposes them. Unlike SSM, it can superpose RNA / DNA as well as proteins.

Pivot atom selects the atom that represents each residue (available only with US-align).

Pivot atom Description Auto (CA / C3') (default) Uses CA for amino acids and C3' for nucleotides (including modified bases) CA / C3' / C4' / P Uses the specified atom

docs.title: SSM
docs.text:
Secondary Structure Matching (SSM) determines similar parts from the secondary structure of proteins (helices, sheets, etc.) and superposes them.

  • The selection can usually be * (all atoms). To superpose onto chain A of the Reference only, specify something like chain A in Selection.
  • SSM determines the secondary structure from the main-chain atoms (main-chain amide nitrogen and carbonyl group), so superposition fails if the selection is limited to Cα atoms (name CA). Include all the main-chain atoms (e.g. name C,N,O,CA).
  • For the same reason, molecules that have only Cα coordinates and non-protein polymers such as nucleic acids cannot be superposed. Use US-align for nucleic acids.

docs.title: LSQ
docs.text:
Superposes by least squares (Least Square Fitting). It works with any molecule, but the Selection of the Reference and the Moving molecule must be specified with the following points in mind.

  • The number of selected atoms is the same in both molecules
  • The corresponding parts of each molecule are selected (e.g. name CA over the same residue range)

docs.title: Dialog items
docs.text:
Item Description Algorithm > Method Superposition method (US-align / SSM / LSQ) Algorithm > Pivot atom Atom that represents each residue in US-align Reference > Molecule / Selection The molecule that stays fixed, and the part used for superposition. An empty Selection means all atoms Moving > Molecule / Selection The molecule to be moved, and the part used for superposition Auto recenter When ON (default), the view is centered on the selected part of the Moving molecule after superposition Use xformMat property When ON, the superposition transform is saved as the xformMat property of the molecule instead of rewriting the coordinates (default is OFF)
  • Method, Pivot atom, the two switches and the molecule choices are kept the next time the dialog is opened. Selection is empty every time.
  • In the Selection input field, the ▼ at the right end gives access to named selections, the input history and the selection builder (→ Selection builder).

docs.title: Running and results
docs.text:
Pressing OK runs the superposition and the Moving molecule moves. A single Undo reverts the superposition. If it fails, an error is shown in the dialog.

The result is written as a log to Output in the bottom panel. With US-align, the format is as follows.

===== US-align superpose result =====
 Ref: <molecule name> (<number of residues> residues), Mov: <molecule name> (<number of residues> residues)
 Pivot: auto, type: protein
 TM-score: ... (normalized by Ref), ... (normalized by Mov)
 RMSD: ... angstrom
 Nalgn: ...
 SeqID: ...
(alignment)
========================
  • TM-score: Structural similarity. Two values are given, normalized by the length of the Reference and of the Moving molecule respectively
  • RMSD: RMSD of the representative atoms of the matched residues
  • Nalgn: Number of matched (aligned) residues
  • SeqID: Fraction of the matched residues that have the same residue type

SSM outputs RMSD (RMSD of the Cα atoms), Nalgn (number of matched residues) and Ngaps (number of gaps in the alignment). LSQ outputs RMSD and Nfit (number of atoms used for the superposition).

docs.title: Using it from the Console
docs.text: In the native mode of the Console, the superpose command performs the same operation. algo specifies the method (USalign / SSM / LSQ) and pivot specifies the Pivot atom. In PyMOL compatibility mode, align / super superpose with US-align and pair_fit with LSQ (→ PyMOL compatibility mode).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Tools menu
  • Making an animation and exporting a movie — an example of superposing with SSM and then creating a morph
  • Selection expression syntax

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Cutting a molecular surface (Mol surface cutter)
docs.text:
Cuts a molecular surface (MolSurfObj) with a plane and creates a cross section. Choose Tools > Mol surface cutter... to open the Mol surface cutter dialog.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Defining the cutting plane
docs.text: The cutting plane is the near slab plane of the molecular view. Before opening the dialog, adjust the viewing direction, the viewpoint position and the slab so that the slab cuts the surface and you can see inside (see Mouse and trackpad input).

docs.title: Dialog items
docs.text:
Item Default Description Target surface — The molecular surface Object to cut Cross section Complete How the cross section is handled (see the table below) Section mesh density (/A) 5.0 Density of the triangle mesh created for the cross section. A larger value gives a finer mesh but takes longer to compute

The choices for Cross section are as follows.

Cross section Description Complete Puts the cut surface and the cross section in the same Object Separately Puts the cut surface and the cross section in separate Objects. The cross section becomes a new Object named sect_<original name>. Use this when you want to color only the cross section differently Section only Keeps only the cross section No section Keeps only the cut surface (a surface with a hole and no cross section)

docs.title: Running and the result
docs.text:
Click OK to cut the surface at the current slab plane. The cut can be undone with a single Undo.

Right after you click OK, the cut can overlap with the clipping by the slab, so it may look as if nothing happened. Rotate the molecule or widen the slab to confirm that the surface has been cut.

If you save the scene as a .qsc file, the cut surface is saved in its cut state.

Save the scene before cutting

If you cut again with a plane that interferes with a surface that has already been cut, an error may occur and the cross section may not be created.

docs.title: Using it from the Console
docs.text: In the native mode of the Console, cut_surface performs the same operation. Use mode to specify how the cross section is handled (full / separate / sect / body) (see Console command list).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Tools menu
  • Generating a molecular surface / MolSurfObj (molecular surface)

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text: This section has two parts: a basic course that teaches the operations step by step, and task-oriented figure-making tutorials. If you are new to CueMol3, start with the Quick tour to get an overview, then move on to the basic course.

docs.title: Basic course
docs.text:
A course that practices the basic operations of CueMol3 using lysozyme (1QIO) as the example. If you proceed in order, each page picks up the state left by the previous one.

  • Loading and displaying a structure — Loading, view manipulation, and the concepts of Scene / Object / Renderer
  • Selecting part of a molecule — Selecting by clicking, with panels, and with selection expressions
  • Adding, removing and configuring Renderers — Layering representations and the property inspector
  • Coloring Renderers — CPK / B-factor / Rainbow / Paint
  • Saving the camera and the scene — Handling views and scene files
  • Measurement and interaction display — Measuring distances and angles, and atomintr

docs.title: Task-oriented tutorials
docs.text:
• Making a protein ribbon figure — The basic figure-making course, from fetching a structure to coloring and outlines
  • Exporting high-resolution images for publication — Choosing between Export scene and ray tracing
  • Overlaying an electron density map — Fetching a map with Get PDB and the Density map panel
  • Displaying symmetry mates and the unit cell — Showing crystal packing and Create SYMM mol
  • Coloring a molecular surface by electrostatic potential — From surface generation to APBS calculation and coloring
  • Making an animation and exporting a movie — Timeline editing, morphing, and movie output

docs.title: Making an animation and exporting a movie
Making an animation and exporting a movie
docs.text:
This tutorial follows the whole process: arranging molecule rotations, camera movements and display switches on a timeline to build an animation, then writing it out as a movie file. The first half uses the scene (3UG9) finished in Making a protein ribbon figure, and the morphing in the second half uses two structures of transducin-α (1TND / 1TAG).

Screenshots planned

Screenshots showing the workflow will be added to this page.

docs.title: 1. How animation works
docs.text: An animation is built by placing animation elements (rotation, camera movement, display switching, etc.) on a timeline. Each element is shown as a band (strip); the position of the band is the start time and its length is the duration (→ Animation).

docs.title: 2. Open the Animation panel
docs.text: With the 3UG9 scene open, open the Animation tab in the bottom panel (→ Bottom panels).

docs.title: 3. Rotate the molecule
docs.text:
First, create the classic animation in which the molecule keeps spinning in place.

  1. Choose Simple spin from the add menu of the panel
  2. A strip is added. Select it and check the inspector on the right
  3. Adjust Rotation angle and Spin axis. At 360°, the molecule makes one full turn and returns to its original orientation (→ SimpleSpin)
  4. Drag the band to change its start position, and drag its edge to change its length (the time taken for the rotation)

docs.title: 4. Play it back to check
