The display is kept while a right-click menu is open, and the item under the pointer is picked again when the menu closes. Even after an operation that moves the view, such as Center at, whatever is now under the pointer is the target.

docs.title: Highlighting what is under the pointer
docs.text:
The same element is highlighted in the molecular view with a translucent fill and an outline. For backbone-type Renderers such as cartoon, the target is the band of one residue; for atom-level Renderers, it is that single atom.

The scene is not redrawn for this highlight. The accumulation of ambient occlusion and anti-aliasing is preserved, so even in a heavy scene, moving the pointer does not reset the image quality to its initial state (→ Scene).

No highlight appears for molecules generated by symmetry operations or for Renderers whose opacity is 0.6 or lower. Renderers with opacity 0.6 or lower are also transparent to clicks (what is behind them is picked).

docs.title: Switches
docs.text:
Three switches in Settings > Input > Mouse & Navigation control this (all default to ON; → Settings).

Setting Behavior when turned OFF GPU Picking Reverts to the previous atom-position hit-testing. The change takes effect immediately Hover Info The chip is no longer shown, and the hit-testing that follows the pointer stops altogether Hover Highlight Only the highlight is no longer shown. It works when both GPU Picking and Hover Info are ON

docs.title: Controlling the view numerically
docs.text: To adjust the view precisely, use the View > View panel in the left side panel, which lets you specify rotation, translation, zoom and slab numerically (→ Side panels).

docs.title: Operations for selection and measurement
docs.text:
When a tool other than Navigate is selected in the tool palette, the meaning of clicks and drags in the molecular view changes (→ Toolbar and tool palette).

Keyboard shortcut customization

The key-binding customization available in CueMol2 is not provided in CueMol3.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.20.539

docs.title: Rendering window
docs.text:
A separate window for producing high-quality ray-traced still images and movies. It is modeless (non-modal), so you can keep it open and work with the molecular view in the main window.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Opening the window
docs.text:
Action Result Rendering > Image rendering... Opens the window in Still mode Rendering > Movie rendering... Opens the window in Movie mode Window > Rendering Window Opens the window or brings it to the front (the mode is not changed) Render button on the toolbar Same as above

If the window is already open, Image / Movie rendering... only switches the mode.

docs.title: Window layout
docs.text: Area Contents Image area (upper left) Preview of the rendering result. The toolbar is used to save, move through the history and change the zoom (see below) Render Settings (right) Settings panel. It has an Image tab and a Render tab, plus a Detail tab when Umbreon (NPR) is selected Run bar + log (bottom) Backend / Target selection, Start / Stop, progress and log

docs.title: Image area
docs.text:
The rendering result is shown here, and the toolbar above it provides the following operations.

Item Description Save Saves the result as a PNG file Copy Copies the result to the clipboard Arrows Move back and forth through the history of rendering results Use settings Restores the settings that were used to render the result currently selected in the history + / - / 100% / Fit Change the zoom. Fit is the zoom at which the whole image fits

The zoom and scroll position are kept across renders. Even if you change one setting and render again, or move through the history, the view stays magnified, so two results can be compared at the same zoom. When the image size changes, the zoom and center are adjusted so that the same region remains visible. The whole image is shown again only for the first image and when you press Fit.

+ / - / 100% / Fit zoom around the center of the viewing area. Pinch and Cmd + wheel zoom around the pointer position.

docs.title: Run bar
docs.text:
Item Description Backend Selects the rendering backend. The default is the built-in ray tracer, Umbreon Target Selects which view to render (the open views are listed) Start Render Starts rendering Stop Cancels the rendering in progress Re-encode (Movie mode only) Rebuilds the movie file from the frame images already written

You can leave Backend set to Umbreon

Umbreon is built into the visualization library, so no external program or path setting is needed. Umbreon (NPR) is the same ray tracer with shading replaced by hatching, producing ink-drawing style figures (→ NPR). The remaining backend, POV-Ray, is the legacy backend used since CueMol2 and is deprecated (→ Rendering).

docs.title: Image tab
docs.text:
Settings that do not depend on the backend, such as the size of the output image. Choose the size from a preset, or specify the width and height directly with Custom.

Mode Size presets Still Custom / Current view / 100×100 (72dpi) / 300×300 (300dpi) / 600×600 (300dpi) / 1200×1200 (600dpi) Movie Custom / QVGA (320×240) / VGA (640×480) / SVGA (800×600) / XGA (1024×768) / HD720 (1280×720) / HD1080 (1920×1080)

Selecting Current view gives the same size as the molecular view in the main window.

docs.title: Render tab
docs.text:
Settings that are specific to each backend. When you switch backends, items the backend does not support are hidden.

For Umbreon, there is a Quality section at the top. Quality is split into independent axes, each with its own dropdown, and usually choosing here is all you need to do.

Item Description Lighting How shading is applied (Raytrace only / Ambient Occlusion / Global Illumination) Supersampling Basic image quality. The quality of edge lines is also determined by this AO quality / GI lighting Quality of the method selected in Lighting (for Global Illumination, the distribution of light) Shadows Cast shadows

The accordion below lists the individual settings. For details and default values, see Rendering.

For Umbreon (NPR), a Hatching section is added at the top, where you specify the drawing feel (Style), the combination of ink and paper (Coloring), and the density and thickness of lines and dots. Global Illumination is no longer available under Lighting in Quality. For the Detail tab, which allows finer adjustment, see NPR.

For the POV-Ray backend, you can specify the radiosity mode, whether shadows are drawn, and lighting (use of the default light / light source spread / intensity), among others. There is no Quality section.

The contents of Render Settings, including the Backend selection, are saved in the scene and restored for each scene. Changes are undoable, and Cmd+Z also works inside this window (→ Saving settings).

docs.title: Movie mode
docs.text:
In Movie mode, in addition to the above, you specify the output folder, frame rate, movie format and so on. The output settings are retained the next time the window is opened.

The process is as follows.

  1. Start Render renders the frames one by one and writes them to the output folder
  2. When all the frames are ready, they are encoded into a movie file with ffmpeg

If you cancel partway, or want to rebuild only the movie after changing settings, the Re-encode button rebuilds the movie from the frames in the output folder.

ffmpeg is required (bundled with the release builds)

ffmpeg is used to encode movies. It is bundled with the macOS / Windows release assets and can be used as is. For builds in which it is not bundled, specify the path in Settings (→ Configuring external tools).

The animation itself is created in the Animation tab of the bottom panel in the main window (→ Bottom panel).

docs.title: Differences from CueMol2
docs.text:
In CueMol2, "POV-Ray rendering" and "Animation rendering" were separate dialogs. In CueMol3 they are combined into a single window, and the type of output (still image / movie) is switched with the mode.

The ray tracing itself has also changed: instead of calling an external POV-Ray, the default is now the built-in Umbreon.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.14.525

docs.title: Selection builder
docs.text:
The selection builder is a widget for assembling a selection through GUI operations, without writing a selection expression by hand. It is available in the following places.

  • Selection panel — always present in the panel (→ Side panels)
  • Any selection expression input field — in the New Renderer dialog, tool dialogs such as molecular surface generation and superposition, the Paint selection cell of the Color panel, and so on, the ▼ button opens the same widget as a popover

The result of an operation in the builder is always reflected in the input field as a selection expression. The generated expression can be edited by hand as it is, so the builder is also a shortcut for learning the syntax.

Screenshots planned

Screenshots of each tab will be added to this page.

docs.title: Tab layout
docs.text:
Tab Role Named Apply a defined selection with one click History Apply a previously used expression with one click Term Build a single condition (term) and combine it with the current selection Mod Transform the current selection itself

Named and History are for choosing a ready-made expression; Term and Mod are for building or modifying a selection.

docs.title: Named
docs.text:
After all (*) (all atoms) at the top, the defined selections are listed in three sections. A click replaces the current selection and applies it immediately (in a popover, the popover then closes).

Only all (*) is placed outside the sections. * is selection expression syntax, not a saved definition, so it belongs to no section (→ Selection expression syntax).

Selected The selection expression currently applied to the target molecule Scene Named selection definitions saved in the scene Global Definitions shared by all scenes. Built-in selections such as protein and water are listed here

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The history of previously applied selection expressions (up to 100 entries). A click applies the expression again. The history is saved in the application and is shared by every operation that applies a selection and records into it (the Selection panel, the selection fields of the inspector and the New Renderer dialog, selections made from the scene tree, the sequence panel and the context menu, rectangle / lasso selection, and the Molecular structure panel). The whole selection (*) and the empty selection are not recorded (the whole selection can always be chosen from the top of Named). Intermediate results of combining in the Term / Mod tabs are not recorded either.

The height of the Named / History lists depends on where they are placed. In the Selection panel the lists fill the rest of the panel; in a popover they fit into the free space on the side where it opened.

docs.title: Term
docs.text:
Build a single condition (term) from a keyword and a value, then combine it with the current selection using the apply buttons.

Button Meaning Set Replace the selection with the term Add Add the term to the selection (union) Sub Remove the term from the selection (difference) Intsec Keep the intersection of the term and the selection (intersection)

When the selection is empty, pressing Enter in the value field is enough to apply Set.

The keywords include the following. The value field changes according to the keyword, and chain names, residue names, atom names and elements are autocompleted from the loaded molecule.

Keyword Meaning How to specify the value Named / History Use a defined selection or a history entry as the term Choose from the list hier Chain / residue / atom hierarchy specification Three fields (e.g. A / 2:3 / CA) chain Chain name Choose from the candidates or type resid Residue number Number or range (e.g. 2:7) resn / name / elem Residue name / atom name / element Choose from the candidates or type Altloc ID of the alternate conformation (altloc) bfac Temperature factor Comparison operator and value rprop Residue property Property name and value all / none Everything / empty No value

Using Named / History as a keyword allows combinations such as "take the intersection with a defined selection" or "remove a history expression from the current selection".

docs.title: Mod
docs.text:
Transforms the current selection itself. No term is taken.

Button Transformation Invert Invert the selection Byres Expand to whole residues that are at least partly selected Sidech / Mainch Keep only the side-chain / main-chain part Arnd Replace with the atoms within the specified distance of the selection (Around) Expn Add the surrounding atoms to the selection (Expand)

The distance for Arnd / Expn is chosen from the preset values (3 to 10 Å) in the adjacent dropdown.

docs.title: Atom count display
docs.text: Next to the apply buttons, the number of atoms that would be selected if the operation were applied is shown, so the result can be anticipated before operating. Values above 9999 are abbreviated as 12k / 1.2M; hovering the pointer shows the exact value.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Selection expression syntax — the grammar of the expressions the builder generates
  • Side panels — the Selection panel
  • Selecting part of a molecule — tutorial

Verified against: CueMol3 2.3.14.525

docs.title: Side panels
docs.text:
The side panel on the left of the window switches between views using the activity bar at the far left. Clicking the selected icon again closes the side panel.

Screenshot planned

docs.title: Activity bar layout
docs.text: Icon View Panels Explorer Scene structure and display settings Scene / Color View Camera and viewpoint control Camera / View Selection Molecule selection Molecular structure / Selection Crystal Crystallographic information Symmetry / Density map Actions Recording and replaying operations History / Actions Gear (at the bottom) Opens the Settings tab (not a side panel)

docs.title: Scene panel (scene tree)
docs.text:
Shows the contents of the scene as a tree. It corresponds to the workspace panel of CueMol2.

  • Node types: scene / Object / Renderer / Renderer group / style set
  • Toggling visibility: The eye icon on each row shows or hides it. A row that is not drawn because a parent node is hidden has a grayed-out icon.
  • Selection: Click to select; Cmd / Ctrl + click selects multiple rows. Shift + click selects a range from the previously selected row, in the order rows appear on screen (the contents of collapsed nodes are not included). The anchor does not move, so repeated Shift + click extends or shrinks the range from the same anchor. Shift + Cmd / Ctrl + click adds a range without replacing the current selection.
  • Keyboard: Up / Down move one row at a time, and Home / End move to the first / last row. Adding Shift extends the selected range, and Shift + Cmd / Ctrl extends it in addition to the current selection. Left / Right collapse / expand a row; when it cannot be collapsed or expanded any further, the focus moves to the parent row / the first child row.
  • Renaming: Press F2 or choose Rename... from the context menu to edit the name in place. Enter or moving the focus away confirms, and Esc cancels. Clicking a row only selects it and does not start editing the name.
  • Reordering: Drag and drop to change the order or the group membership.
  • Double-click: Shows the contents in the property inspector.
  • Right-click: Opens a menu for each node type (see below).

The toolbar at the top of the panel has Add / Focus / Delete / Property buttons. Focus and Property are unavailable while multiple nodes are selected. Delete removes all selected nodes and can be undone in one step with a single Undo. The Del / Backspace keys do the same.

docs.title: Main context menu operations
docs.text:
Target Main operations Scene Background color (White / Black), toggling color proofing, renaming, pasting an Object Object Specifying a selection, renaming, copy & paste, creating a new Renderer / Renderer group, setting colors, Save As, regenerating molecular surfaces Renderer Renaming, copy & paste (pastes into the same Object and the same group), setting colors, applying / creating / editing styles, changing the selection, generating a surface Object, changing the Renderer type, editing the interaction list Renderer group Show / hide (applies to its members), renaming, copy & paste, creating a new Renderer Style set Create / copy & paste / delete, toggling read-only, reading and writing files, style editor

When multiple nodes are selected, copy is available in addition to show, hide and delete. Selecting a Renderer group targets its member Renderers. Copying is not possible when nodes of different types are mixed, or when two or more Objects are selected.

Copy & paste can also be done with the shortcuts of the Edit menu (→ Edit menu).

docs.title: Creating a Renderer
docs.text:
Use New Renderer in the context menu of an Object row or a Renderer group row to choose the Renderer type and target.

  • Choosing a preset creates a group of several predefined Renderers at once.
  • Creation is performed immediately with default values; fine adjustments are made afterwards in the inspector. To cancel, use Undo.

docs.title: Color panel
docs.text:
Sets the Coloring of each Renderer. Choose a Renderer at the top (Renderers that can handle colors and their parent Objects are listed; when you select an Object or a Renderer in the scene tree, this list follows), then choose a Coloring type, and the settings for that type are shown below. The button for choosing the type shows the current type of that Renderer (Paint / Solid / CPK / B-factor / Rainbow / Potential / Multi-gradient).

Type Settings Solid Specifies a single default color Paint Specifies pairs of a selection and a color in a table. Rows can be added, deleted, cleared and reordered, and Cut / Copy / Paste are available CPK Color for each element (C / N / O / S / P / H / others) Rainbow Mode, quantity to vary, start and end hue, brightness, saturation B-factor Mode (B-factor / occupancy / distance), lower and upper colors, lower and upper values (editable only when Auto is set to Manual) Electrostatic potential Target potential map, whether to color by SAS, low / middle / high values and colors Multi-gradient Edit the stops (color breakpoints) directly on the map histogram and the gradient bar

The Paint table supports multiple selection. Cmd / Ctrl + click adds a row to or removes it from the selection, and Shift + click selects a range. Delete, Cut and Copy act on all selected rows. Reordering (Move up / Move down) is available when exactly one row is selected. Rows can also be reordered by dragging. Dropping a row below the last row moves it to the end. Rows can also be moved and selected with the same keys as the scene tree (Up / Down / Home / End and their combinations with Shift).

The toolbar above the table has four buttons: add a row (Add), reorder (Move up / Move down), and delete (Delete). Delete all and Cut / Copy / Paste are in the right-click menu of a row. The selected rows can also be deleted with the Del / Backspace keys. The boundary between the Selection column and the Color column can be dragged to change the column width.

Clicking a row only selects it. To edit a cell, start with any of double-clicking the cell, Enter, F2, or Edit selection... in the right-click menu, and confirm with Enter or cancel with Esc. For colors, click the color swatch to open the color picker. Because the displayed rows have no text input field, Cmd+C / Cmd+V / Cmd+Z act on rows, not on text.

A Paint Cut can be undone in one step with a single Undo. Paste is unavailable when the clipboard is empty. Pasted rows keep the order in which they were copied.

docs.title: Camera panel
docs.text:
A list of cameras (saved named viewpoints). Click a row to select it, and use the toolbar or the right-click menu to operate on it. When there are no cameras, (no cameras) is shown.

Screenshot planned

The toolbar at the top of the panel has six buttons.

Button Action New camera from view Creates a new camera from the current view. A dialog asks for the name Save from view Overwrites the selected camera with the current view Save from view with show/hide Same as above. The show / hide state is also saved Apply to view Restores the view of the selected camera Apply to view with show/hide Same as above. The saved show / hide state is also restored Delete Deletes the selected camera
  • Double-click: Applies the camera, including its show / hide state.
  • Renaming: Press F2 or choose Rename... from the right-click menu to edit in place.
  • Deleting: The Del / Backspace keys also delete it.
  • Reordering: Drag rows to change the order. Dropping a row below the last row of the list moves it to the end. The order is saved in the scene file (.qsc).
  • __current: A special camera that records the view at the time the scene was saved. It is pinned to the top of the list and cannot be moved by dragging.
  • Row badges: A camera that holds a show / hide state has an eye icon, and a camera loaded from a camera file has a link icon.

In addition to the above, the right-click menu offers copy & paste, loading, reloading and saving camera files (.cam), and editing and clearing display flags (→ Camera). Right-clicking on an empty area opens a menu with only New, Paste and loading a camera file.

Creating a camera with an existing name overwrites it

Running New camera from view with the same name as an existing camera overwrites that camera without confirmation.

docs.title: View panel
docs.text:
Controls the viewpoint numerically. It corresponds to the fake dial (View panel) of CueMol2.

Section Contents Rotation Rotation about X / Y / Z. Dragging rotates relatively Translation Translation Zoom / Slab Zoom, slab (width of the visible depth), distance Projection Projection mode (Perspective / Orthographic) and the center mark

Note

Changes of the view are not subject to Undo. The background color is a scene setting, so set it from the Scene menu or the inspector, not from this panel.

docs.title: Molecular structure panel
docs.text:
Shows a molecule as a chain → residue → atom hierarchical tree and builds selections.

  • Choose the target molecule at the top.
  • The tree is loaded when a node is expanded.
  • Multiple selection is supported (Cmd / Ctrl + click, Shift + click).
  • With Select / Center / Zoom on the toolbar, the chosen range can be made the current selection / brought to the center / zoomed in on.

docs.title: Selection panel
docs.text:
A dedicated panel for displaying and editing the selection of a molecule.

  • When you choose the target molecule in Molecule, the current selection of that molecule is shown in the Selection field as a selection expression. Operations in the panel are applied to the selection immediately and can be undone with Undo.
  • The selection builder (four tabs: Named / History / Term / Mod) lets you build a selection without writing an expression. You can apply a named selection or a history entry with one click, combine conditions (Set / Add / Sub / Intsec), and transform the current selection (Invert / Byres / Sidech / Mainch / Arnd / Expn). Each operation shows the number of atoms that would result if it were applied (→ Selection builder).
  • The Selection field can also be edited by hand. The expression is validated as you type, and a warning is shown if it is invalid. Apply a hand-typed expression with the Select button.
  • The history is saved in the application and shared with the selection fields of Renderers and elsewhere.

Differences from CueMol2

The hierarchical editor (Hierarchical / Terminal / Around-Expand) of the CueMol2 selection panel has been replaced by the selection builder.

docs.title: Symmetry panel
docs.text:
Handles crystallographic symmetry.

  • When you choose the target Object (molecular coordinates / density map), the lattice type, space group and cell constants are shown.
  • Change... changes the crystal system and the space group. When "restriction by symmetry" is enabled, the input of cell constants is linked according to the constraints of the crystal system.
  • Symm mol displays symmetry mates. The range can be chosen from 20 / 50 / 100 / 200 Å or the unit cell.
  • Unit cell displays the frame of the unit cell.

docs.title: Density map panel
docs.text:
Adjusts the display of density map Renderers (contour / isosurface, etc.).

  • Choose a Renderer and adjust the transparency / contour level / display extent with the sliders.
  • The level can be specified either in a unit that depends on the map type (σ for crystallographic maps, the top % of grid point values for cryo-EM maps) or as an absolute value (switch with the ▼ menu). The value in the other unit is shown below Level. A cryo-EM map is in absolute values from the moment it is loaded.
  • Redraw updates the center of the display to the current view center. Cell displays the unit cell.
  • When the whole map is displayed (the Region of the Renderer is Full map), the Extent slider and Redraw have no effect (→ contour).

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Handles the recording of performed operations and their replay. For details, see Recording and replaying operations (Actions).

docs.title: History panel
docs.text: Shows the Undo history of the active scene, one step per row. A step that contains two or more operations can be expanded to list the operations performed. From the toolbar you can move to the state of the selected row (Go to step), copy it as commands (Copy as commands), save it to a qax file (Save as qax), or save it to the Actions panel (Save to Actions). Double-clicking a step shows its contents read-only in the inspector.

docs.title: Actions panel
docs.text:
Lists the Presets bundled with the app and the User Actions you saved. Select one and press Run to apply it to the Object selected in the scene tree.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546

docs.title: Toolbar and tool palette
docs.text:
CueMol3 has two rows of buttons with different roles.

Toolbar Tool palette Position Top of the window Floats at the left edge of the molecular view Role Commands that are executed immediately when pressed Switch the operation mode of the molecular view

Screenshots planned

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
Button Action Corresponding menu item New Tab Creates a new tab. File > New Tab Open File Opens a file. File > Open File... Save As Saves an Object to a file. File > Save File As... Open Scene Opens a scene file. File > Open Scene... Reload Scene Reloads the scene. File > Reload Scene Save Scene Saves the scene. File > Save Scene Get PDB Fetches a structure by PDB ID. File > Get PDB... Render Opens the rendering window. Rendering > Image / Movie rendering... Undo Undoes the last operation. Edit > Undo Redo Redoes an undone operation. Edit > Redo
  • When the window is too narrow, the labels are omitted and only the icons are shown (the name appears in the tooltip).
  • When no scene is open, buttons that require a scene are disabled.
  • The Render button opens the rendering window but does not change the output mode (still image / movie).

docs.title: Undo / Redo history dropdown
docs.text: The Undo / Redo buttons have a history dropdown. Selecting an entry in the list undoes / redoes all operations up to that point at once. The text of each entry is generated from the recorded operations and shows, for example, which Renderer was created or which property was changed (→ Recording and replaying operations).

docs.title: Tool palette
docs.text:
A vertical row of buttons at the left edge of the molecular view. It switches the meaning of clicks and drags in the molecular view. The cursor shape also changes according to the selected tool.

Group Tool Shortcut Action Navigate Navigate N View manipulation (default mode) Select Rect Select B Selects atoms in a rectangular region. Lasso L Selects atoms with a lasso. Measure Distance D Click 2 atoms to measure a distance. Angle A Click 3 atoms to measure an angle. Torsion T Click 4 atoms to measure a dihedral angle. Edit Add Bond E Click 2 atoms in the same molecule to add a bond.
  • Pressing Esc resets the clicks accumulated so far.
  • Switching tools or views also resets them.

At the top of the palette there is a collapse handle. Pressing it shrinks the palette to just the handle; pressing it again restores the palette. View > Tool palette (Cmd+Shift+P) toggles it in the same way, and the state is kept for the next launch (→ View menu).

docs.title: Selection tools
docs.text:
Rect Select selects the atoms inside a rectangle, and Lasso selects the atoms inside a free-form polygon.

Operation Action Drag Replaces the selection with the enclosed region. Shift + drag Adds the enclosed region to the current selection (the cursor shape changes).

While the Rect Select tool is selected, view manipulation (Navigate) is still available.

docs.title: Measurement tools
docs.text:
With Distance / Angle / Torsion, clicking the required number of atoms adds the measured value as a label in the molecular view. Intermediate clicks are indicated by cross marks.

The measurement tool group has an option handle; opening it lets you choose the label set to which labels are added.

Measurements can span multiple molecules.

docs.title: Add Bond tool
docs.text:
Clicking 2 atoms in the same molecule in turn adds a bond. The addition can be undone with Undo.

Opening the option handle of the group shows a list of the non-standard bonds of that molecule, and each row can be deleted. Even when several bonds are deleted together, a single Undo restores them.

Replaces the CueMol2 Mol bond editor

In CueMol2, a modal dialog was opened from the Tools menu, and atom IDs were entered into the input fields while moving the dialog out of the way. In CueMol3, bonds are added by clicking directly in the molecular view, and the menu item has been removed.

Verified against: CueMol3 2.4.0.546
